title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
道在天地間載而行之者人
也行於己則聖行於世則治
自周之季上不知以是教下
不知以是學至宋是學始講
於下而上之教未聞也我
太祖高皇帝以是道受天明命建
===
儒學於天下而非儒若律筭
等學皆罷
太宗文皇帝以是道纘國大統頒
五經四書於天下而非聖若
百家諸書皆黜俾天下之名
為儒者非經書不讀非孔孟
程朱之業不講
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序

道在天地間，載而行之者人也。行於己則聖，行於世則治。自周之季，上不知以是教，下不知以是學。至宋，是學始講於下，而上之教未聞也。我太祖高皇帝以是道受天明命，建儒學於天下，而非儒若律筭等學皆罷。太宗文皇帝以是道纘國大統，頒五經四書於天下，而非聖若百家諸書皆黜。俾天下之名為儒者，非經書不讀，非孔孟程朱之業不講。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

The Way exists between Heaven and Earth; it is human beings who bear it and put it into practice. Practiced in oneself, it brings sagehood; practiced throughout the world, it brings good government. From the closing years of the Zhou, those above did not know to teach by it, and those below did not know to learn by it. Only in the Song did this learning begin to be expounded among those below, yet teaching by it from above remained unheard of. Our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s illustrious mandate through this Way and established Confucian schools throughout the realm, abolishing all non-Confucian schools, such as those devoted to law and mathematics. Emperor Taizong Wen succeeded to the great imperial line through this Way and promulgated the Five Classics and Four Books throughout the realm, rejecting writings not of the sages, such as the various books of the Hundred Schools. He thereby ensured that all throughout the realm who called themselves Confucian scholars read only the canonical books and expounded only the learning of Kongzi, Mengzi, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相繼逮我
皇上其揆惟一百三十餘年來上
無異教下無異學治化之盛
直追唐虞三代與之並而漢
唐以下弗數焉有由然哉然
取士之法不全用周人考德
行道藝之典而以文不論其
===
賢能之實於鄉大夫州長黨
正族師閭胥而以科舉者勢
不行也唐宋科舉所謂文者
詩賦今則非析經書之義明
兼策論表判之成章不取漢
法近古其徵吏民曰明當世
之務習先聖之術非是之謂
punctuated: 列聖相繼，逮我皇上，其揆惟一。百三十餘年來，上無異教，下無異學，治化之盛，直追唐虞三代，與之並，而漢唐以下弗數焉，有由然哉！然取士之法，不全用周人考德行道藝之典，而以文；不論其賢能之實於鄉大夫、州長、黨正、族師、閭胥，而以科舉者，勢不行也。唐宋科舉所謂文者，詩賦；今則非析經書之義明，兼策論表判之成章，不取。漢法近古，其徵吏民曰：「明當世之務，習先聖之術。」非是之謂
translation_en:
Successive sage emperors, down to our present sovereign, have followed one and the same guiding principle. For more than a hundred and thirty years, those above have upheld no divergent teaching, and those below have pursued no divergent learning. The flourishing of government and moral transformation directly rivals the ages of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties, standing equal to them; the Han, Tang, and subsequent dynasties scarcely merit mention by comparison. Surely there is a reason for this!

Yet the method of selecting officials does not wholly employ the Zhou institutions for examining moral character, conduct, learning, and skills, but relies on written composition. Rather than assessing candidates’ actual worth and abilities through township grandees, district chiefs, neighborhood heads, clan preceptors, and hamlet headmen, it employs the examination system, because circumstances make the former approach impracticable. What the Tang and Song examinations called written composition consisted of poetry and rhapsodies. Today, however, candidates are not selected unless they clearly explicate the meaning of the canonical books and also produce accomplished compositions in policy essays, discourses, memorials, and legal judgments. Han methods were close to those of antiquity. In summoning officials and commoners for service, their stated requirements were: “Understand the affairs of the present age and be versed in the learning of the former sages.” Does this not describe precisely…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
與然漢一行而止我
國家成憲萬世是遵又非漢比
也是雖不全用周人之典而
本之德行道藝一也弘治甲
子秋為取士之期巡按監察
御史李〔春〕當監臨下教凡試
事稽于故而加重禮文一新
===
焉乃以參政李〔贊〕參議倪〔天民〕
提調按察副使王〔雲鳳〕張〔璥〕監
試〔琛〕與學正張〔萓〕考試學正
張〔煥〕教諭吳〔夔〕王〔宣〕訓導刁
〔毅〕陳〔頊〕何〔宗源〕同考試暨諸執
事皆合僉議擇以充萃提學
副使李〔遜學〕所選士而試之三
punctuated:
與？然漢一行而止，我國家成憲，萬世是遵，又非漢比也。是雖不全用周人之典，而本之德行道藝，一也。弘治甲子秋，為取士之期，巡按監察御史李〔春〕當監臨，下教凡試事稽于故，而加重禮文，一新焉。
乃以參政李〔贊〕、參議倪〔天民〕提調，按察副使王〔雲鳳〕、張〔璥〕監試，〔琛〕與學正張〔萓〕考試，學正張〔煥〕、教諭吳〔夔〕、王〔宣〕、訓導刁〔毅〕、陳〔頊〕、何〔宗源〕同考試。暨諸執事，皆合僉議，擇以充。萃提學副使李〔遜學〕所選士，而試之三
translation_en:
…is this not what was meant? Yet the Han implemented this only once and then stopped. The established statutes of our dynasty are to be followed for ten thousand generations, so here again it cannot be compared with the Han. Although it does not employ the institutions of the Zhou in their entirety, its foundation in virtue, conduct, the Way, and the arts is the same. The autumn of the jiazi year of Hongzhi [1504] was the appointed time for selecting scholars. Li Chun, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, acted as Supervising Official. He issued instructions that all examination procedures should follow precedent, while giving greater weight to ritual observances, thereby renewing them throughout.
Accordingly, Li Zan, Administration Vice Commissioner, and Ni Tianmin, Administration Assistant Commissioner, served as Proctors. Wang Yunfeng and Zhang Jing, Surveillance Vice Commissioners, oversaw the examination. I, Chen, together with Zhang Yi [?], a School Instructor, served as Examiners. Zhang Huan, a School Instructor; Wu Kui and Wang Xuan, Instructors; and Diao Yi, Chen Xu, and He Zongyuan, Assistant Instructors, served as Associate Examiners. These men, together with all the other functionaries, were selected to fill their posts through collective deliberation. The scholars selected by Li Xunxue, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, were assembled and examined in three sessions…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
士凡一千四百有竒取六十
五焉限于額也先是總制軍
務太子少保戶部尚書秦〔紘〕
鎮守太監劉〔雲〕武安侯鄭〔英〕
督理馬政都御史楊〔一清〕巡撫
陜西都御史孫〔需〕巡撫各邊
都御史文〔貴〕畢〔亨〕劉〔憲〕盤粮
===
給事中王〔宸〕巡按監察御史
杜〔旻〕李〔高〕見關中之士之盛
也皆將有得人之慶〔琛〕濫竽
較文之列因其言以知其藴
雖不無遺材之嘆然是六十
五人者固有可慶者矣事既
竣當有録以第其名氏表其
punctuated: 士凡一千四百有竒，取六十五焉，限于額也。先是，總制軍務太子少保戶部尚書秦〔紘〕、鎮守太監劉〔雲〕、武安侯鄭〔英〕、督理馬政都御史楊〔一清〕、巡撫陜西都御史孫〔需〕、巡撫各邊都御史文〔貴〕、畢〔亨〕、劉〔憲〕、盤粮給事中王〔宸〕、巡按監察御史杜〔旻〕、李〔高〕，見關中之士之盛也，皆將有得人之慶。〔琛〕濫竽較文之列，因其言以知其藴，雖不無遺材之嘆，然是六十五人者，固有可慶者矣。事既竣，當有録，以第其名氏，表其
translation_en: …The candidates numbered more than fourteen hundred; sixty-five were selected, the number being restricted by the quota. Before this, Qin Hong, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Revenue; Liu Yun, Regional Commander and Grand Eunuch; Zheng Ying, Marquis of Wu’an; Yang Yiqing, Censor-in-chief supervising horse administration; Sun Xu, Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi; Wen Gui, Bi Heng, and Liu Xian, Censors-in-chief and Grand Coordinators of the various frontier regions; Wang Chen, Supervising Secretary inspecting grain supplies; and Du Min and Li Gao, Regional Inspecting Censors, had observed the abundance of scholars in Guanzhong and all anticipated the joy of obtaining worthy men. I, Chen, unworthily included among those judging the compositions, came to understand the candidates’ inner resources through their words. Though there was some cause to lament that worthy talent had been overlooked, these sixty-five men certainly gave grounds for celebration. Once the proceedings were completed, a record was required to list their names in order of rank and display their …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
文錄既成琛當序諸首琛當
何言哉嗟乎士生斯世得以
孔孟程朱所以繼往聖開來
學之書而讀之雖才有强弱
志有遠近學有淺深皆與聞
乎大道之要視漢唐之世雖
有通經學古明睿卓越之士
而惟知訓詁之精為高辭章
===
之工為奇茫不識道為何物
者豈不大相遠哉然則今之
士一何幸也譬之飲食朝夕
于是而味焉罔察以至終身
由之而不知則有負
盛世之教者矣爾諸生其以平
punctuated: 文。錄既成，琛當序諸首，琛當何言哉？嗟乎！士生斯世，得以孔孟程朱所以繼往聖、開來學之書而讀之，雖才有强弱，志有遠近，學有淺深，皆與聞乎大道之要。視漢唐之世，雖有通經學古、明睿卓越之士，而惟知訓詁之精為高、辭章之工為奇，茫不識道為何物者，豈不大相遠哉？然則今之士一何幸也！譬之飲食，朝夕于是而味焉罔察，以至終身由之而不知，則有負盛世之教者矣！爾諸生，其以平
translation_en: …their compositions. Now that the record is complete, I, Chen, am to place a preface at its beginning. What should I say? Alas! Scholars born into this age can read the books through which Kongzi, Mengzi, Cheng, and Zhu carried forward the legacy of the past sages and opened the way for future learners. Though their abilities vary in strength, their aspirations in reach, and their learning in depth, all have the opportunity to learn the essentials of the Great Way. Compared with the Han and Tang ages, when even penetrating and outstanding scholars versed in the classics and ancient learning knew only to esteem precision in textual glosses and marvel at skill in literary composition, yet remained utterly ignorant of what the Way was, is the difference not immense? How fortunate, then, are the scholars of today! Yet if, as with eating and drinking, they partake of it morning and evening without discerning its flavor, and spend their whole lives following it without understanding it, they will have failed the teachings of this flourishing age! You students should take your ordinary…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
日之所業而反之身之進而有
職有位則以所業者施之政
反之身致謹於隱微而不以
名利動其心施之政以脩於
家而壤於天子之廷者為戒
夫如是則雖遇有亨蹇秩有
崇卑功有大小而自處或有
===
戾於道焉者寡矣此固今日
之所為慶者也諸士其以予
言為然乎相是役者叅政史
簡〔思明〕李胡〔瑞〕叅議張〔勛〕錢〔敬〕
邵〔棠〕按察副使馬〔懋〕李〔端澄〕王
寅〔忠〕燕高〔崇熙〕蕭〔翀〕僉事任〔鑑〕
李〔蕖〕胡〔經〕官〔賢〕唐〔希介〕丁〔瑚〕賈
punctuated:
日之所業而反之身之，進而有職有位，則以所業者施之政。反之身，致謹於隱微，而不以名利動其心；施之政，以脩於家而壤於天子之廷者為戒。夫如是，則雖遇有亨蹇，秩有崇卑，功有大小，而自處或有戾於道焉者寡矣。此固今日之所為慶者也。諸士其以予言為然乎？
相是役者，叅政史簡〔思明〕、李胡〔瑞〕，叅議張〔勛〕、錢〔敬〕、邵〔棠〕，按察副使馬〔懋〕、李〔端澄〕、王寅〔忠〕、燕高〔崇熙〕、蕭〔翀〕，僉事任〔鑑〕、李〔蕖〕、胡〔經〕、官〔賢〕、唐〔希介〕、丁〔瑚〕、賈
translation_en:
…apply what you study daily to your own conduct [?]; when you advance to hold office and rank, apply what you have studied to government. In applying it to yourselves, exercise the utmost care in what is hidden and subtle, and do not let fame or profit stir your hearts. In applying it to government, take warning from those who cultivate themselves at home but fail at the Son of Heaven’s court [?]. If you do this, then, although your circumstances may be favorable or adverse, your ranks high or low, and your achievements great or small, you will seldom conduct yourselves in ways contrary to the Way. This, indeed, is what we celebrate today. Do you gentlemen consider my words sound?
Those assisting with this examination included the following. Shi Jian (with the annotation “Siming”) [?] and Li Hu (with the annotation “Rui”) [?] served as Administration Vice Commissioners. Zhang Xun, Qian Jing, and Shao Tang served as Assistant Administration Commissioners. Ma Mao, Li Duancheng, Wang Yin (with the annotation “Zhong”) [?], Yan Gao (with the annotation “Chongxi”) [?], and Xiao Chong served as Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Ren Jian, Li Qu, Hu Jing, Guan Xian, Tang Xijie, Ding Hu, and Jia… served as Assistant Surveillance Commissioners.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時劉〔道立〕曹玉也
江西瑞州府儒學教授方琛
謹序
punctuated:
時、劉〔道立〕、曹玉也。

江西瑞州府儒學教授方琛謹序。
translation_en:
…Jia Shi, Liu Daoli, and Cao Yu.

Preface respectfully composed by Fang Chen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
弘治十七年陜西鄉試
監臨官
巡按陜西監察御史李春〔體仁山西振武衛人　丙辰進士〕
提調官
陜西等處承宣布政使司左叅政李贊〔惟誠直隸蕪湖縣人　甲辰進士〕
陜西等處承宣布政使司右叅議倪天民〔秀夫武功中衛軍籍　丁未進士〕
監試官
陜西等處提刑按察司副使王雲鳳〔應韶山西和順縣人　甲辰進士〕
陜西等處提刑按察司副使張繖〔廷儀山西陽城縣人　甲辰進士〕
===
考試官
江西瑞州府儒學教授方琛〔廷獻湖廣咸寧縣人　壬子貢士〕
順天府涿州儒學學正張喆〔子卿山西安邑縣人　乙卯貢士〕
同考試官
順天府薊州儒學學正張煥〔文煥江西浮梁縣人　戊午貢士〕
直隸蘇州府吳縣儒學教諭吳夔〔學夔浙江西安縣人　壬子貢士〕
山西平陽府解州安邑縣儒學教諭王宣〔德敷河南內鄉縣人　乙卯貢士〕
山東東昌府高唐州儒學訓導刁毅〔景仁直隸束鹿縣人　丙午貢士〕
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓導陳頊〔子敬廣東東莞縣人　己酉貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治十七年陜西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按陜西監察御史李春〔體仁，山西振武衛人，　丙辰進士〕。

提調官：
陜西等處承宣布政使司左叅政李贊〔惟誠，直隸蕪湖縣人，　甲辰進士〕。
陜西等處承宣布政使司右叅議倪天民〔秀夫，武功中衛軍籍，　丁未進士〕。

監試官：
陜西等處提刑按察司副使王雲鳳〔應韶，山西和順縣人，　甲辰進士〕。
陜西等處提刑按察司副使張繖〔廷儀，山西陽城縣人，　甲辰進士〕。

考試官：
江西瑞州府儒學教授方琛〔廷獻，湖廣咸寧縣人，　壬子貢士〕。
順天府涿州儒學學正張喆〔子卿，山西安邑縣人，　乙卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
順天府薊州儒學學正張煥〔文煥，江西浮梁縣人，　戊午貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府吳縣儒學教諭吳夔〔學夔，浙江西安縣人，　壬子貢士〕。
山西平陽府解州安邑縣儒學教諭王宣〔德敷，河南內鄉縣人，　乙卯貢士〕。
山東東昌府高唐州儒學訓導刁毅〔景仁，直隸束鹿縣人，　丙午貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓導陳頊〔子敬，廣東東莞縣人，　己酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shaanxi Provincial Examination, the seventeenth year of Hongzhi (1504).

Supervising Official:
Li Chun, Investigating Censor assigned to巡inspect Shaanxi, courtesy name Tiren, was a native of Zhenwu Guard in Shanxi and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year.

Proctors:
Li Zan, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left in the Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Weicheng, was a native of Wuhu County in Zhili and a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Ni Tianmin, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right in the Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Xiufu, was registered in a military household of Wugong Central Guard and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Examination Inspectors:
Wang Yunfeng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Yingshao, was a native of Heshun County in Shanxi and a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Zhang San, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Tingyi, was a native of Yangcheng County in Shanxi and a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Examiners:
Fang Chen, Professor in the Confucian School of Ruizhou Prefecture in Jiangxi, courtesy name Tingxian, was a native of Xianning County in Huguang and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Zhang Zhe, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhuozhou Subprefecture in Shuntian Prefecture, courtesy name Ziqing, was a native of Anyi County in Shanxi and a tribute scholar of the yimao year.

Associate Examiners:
Zhang Huan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jizhou Subprefecture in Shuntian Prefecture, courtesy name Wenhuan, was a native of Fuliang County in Jiangxi and a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Wu Kui, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Xuekui, was a native of Xi'an County in Zhejiang and a tribute scholar of the renzi year.
Wang Xuan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Anyi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Neixiang County in Henan and a tribute scholar of the yimao year.
Diao Yi, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Jingren, was a native of Shulu County in Zhili and a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.
Chen Xu, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Zijing, was a native of Dongguan County in Guangdong and a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫如是故遠人不服則脩文德以來之
故君子語大天下莫能載焉
且一人之身而百工之所為備如必自為
而後用之是率天下而路也
易
九二包蒙吉納婦吉子克家
順而麗乎大明柔進而上行
===
變化者進退之象也
若夫雜物撰德辨是與非則非其中爻不
備
書
無敎逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日萬幾
無曠庶官天工人其代之
念終始典于學
百姓王人罔不秉德明恤小臣屏侯甸矧
咸奔走
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
夫如是，故遠人不服，則脩文德以來之。
故君子語大，天下莫能載焉。
且一人之身，而百工之所為備。如必自為而後用之，是率天下而路也。

易
九二：包蒙，吉；納婦，吉；子克家。
順而麗乎大明，柔進而上行。
變化者，進退之象也。
若夫雜物撰德，辨是與非，則非其中爻不備。

書
無敎逸欲有邦，兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。無曠庶官，天工人其代之。
念終始典于學。
百姓王人，罔不秉德明恤；小臣屏侯甸，矧咸奔走。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“This being so, if distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to attract them.”
“Thus, when the gentleman speaks of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can contain it.”
“Moreover, a single person requires the products of all the various crafts. If everyone must make things personally before using them, this would lead everyone under Heaven to exhaustion on the roads.”

Book of Changes
“Nine in the second place: embracing the untutored brings good fortune; taking a wife brings good fortune; the son can manage the household.”
“Yielding and adhering to great brightness, the yielding advances and moves upward.”
“Changes and transformations are images of advancing and withdrawing.”
“As for intermingling things, defining their qualities, and distinguishing right from wrong, these cannot be fully represented without the middle lines.”

Book of Documents
“Do not teach those who possess states to indulge in ease and desire. Be vigilant and diligent: in a single day or two, there are ten thousand incipient affairs to attend to. Let none of the many offices lie neglected: Heaven’s work is to be performed by human beings in its stead.”
“Remember, from beginning to end, to take learning as your guide.”
“Among the great families and the king’s servants, none failed to uphold virtue and show discerning care. Even lesser servants served as bulwarks for the lords of the hou and dian domains [?]; how much more did they all hasten to render service.”

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
獄成而孚輸而孚
詩
二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌陰
既立之監或佐之史
文武受命召公維翰無曰予小子召公是
似肇敏戎公用錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬
鬯一卣告于文人錫山土田于周受
命自召祖命
奄有四方斤斤其明
===
春秋
及宋人盟于宿〔隱公元年〕
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男滑伯滕
子同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕
宋公曹伯衛人邾人伐齊　師救齊　宋
師及齊師戰于甗齊師敗績　狄救
齊〔僖公十八年〕
公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯
莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子于
punctuated:
獄成而孚，輸而孚。

詩
二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。
既立之監，或佐之史。
文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告于文人。錫山土田，于周受命，自召祖命。
奄有四方，斤斤其明。

春秋
及宋人盟于宿〔隱公元年〕。
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子，同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕。
宋公、曹伯、衛人、邾人伐齊。師救齊。宋師及齊師戰于甗，齊師敗績。狄救齊〔僖公十八年〕。
公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于
translation_en:
When a legal case is concluded, its judgment must be credible; when the judgment is reported, it must likewise be credible.

Book of Odes
In the second month they cut the ice with resounding blows; in the third month they store it in the icehouse.
Having established overseers for them, he also appointed scribes to assist them.
Kings Wen and Wu received the mandate; the Duke of Shao was their mainstay. Do not say, “I am but a young man”; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently to perform your great service, and blessings will be bestowed upon you. You are granted a jade-handled libation ladle and a jar of black-millet sacrificial wine, to announce the grant to your cultivated ancestors. Mountains, lands, and fields are bestowed upon you. Receive your charge at the Zhou court, continuing the charge of your ancestor, the Duke of Shao.
He possessed all four quarters; keen was his discernment.

Spring and Autumn Annals
A covenant was made with men of Song at Su. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕
A meeting was held with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng; together they made a covenant at You. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
The Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, and men of Wei and Zhu attacked Qi. Our army came to the aid of Qi. The army of Song fought the army of Qi at Yan, and the army of Qi was routed. The Di came to the aid of Qi. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xi.〕
The duke met with the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
禮記
羣居五人則長者必異席
司寇正刑明辟以聽獄訟
故聽其雅頌之聲志意得廣焉執其干戚
習其俯仰詘伸容貌得莊焉行其綴
兆要其節奏行列得正焉進退得齊
焉
間歌三終合樂三終
===
第貳場
論
主敬便是為善
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢罷苑馬賜貧民詔〔建元元年〕
擬唐以魏徵為侍中誥〔貞觀七年〕
擬宋諫臣謝詔儆悉心獻替表〔景德三年〕
判語〔五條〕
濫設官吏
punctuated:
禮記
羣居五人，則長者必異席。
司寇正刑明辟，以聽獄訟。
故聽其雅頌之聲，志意得廣焉；執其干戚，習其俯仰詘伸，容貌得莊焉；行其綴兆，要其節奏，行列得正焉，進退得齊焉。
間歌三終，合樂三終。

第貳場
論
主敬便是為善。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢罷苑馬賜貧民詔〔建元元年〕。
擬唐以魏徵為侍中誥〔貞觀七年〕。
擬宋諫臣謝詔儆悉心獻替表〔景德三年〕。

判語〔五條〕
濫設官吏。
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)
When five people sit together, the eldest must occupy a separate mat.
The Minister of Justice sets punishments in order and clarifies penal laws, thereby adjudicating criminal cases and civil suits.
Thus, by listening to the sounds of the Elegantiae and Hymns, their aspirations and thoughts are broadened; by holding shields and battle-axes and practicing bowing, rising, bending, and extending, their bearing becomes dignified; by moving through the designated dance positions and keeping to the rhythm, their ranks become orderly and their advances and retreats become coordinated.
There are three performances of alternating song and instrumental music, followed by three performances of combined music.

Second Session
Discourse
Maintaining reverent attentiveness is itself doing good.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor abolishing the imperial park’s horse establishment and granting its resources to poor commoners. 〔First year of Jianyuan.〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor appointing Wei Zheng as Palace Attendant. 〔Seventh year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of a Song remonstrance official expressing gratitude for an imperial edict of admonition and pledging wholeheartedly to recommend what is good and oppose what is wrong. 〔Third year of Jingde.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Indiscriminately establishing posts for officials and clerks.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
私借官物
冒支官粮
擅調官軍
詐假官
第叄場
策五道
問先王之世以道治天下後世只是以法
把持天下程子有是言也我
太祖高皇帝嘗御奉天門諭羣臣曰治天下之
===
道禮樂二者而已若通於禮而不通於樂非
所以淑人心而出治道達於樂而不達於禮
非所以振紀綱而立大中必禮樂並行然後
治化醇一大哉
皇言以禮樂為治天下之道蓋即程子之意古
帝王之所未發也於戲非
天下之至聖其孰能與於此哉若唐太宗以禮
樂為聖人緣物設教而非由於治之隆
替者安足與論治也是禮樂也有欲與
punctuated:
私借官物。
冒支官粮。
擅調官軍。
詐假官。

第叄場
策五道

問：先王之世，以道治天下；後世只是以法把持天下。程子有是言也。我太祖高皇帝嘗御奉天門，諭羣臣曰：「治天下之道，禮樂二者而已。若通於禮而不通於樂，非所以淑人心而出治道；達於樂而不達於禮，非所以振紀綱而立大中。必禮樂並行，然後治化醇一。」大哉，皇言！以禮樂為治天下之道，蓋即程子之意，古帝王之所未發也。於戲！非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此哉？若唐太宗以禮樂為聖人緣物設教，而非由於治之隆替者，安足與論治也？是禮樂也，有欲與
translation_en:
Privately lending government property.
Fraudulently drawing government grain.
Unauthorized deployment of government troops.
Fraudulently assuming official status.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: In the age of the former kings, the realm was governed through the Way; in later ages, it was merely held in check through laws. Master Cheng made this statement. Our Emperor Taizu Gao once presided at Fengtian Gate and instructed his assembled ministers, saying: “The way to govern the realm consists solely of rites and music. To understand rites but not music is no means of improving people’s hearts and bringing forth good government; to comprehend music but not rites is no means of invigorating the governing order and establishing the great mean. Only when rites and music operate together can government and moral transformation become pure and unified.”

How great are these imperial words! Taking rites and music as the way to govern the realm accords with Master Cheng’s meaning and articulates what the emperors and kings of antiquity had not expressed. Ah! Who but the supreme sage of the realm could attain such understanding? As for Tang Taizong, who held that rites and music were teachings devised by sages in response to circumstances and did not depend upon the flourishing or decline of government, how could he be worthy of discussing government?

As for these rites and music, there were those who wished to take part in their establishment [?]…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
於漢而其君謙讓未遑有欲行於唐而
其臣愧無素業宋則君或有意而未及
嘗表臣或有見而未獲施行然當時或
作於叔孫通司馬相如或作於房玄齡
祖孝孫或作於劉溫叟和峴實亦未嘗
無禮樂而不得為道之治何歟又有以
立太學為禮以大射養老為禮以興辟
雍設庠序為禮以封泰山祀汾陰為禮
者有以鏗鏘鼓舞為樂以隆雅頌之聲
為樂以鑄鎛鐘編鐘為樂以度帝指定
黃鐘為樂者是果有得於禮樂否也且
禮樂亦有全體本末之可言乎我
===
聖祖制禮作樂達於天下
列聖相承逮我
皇上授受此道禮樂之化洋洋乎充塞兩間矣
近者從大臣之請又有議於樂焉
盛世大制作草野之下何足以知之然樂之
故亦有聞乎諸生蓋皆有志於禮樂者
punctuated: 於漢，而其君謙讓未遑；有欲行於唐，而其臣愧無素業。宋則君或有意而未及嘗表，臣或有見而未獲施行。然當時或作於叔孫通、司馬相如，或作於房玄齡、祖孝孫，或作於劉溫叟、和峴，實亦未嘗無禮樂，而不得為道之治，何歟？又有以立太學為禮，以大射養老為禮，以興辟雍、設庠序為禮，以封泰山、祀汾陰為禮者；有以鏗鏘鼓舞為樂，以隆雅頌之聲為樂，以鑄鎛鐘、編鐘為樂，以度帝指、定黃鐘為樂者。是果有得於禮樂否也？且禮樂亦有全體本末之可言乎？我聖祖制禮作樂，達於天下。列聖相承，逮我皇上授受此道，禮樂之化洋洋乎充塞兩間矣。近者從大臣之請，又有議於樂焉。盛世大制作，草野之下何足以知之？然樂之故亦有聞乎？諸生蓋皆有志於禮樂者。
translation_en:
…in the Han, but its ruler modestly deferred, having had no opportunity to undertake it; there were those who wished to put them into practice in the Tang, but its ministers were ashamed of lacking prior accomplishment. In the Song, rulers sometimes had the intention but did not reach the point of expressing it [?], while ministers sometimes had insight but obtained no opportunity to put it into practice. Yet rites and music were established in those times by Shusun Tong and Sima Xiangru, by Fang Xuanling and Zu Xiaosun, or by Liu Wensou and He Xian. There was, indeed, no lack of rites and music. Why, then, did they fail to achieve government in accordance with the Way?

There were also those who took establishing the Imperial University to constitute ritual; those who took the great archery ceremony and the ceremonial care of the aged to constitute ritual; those who took founding the Biyong and establishing local schools to constitute ritual; and those who took performing the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai and offering sacrifice at Fenyin to constitute ritual. There were those who took the clangor of instruments, drumming, and dancing to constitute music; those who took exalting the sounds of the Odes and Hymns to constitute music; those who took casting large bells and sets of chime bells to constitute music; and those who took measuring the emperor’s finger to determine the Yellow Bell pitch to constitute music. Did these truly attain an understanding of rites and music? Moreover, can one speak of rites and music in terms of their complete substance, their roots, and their ramifications?

Our Sagely Progenitor established rites and composed music, extending them throughout the realm. Successive sage sovereigns carried on this tradition, down to our present Emperor, receiving and transmitting this Way. The transforming influence of rites and music now abundantly fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Recently, in response to a request from high ministers, there has again been deliberation concerning music. How could those in the obscurity of private life adequately understand the great institutions of a flourishing age? Yet have you heard something of the principles and precedents of music? You candidates are, presumably, all men with an earnest commitment to rites and music.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
果有志也言及之又何讓焉
問廉者君子守身之常法然非細行末節
也故古人以是為重焉今舉其甚著為
學士大夫之所傳誦者言之有為相而
不別治生以長尺寸者甚至妾不衣帛
待賓客蒸豆兩器食而自拔其葵有為
將而辭齊三萬戶者甚至車惟蒠苡槖
惟衣書夫人棠不加緣有為守而以清
白遺子孫者甚至不持一硯愧市白集
===
載米之郡有為令而清身苦體者甚至
笥餘一縑單車就路留犢以去有為士
而辭封卻金者甚至非其力不食饋於
師弗食并日而食是皆問學之力資稟
之高有不待文王而興者然非道義不
取一介行於伊尹畜馬乘不察雞豚稱
於獻子魏以食二卵棄將宋禁種蔬以
責則人安得不砥礪克治而肯甘為汙
濁之歸乎茲欲立心者令聞廣譽不願
punctuated:
果有志也，言及之，又何讓焉？

問：廉者，君子守身之常法，然非細行末節也，故古人以是為重焉。今舉其甚著、為學士大夫之所傳誦者言之：有為相而不別治生以長尺寸者，甚至妾不衣帛，待賓客蒸豆兩器，食而自拔其葵；有為將而辭齊三萬戶者，甚至車惟蒠苡，槖惟衣書，夫人棠不加緣；有為守而以清白遺子孫者，甚至不持一硯，愧市白集，載米之郡；有為令而清身苦體者，甚至笥餘一縑，單車就路，留犢以去；有為士而辭封卻金者，甚至非其力不食，饋於師弗食，并日而食。是皆問學之力、資稟之高，有不待文王而興者。然非道義不取一介，行於伊尹；畜馬乘不察雞豚，稱於獻子；魏以食二卵棄將，宋禁種蔬以責則。人安得不砥礪克治，而肯甘為汙濁之歸乎？茲欲立心者，令聞廣譽不願
translation_en:
…If you truly have such aspirations, why hold back from speaking of them?

Question: Integrity is the gentleman’s constant rule for maintaining his personal conduct; it is no minor observance or trivial detail. Thus the ancients attached great importance to it. Let us discuss some especially conspicuous examples, handed down and celebrated among scholars and officials. There were chief ministers who undertook no separate business to increase their wealth even by the slightest amount; some went so far as to leave their concubines unclothed in silk, entertain guests with two dishes of steamed beans, or uproot their own mallows after eating them. There were generals who declined grants of thirty thousand households in Qi; some carried only Job’s tears [?] in their carts and only clothing and books in their bags, while a wife’s garment [?] had no added edging. There were prefects who bequeathed an unsullied reputation to their descendants; some would not take away even a single inkstone, felt ashamed of purchasing Bai’s collected writings, or brought their own rice when going to their prefectures. There were district magistrates who kept themselves pure and subjected their bodies to hardship; some had only a single piece of silk left in their chests, set out in a lone carriage, or left a calf behind when departing. There were scholars who declined enfeoffment and rejected gold; some would eat nothing not earned by their own labor, refused food offered by their teacher, or ate only once in several days. These all exemplify the power of learning and the loftiness of natural endowment: among them were those who rose to virtue without waiting for a King Wen to inspire them.

Yet to accept not even the smallest thing unless it accords with the Way and righteousness was Yi Yin’s practice; the saying that one who keeps a team of horses should not concern himself with chickens and pigs was attributed to Xianzi. Wei dismissed a general for eating two eggs, and Song prohibited growing vegetables in order to enforce accountability [?]. How, then, could people fail to discipline themselves and master their faults, willingly resigning themselves to corruption? Now, for those who wish to set their hearts aright: a good name and widespread renown, without desiring…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
文繡宮室妻妾輕於身死如孟子之所
稱有位于朝以餽遺為恥受任于外以
包苴為羞如真西山之所論以金珠為
脯醢以契券為詩文免於朱晦庵之所
譏必有道焉二三子固所謂士者盍各
言爾志
問不讀天下之書則無以窮天下之理不
窮天下之理則不敢論天下之事然理
之在書者雖罄南山竹不能盡也姑錯
===
舉萬一以勤二三子其明以告我三皇
五帝當據何說七十弟子當考何書孟
子見時君隨事以荅而朱子必曰誠意
正心論語記聖言始於學習而周子著
書首太極圖公仲有進士而槍石之田
止絳灌選長者而賓君皆退讓何以有
助不見黃生而鄙吝復萌見紫芝而名
利都盡何以能感北軍不左袒周勃何
以處之龐涓不燭書孫臏何以敗之韓
punctuated:
文繡，宮室妻妾輕於身死，如孟子之所稱；有位于朝，以餽遺為恥，受任于外，以包苴為羞，如真西山之所論；以金珠為脯醢，以契券為詩文，免於朱晦庵之所譏，必有道焉。二三子固所謂士者，盍各言爾志？
問：不讀天下之書，則無以窮天下之理；不窮天下之理，則不敢論天下之事。然理之在書者，雖罄南山竹，不能盡也。姑錯舉萬一，以勤二三子，其明以告我。三皇五帝，當據何說？七十弟子，當考何書？孟子見時君，隨事以荅，而朱子必曰誠意正心；論語記聖言，始於學習，而周子著書，首太極圖。公仲有進士，而槍石之田止；絳灌選長者，而賓君皆退，讓何以有助？不見黃生，而鄙吝復萌；見紫芝，而名利都盡，何以能感？北軍不左袒，周勃何以處之？龐涓不燭書，孫臏何以敗之？韓
translation_en:
…embroidered finery, and regard palaces, wives, and concubines as of less consequence than death, as Mencius described; hold office at court and regard gifts as disgraceful, or accept a posting outside the capital and regard bribes as shameful, as Zhen Xishan argued; and avoid Zhu Hui’an’s ridicule of those who treat gold and pearls as dried meat and mincemeat, and deeds and contracts as poetry and prose. There must be a way to achieve this. You gentlemen are surely what are called scholars: why not each state your aspirations?
Question: Without reading the books of the world, one has no means of fully investigating the principles of the world; without fully investigating those principles, one dare not discuss the affairs of the world. Yet even if all the bamboo of the Southern Mountains were exhausted, it could not encompass all the principles contained in books. Let us select a few scattered examples to challenge you gentlemen. Explain them clearly to me. Which accounts should we rely upon concerning the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors? Which books should we consult concerning the seventy disciples? When Mencius met the rulers of his day, he answered according to the matter at hand, yet Master Zhu invariably spoke of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. The Analects records the sage’s words, beginning with learning and practice, yet Master Zhou began his writing with the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. Gongzhong recommended men for service, but the grant of land at Qiangshi stopped [?]; Jiang and Guan selected respected elders, but Bin and Jun both withdrew [?]: how did yielding help? When he did not see Master Huang, his meanness and stinginess sprang up again; when he saw Zizhi, all thoughts of fame and profit vanished: how could such influence be exerted? Had the Northern Army not bared their left shoulders, how would Zhou Bo have dealt with them? Had Pang Juan not illuminated the writing, how would Sun Bin have defeated him? Han…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
琦何言歐陽脩為己之文章范鎮何視
司馬光如己之事為敎熊羆貔貅貙虎
與驅虎豹犀象獸何以能戰借突厥起
兵與北貉燕人助以梟騎夷何以可邇
井田封建肉刑古可復於今乎郊社宗
廟樂律今有合於古乎薄昭當殺與不
當殺何所折衷濮王稱親與不稱親何
所取正佛之禪何學仙之丹何物圜丘
不按或不以為非完璧歸趙或不以為
===
是是皆主司所疑者
問人有恒言皆曰今之将不如古然将才
各有所長雖古良将亦各用其所長耳
非有甚異於人也救韓救趙皆避敵而
擣虛擊魏擊趙擊齊皆因水而出竒或
将六十萬滅楚置郡用四十萬破秦入
關或精銳八千敗符堅背嵬五百走兀
朮或御下以恕寛厚得人行無部伍人
人自便或天下威名将不敢視吏治軍
punctuated:
琦何言歐陽脩為己之文章？范鎮何視司馬光如己之事為？敎熊羆貔貅貙虎，與驅虎豹犀象，獸何以能戰？借突厥起兵，與北貉燕人助以梟騎，夷何以可邇？井田、封建、肉刑，古可復於今乎？郊社、宗廟、樂律，今有合於古乎？薄昭當殺與不當殺，何所折衷？濮王稱親與不稱親，何所取正？佛之禪何學？仙之丹何物？圜丘不按，或不以為非；完璧歸趙，或不以為是。是皆主司所疑者。
問：人有恒言，皆曰今之将不如古。然将才各有所長，雖古良将，亦各用其所長耳，非有甚異於人也。救韓救趙，皆避敵而擣虛；擊魏擊趙擊齊，皆因水而出竒。或将六十萬滅楚置郡，用四十萬破秦入關；或精銳八千敗符堅，背嵬五百走兀朮；或御下以恕，寛厚得人，行無部伍，人人自便；或天下威名，将不敢視，吏治軍
translation_en:
…Why did Han Qi speak of Ouyang Xiu’s writings as writings for his own moral cultivation? Why did Fan Zhen regard Sima Guang’s deeds as though they were his own? In training bears, brown bears, pi, xiu, chu, and tigers, and in driving tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants into battle, how could beasts be made to fight? In borrowing Tujue support to raise troops, and in receiving assistance from the northern Mo and the men of Yan with their valiant cavalry, how could foreign peoples be brought into close association? Can the ancient well-field system, enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments be restored today? Do today’s suburban and soil altars, ancestral temples, and musical pitch standards accord with antiquity? Between the views that Bo Zhao deserved execution and that he did not, how should one adjudicate? Between addressing the Prince of Pu as a parent and not doing so, where should one seek the correct ruling? What kind of learning is Buddhist meditation? What substance is the immortals’ elixir? Some do not consider the failure to investigate the Circular Mound [?] wrong; some do not consider returning the jade intact to Zhao right. These are all matters about which the presiding examiners have doubts.
Question: People have a habitual saying: all declare that today’s generals fall short of those of antiquity. Yet military talents each have their particular strengths. Even the good generals of antiquity merely employed their respective strengths; they possessed nothing extraordinarily different from other men. In rescuing Han and rescuing Zhao, they avoided the enemy and struck where defenses were weak; in attacking Wei, Zhao, and Qi, they used water to achieve surprise. One commanded six hundred thousand men to destroy Chu and establish commanderies; another used four hundred thousand to defeat Qin and enter the passes. One defeated Fu Jian with eight thousand elite troops; another routed Wuzhu with five hundred Beiwei troops. One treated his subordinates with forbearance and won men over through generosity: on the march there were no organized units or ranks, and each man acted as suited him. Another had an awe-inspiring reputation throughout the realm, so that generals dared not look upon him; officers administered the army…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
薄軍不得休又有將騎而馮敬不能當
將步而項它不能當用車而樹機能不
能當皆各用其所長也若斬王愛姬可
赴水火斬君寵臣三軍振慄似未易窺
其長卧不設席行不騎乘進食十數所
友百數似無以見其長諸葛亮為天下
奇才霍去病不學古兵法張巡行兵不
依古法似非可目其長然亦有可窺可
見可目者乎今之握邊兵而建將旗者
===
亦有如前所云者乎近者虜薄榆林擾
遼東掠大同入固原不但有諸將也而
又有主將焉不但有主將也而又有大
將焉卒未有能多為奇陳大敗匈奴十
餘萬如李牧以大斧斷其臂碎其首如
劉錡者其故何歟豈皆劣才無所長歟
抑雖有才而兵非常試亦不敢自見其
長但彼此相諉功不可幸而得則罪可
幸為免歟古人有言兵死地將死官故
punctuated: 薄，軍不得休。又有將騎而馮敬不能當，將步而項它不能當，用車而樹機能不能當，皆各用其所長也。若斬王愛姬，可赴水火；斬君寵臣，三軍振慄，似未易窺其長。卧不設席，行不騎乘，進食十數，所友百數，似無以見其長。諸葛亮為天下奇才，霍去病不學古兵法，張巡行兵不依古法，似非可目其長。然亦有可窺、可見、可目者乎？今之握邊兵而建將旗者，亦有如前所云者乎？近者虜薄榆林，擾遼東，掠大同，入固原。不但有諸將也，而又有主將焉；不但有主將也，而又有大將焉。卒未有能多為奇陳、大敗匈奴十餘萬如李牧，以大斧斷其臂、碎其首如劉錡者，其故何歟？豈皆劣才無所長歟？抑雖有才，而兵非常試，亦不敢自見其長，但彼此相諉，功不可幸而得，則罪可幸為免歟？古人有言：「兵死地，將死官。」故
translation_en:
…harsh [?], and the troops could obtain no rest. There were also those who commanded cavalry that Feng Jing could not withstand, commanded infantry that Xiang Tuo could not withstand, or employed chariots that Shujineng could not withstand. Each made use of his particular strengths. As for executing a king’s beloved concubines so that the troops would brave water and fire, or executing a ruler’s favored minister so that the entire army trembled, it seems no easy matter to discern the particular strengths involved. Sleeping without a mat, traveling without riding, offering food more than ten times [?], and numbering one’s friends in the hundreds seem to provide no means of seeing those strengths. Zhuge Liang was an extraordinary talent in the realm; Huo Qubing did not study ancient military methods; Zhang Xun conducted military operations without following ancient methods. It seems impossible to identify their particular strengths. Yet might there nevertheless be something that can be discerned, seen, and identified?

Among those who now command frontier troops and raise a general’s banner, are there any like those just described? Recently, the enemy pressed upon Yulin, harassed Liaodong, plundered Datong, and entered Guyuan. There are not merely individual generals, but chief commanders above them; and not merely chief commanders, but great generals above them. Yet ultimately none has been able to devise numerous unconventional formations and utterly defeat more than a hundred thousand Xiongnu, as Li Mu did, or to sever their arms and smash their heads with great axes, as Liu Qi did. Why is this? Are they all men of inferior ability, without any particular strengths? Or, although they possess talent, do they dare not display their strengths because warfare is no ordinary trial? Do they merely shift responsibility onto one another, thinking that although military achievements cannot be gained by luck, punishment might luckily be escaped? The ancients said: “Soldiers die on the battlefield; generals die at their posts.” Therefore…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
將受命而曰臣不敢生還士聞命而無
不㵼泣以必死故也今敗軍之將往往
得以分地為解守城為辭不曰勢不可
戰則曰時不可出卒置身於無過之地
彼此相效習以成風將無援枹忘身之
心無以令其下士無敢死樂傷之氣無
以助其上則無怪其將士聚如兒戲勝
敗付之儻來也茲欲使將皆牧錡之輩
隱然為西北長城以紓
宵旰之憂何以識其才而用之此正今日當
路者之所欲聞也
問陝西地廣而有强弓健馬之産民貧而
有忘生輕死之心且北鄰於狄西近於
羌故古人以天下之首譬之言所當重
而不可使有汚陷虧虺也我
朝防胡大鎮六而陝西三焉其重可知也三
鎮之兵素號充足近者虜來如蹈無人
之境掠饜而自引去食盡而又欲來論
punctuated:
將受命而曰：「臣不敢生還。」士聞命而無不㵼泣，以必死故也。今敗軍之將，往往得以分地為解、守城為辭，不曰勢不可戰，則曰時不可出，卒置身於無過之地。彼此相效，習以成風。將無援枹忘身之心，無以令其下；士無敢死樂傷之氣，無以助其上。則無怪其將士聚如兒戲，勝敗付之儻來也。茲欲使將皆牧、錡之輩，隱然為西北長城，以紓宵旰之憂，何以識其才而用之？此正今日當路者之所欲聞也。

問：陝西地廣，而有强弓健馬之産；民貧，而有忘生輕死之心。且北鄰於狄，西近於羌，故古人以天下之首譬之，言所當重，而不可使有汚陷虧虺也。我朝防胡大鎮六，而陝西三焉，其重可知也。三鎮之兵，素號充足。近者虜來，如蹈無人之境，掠饜而自引去，食盡而又欲來。論
translation_en:
… generals, on receiving their orders, said, “Your servant dares not return alive,” and soldiers, on hearing their orders, invariably shed tears, because they were resolved to die. Nowadays, generals whose armies have been defeated can often excuse themselves by invoking their assigned territorial responsibilities or pleading that they were defending a city. If they do not say that circumstances made battle impossible, they say that the time was unsuitable for a sortie. In the end, they place themselves beyond reproach. They imitate one another until this practice becomes customary. Generals lack the resolve to seize the drumstick and forget their own safety, and so cannot command their subordinates; soldiers lack the spirit to brave death and welcome wounds, and so cannot support their superiors. It is therefore no wonder that the assembly of their officers and men resembles children’s play, with victory and defeat left to chance. If we now wish to make all our generals men like Li Mu and Liu Qi, standing firm as a Great Wall in the northwest and relieving the worries that keep His Majesty occupied before dawn and after dark, how can we recognize their talents and employ them? This is precisely what those in authority today wish to hear.

Question: Shaanxi has extensive territory and produces strong bows and sturdy horses. Its people are poor, yet possess a spirit that disregards life and holds death lightly. Moreover, it borders the Di to the north and lies close to the Qiang to the west. Thus the ancients likened it to the head of all under Heaven, meaning that it must be given great weight and must not be allowed to suffer defilement, loss, or impairment [?]. Our dynasty has six major defense commands guarding against the Hu, and three of them are in Shaanxi: its importance is evident. The troops of these three commands have always been reputed sufficient in number. Recently, however, the enemy have come as though entering an uninhabited land, withdrawing of their own accord once sated with plunder, then wishing to return when their provisions run out. Discussion …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者曰軍少也嘗
遣廷臣以募軍矣然急一時取盈之數有未
能不爽實者茲欲軍不益而兵不乏何
以致之三鎮之兵素號勇健近者師與
多爲閉門之計敵至不能遏敵去不敢
追論者曰馬少也今
簡大臣以督馬矣然起百年已廢之政有不
能不煩民者茲欲馬不增而兵益强亦
有道乎古人有使匈奴寇邊少利希復
===
犯塞者有敵入寇必能先知預爲之備
者彼皆何人也然則軍亦當講而不專
在多者邪有言養馬太多虛耗國力者
有言馬少則騎精步多則鬬健者此豈
無稽也然則馬亦有當講而不必欲多
者邪兵與馬乃今日之急務而三鎮之
事亦諸生所目覩者寧能默然
punctuated: 者曰：「軍少也。」嘗遣廷臣以募軍矣，然急一時取盈之數，有未能不爽實者。茲欲軍不益而兵不乏，何以致之？三鎮之兵素號勇健，近者師與，多爲閉門之計，敵至不能遏，敵去不敢追。論者曰：「馬少也。」今簡大臣以督馬矣，然起百年已廢之政，有不能不煩民者。茲欲馬不增而兵益强，亦有道乎？古人有使匈奴寇邊少利、希復犯塞者，有敵入寇必能先知、預爲之備者，彼皆何人也？然則軍亦當講，而不專在多者邪？有言養馬太多、虛耗國力者，有言馬少則騎精、步多則鬬健者，此豈無稽也？然則馬亦有當講，而不必欲多者邪？兵與馬乃今日之急務，而三鎮之事亦諸生所目覩者，寧能默然？
translation_en: …those discussing the matter say: “There are too few troops.” The throne has previously dispatched court officials to recruit troops. Yet, in the haste to fill the quota for the immediate occasion, some reported numbers have failed to accord with reality. If we now wish to have sufficient military manpower without increasing the army, how can this be achieved? The troops of the three garrisons have long been reputed brave and strong. Recently, however, the armies [?] have mostly adopted the expedient of shutting their gates: when the enemy arrives, they cannot stop him; when he departs, they dare not pursue. Those discussing the matter say: “There are too few horses.” The throne has now selected high officials to supervise horse administration. Yet reviving a system abandoned for a hundred years cannot entirely avoid burdening the people. Is there a way to strengthen the troops without increasing the number of horses? Among the men of antiquity, some ensured that the Xiongnu gained little from raiding the frontier and seldom invaded it again; others invariably learned of enemy incursions in advance and made preparations against them. Who were these men? Does this not suggest that military affairs require careful consideration, rather than reliance solely on numbers? Some have said that raising too many horses needlessly drains the resources of the state; others have said that fewer horses make for picked cavalry, while more infantry make for vigorous fighting. Can these statements be without foundation? Does this not suggest that horse administration, too, requires careful consideration, without necessarily seeking greater numbers? Troops and horses are the urgent concerns of the present day, and affairs in the three garrisons are also matters you candidates have witnessed with your own eyes. Can you remain silent?

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫如是故遠人不服則脩文德以來之
胡鎰
同考試官教諭吳　批〔題本平易作者分截欠明及講遠人處殊失輕重此篇組織當時事入講且理氣充蔚讀之令人心目豁然〕
考試官學正張　批〔詞理俱到宜録〕
考試官教授方　批〔說出孔子責冉求以抑季氏意〕
===
既有以脩乎內治當有以感乎遠人盖內治脩
而文德敷感人之本也有國有家者舍是其何
以哉夫子抑冉求顓臾之謀其意盖以為治莫
先於自脩服遠無外於文德誠使吾國家之中
彼此各得分願而無貧寡之憂則既以均而和
矣上下不相疑忌而無傾覆之患則既以和而
安矣夫如是宜乎遠人之服也乃或聘問之使
弗通而負固之自若事大之禮罔脩而不恭之
自如於焉置彼度外脩我文德敬老慈幼而興
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「夫如是，故遠人不服，則脩文德以來之。」
胡鎰
同考試官教諭吳，批〔題本平易，作者分截欠明，及講遠人處，殊失輕重。此篇組織當時事入講，且理氣充蔚，讀之令人心目豁然。〕
考試官學正張，批〔詞理俱到，宜録。〕
考試官教授方，批〔說出孔子責冉求以抑季氏意。〕

既有以脩乎內治，當有以感乎遠人。盖內治脩而文德敷，感人之本也。有國有家者舍是，其何以哉？夫子抑冉求顓臾之謀，其意盖以為治莫先於自脩，服遠無外於文德。誠使吾國家之中，彼此各得分願，而無貧寡之憂，則既以均而和矣；上下不相疑忌，而無傾覆之患，則既以和而安矣。夫如是，宜乎遠人之服也。乃或聘問之使弗通，而負固之自若；事大之禮罔脩，而不恭之自如。於焉置彼度外，脩我文德，敬老慈幼而興
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When matters are thus, if distant peoples still do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to bring them here.”
Hu Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔The topic is fundamentally straightforward, but writers do not distinguish its divisions clearly, and in discussing distant peoples they seriously misjudge the relative importance of the points. This essay weaves the circumstances of the time into its exposition; its reasoning and expressive force are abundant. Reading it opens the mind and clears the vision.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Director: 〔Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. It merits inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Fang, Professor: 〔It brings out Confucius’s intention in reproaching Ran Qiu in order to restrain the Ji clan.〕

Once there are means to put internal government in order, there should also be means to move distant peoples. For orderly internal government and the spread of civil virtue are the foundation for moving others. If those who possess states or hereditary domains abandon this, what means will they have? When the Master opposed Ran Qiu’s scheme concerning Zhuanyu, his meaning was surely that nothing in government takes precedence over self-cultivation, and that bringing distant peoples to submission requires nothing beyond civil virtue. If, indeed, within our states and domains, all parties receive their due shares and have their aspirations satisfied, without anxiety over poverty or scarcity of people, then equitable distribution will already have produced harmony. If superiors and inferiors neither suspect nor resent one another, without danger of overthrow, then harmony will already have produced stability. With matters thus, distant peoples ought to submit. Yet perhaps they send no envoys on diplomatic visits and remain complacently reliant on their fortified defenses; they fail to observe the rites of serving a greater state and persist unconcernedly in their disrespect. Then set them outside your calculations and cultivate our own civil virtue: respect the aged, cherish the young, and foster …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
仁讓之風庶幾動傾向之誠而負固之志為之
潛消也惇禮崇信而脩先王之教使之被觀感
之餘而不恭之心為之默化也嘉矜有道磨歲
月以致之何患乎人各異心耶撫字有方推赤
心以待之奚慮乎民罔常懷耶夫文德脩而遠
人服其易若此彼顓臾之未服抑惟自盡焉耳
尚奚以勤兵為哉抑冉求之謀僭叛之事孔子
之言湯文之舉其大小順逆之間不待智者〔知〕
也使求也能用是言以輔季〔氏季氏〕能因是言
===
耶
之不齒也嗚呼硜硜斗筲之徒亦豈足以知此
朝諸侯不至則於晉六卿之列以為天下後世
而易道改轍焉則其事業之所就必能王魯以
故君子語大天下莫能載焉
韓邦竒
同考試官學正張　批〔中庸說理之學作者不畧則〕
泛此篇就題化出畧無冗語一結尤有深見豈亦用心
於道者耶
punctuated:
仁讓之風，庶幾動傾向之誠，而負固之志為之潛消也。惇禮崇信，而脩先王之教，使之被觀感之餘，而不恭之心為之默化也。嘉矜有道，磨歲月以致之，何患乎人各異心耶？撫字有方，推赤心以待之，奚慮乎民罔常懷耶？夫文德脩而遠人服，其易若此。彼顓臾之未服，抑惟自盡焉耳，尚奚以勤兵為哉？抑冉求之謀，僭叛之事；孔子之言，湯文之舉。其大小順逆之間，不待智者〔知〕也。使求也能用是言以輔季〔氏季氏〕，能因是言耶？之不齒也。嗚呼！硜硜斗筲之徒，亦豈足以知此？朝諸侯不至，則於晉六卿之列，以為天下後世。而易道改轍焉，則其事業之所就，必能王魯以。

故君子語大，天下莫能載焉。

韓邦竒

同考試官學正張，批〔中庸說理之學，作者不畧則〕泛。此篇就題化出，畧無冗語，一結尤有深見，豈亦用心於道者耶？
translation_en:
…a spirit of benevolence and deference, hoping thereby to awaken sincere allegiance, so that their resolve to rely on their strongholds will gradually dissolve. By honoring ritual, esteeming trustworthiness, and cultivating the teachings of the former kings, one allows their influence to reach these people through observation and inspiration, silently transforming their disrespectful hearts. With proper commendation and compassion [?], taking time to win them over, why worry that people have divided loyalties? With proper methods of nurturing the people and treating them with utter sincerity, why fear that their attachment will be inconstant? Cultivating civil virtue and securing the submission of distant peoples is as easy as this. As for Zhuanyu’s failure to submit, one need only exert oneself to the utmost. Why resort to military action? Ran Qiu’s proposal was an act of usurpation and rebellion; Confucius’s words accorded with the deeds of Tang and King Wen. The distinction between these in magnitude, and between obedience and rebellion, requires no wise person to recognize it〔recognize〕. If Qiu could have used these words to assist the Ji〔clan; the Ji clan〕, could they have acted upon these words?

[? The following columns appear out of sequence.] …being excluded from their company. Alas! How could stubborn men of paltry capacity comprehend this? …when the feudal lords failed to attend court, then among the ranks of Jin’s six ministers, for the world and later generations… And if they changed their course, their achievements would surely have enabled them to establish royal rule in Lu, thereby…

“Thus, when the gentleman speaks of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can contain it.”

Han Bangqi.

Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔In treating the Doctrine of the Mean’s learning concerning principle, writers are either cursory or〕 diffuse. This essay develops its argument directly from the topic, without any superfluous words. Its conclusion in particular shows profound insight. Might its author also be someone who applies his mind to the Way?

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正張　批〔講道之大是〕
考試官教授方　批〔理明詞順〕
中庸論道之大而世無復有大者焉蓋大而至
於天下莫能載其大也極矣道之大也有如是
夫中庸言道之費隱以明不可離之意如此謂
夫道無往而不在則無物而不該往古來今何
者而非道之所寓天高地下何者而非道之所
形彼物之大者莫天地若也天地謂之物則亦
有所盡矣有所盡非大之極也故君子語道之
===
大無得而比擬焉人之至者莫聖人若也聖人
同乎人或有拘於命矣拘於命非大之至也故
君子語道之大無得而指陳焉洋洋乎流通而
無間盖不可以限量窺也優優乎充足而有餘
有不容以涯際測也雖天地為物之大也然道
生乎天地而天地亦道中之一物耳及其至天
地尤有所未盡道之大也舉天下豈能載之哉
雖聖人為人之至也然道脩於聖人而聖人特
吾道之一人耳舉其全聖人尤有所未能道之
punctuated:
考試官學正張，批〔講道之大是〕。
考試官教授方，批〔理明詞順〕。
中庸論道之大，而世無復有大者焉。蓋大而至於天下莫能載，其大也極矣。道之大也有如是夫！中庸言道之費隱，以明不可離之意，如此。謂夫道無往而不在，則無物而不該。往古來今，何者而非道之所寓？天高地下，何者而非道之所形？彼物之大者，莫天地若也。天地謂之物，則亦有所盡矣。有所盡，非大之極也。故君子語道之大，無得而比擬焉。人之至者，莫聖人若也。聖人同乎人，或有拘於命矣。拘於命，非大之至也。故君子語道之大，無得而指陳焉。洋洋乎流通而無間，盖不可以限量窺也；優優乎充足而有餘，有不容以涯際測也。雖天地為物之大也，然道生乎天地，而天地亦道中之一物耳。及其至，天地尤有所未盡。道之大也，舉天下豈能載之哉！雖聖人為人之至也，然道脩於聖人，而聖人特吾道之一人耳。舉其全，聖人尤有所未能。道之
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of the greatness of the Way is correct.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔The reasoning is clear and the language flows smoothly.〕
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the greatness of the Way: nothing in the world is greater. Indeed, when its greatness reaches the point where nothing under Heaven can contain it, that greatness is ultimate. Such is the greatness of the Way! The Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way’s pervasive operation and hidden subtlety to clarify, in this manner, why it cannot be departed from. This means that, since the Way is present everywhere, there is nothing it does not encompass. From antiquity to the present, what has not been a dwelling place of the Way? In Heaven above and Earth below, what has not been a manifestation of the Way? Among things of great magnitude, none equals Heaven and Earth. Yet insofar as Heaven and Earth are called things, they too have their limits. Whatever has limits cannot be the ultimate in greatness. Thus, when the gentleman speaks of the greatness of the Way, nothing can serve as a comparison. Among human beings of consummate attainment, none equals the sage. Yet sages share in the human condition and may be constrained by their allotted destiny. Whatever is constrained by destiny cannot be the utmost in greatness. Thus, when the gentleman speaks of the greatness of the Way, nothing can be pointed to as an adequate expression of it. Vastly it circulates without interruption; it cannot be apprehended through finite measures. Abundantly it fills all things, with more to spare; it cannot be measured by boundaries. Although Heaven and Earth are the greatest of things, the Way gives birth to Heaven and Earth [?], and Heaven and Earth are merely one thing within the Way. In its utmost reach, there is still something that Heaven and Earth cannot exhaust. Such is the greatness of the Way: how could all under Heaven contain it? Although sages represent the highest human attainment, the Way is cultivated by sages, and a sage is merely one person within our Way. Taken in its entirety, there is still something that even sages cannot accomplish. The greatness of the Way…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
大也豈天下所能載之哉道之大而無外其用
廣矣而其所以然者則非見聞所及非所謂費
而隱乎嗟夫道雖極於至大而實具於吾心彼
寂然不動者心之體感而遂通者心之用心之
體用道之體用也但人心為形役於道始相遠
而自小耳苟能靜而存養以存其體動而省察
以達其用則大者庶於我全也後之學者與其
求道於道盍先求道於心
且一人之身而百工之所為備如必自為
而後用之是率天下而路也
王龍山
同考試官教諭王　批〔孟子一題作者類能言之率浮冗厭觀此篇剖析明白詞氣老健儼然當時闢青〕
氣象故錄
考試官學正張　批〔得孟子闢許行之旨〕
考試官教授方　批〔頗學孟子文法〕
===
一身資乎藝也衆一人無乎藝也難夫百工交
易固其理也然則以一人無為而始用焉豈理
punctuated:
大也，豈天下所能載之哉？道之大而無外，其用廣矣，而其所以然者，則非見聞所及，非所謂費而隱乎？嗟夫！道雖極於至大，而實具於吾心。彼寂然不動者，心之體；感而遂通者，心之用。心之體用，道之體用也。但人心為形役，於道始相遠，而自小耳。苟能靜而存養以存其體，動而省察以達其用，則大者庶於我全也。後之學者，與其求道於道，盍先求道於心？
且一人之身，而百工之所為備。如必自為而後用之，是率天下而路也。
王龍山
同考試官教諭王，批〔孟子一題，作者類能言之，率浮冗厭觀。此篇剖析明白，詞氣老健，儼然當時闢青〕氣象，故錄。
考試官學正張，批〔得孟子闢許行之旨。〕
考試官教授方，批〔頗學孟子文法。〕
一身資乎藝也衆，一人無乎藝也難。夫百工交易，固其理也。然則以一人無為而始用焉，豈理
translation_en:
…such is its greatness: how could all under Heaven contain it? The Way is so great that nothing lies outside it, and its operation is vast. Yet what makes it so lies beyond what can be seen or heard. Is this not what is meant by being “all-pervasive yet hidden”? Alas! Although the Way reaches the utmost greatness, it is fully present within our own minds. What remains still and unmoving is the mind’s substance; what responds to stimuli and thereby penetrates all things is the mind’s functioning. The mind’s substance and functioning are those of the Way. Only when the human mind becomes enslaved to bodily form does it grow distant from the Way and diminish itself. If, in stillness, we can preserve and nurture its substance, and, in activity, examine ourselves to realize its functioning, then perhaps this greatness can be complete within us. Rather than seeking the Way in the Way, why should later students not first seek it within their minds?
“Moreover, a single person requires the products of all the various craftsmen. If one must make everything oneself before using it, this would lead everyone under Heaven into exhaustion [路, doubtful transcription].”
Wang Longshan
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “On this passage from the Mencius, most writers can offer an explanation, but their writing is generally superficial and verbose, tiresome to read. This essay analyzes it clearly; its language and tone are mature and vigorous. It vividly conveys the spirit of the refutation of Qing [?] at that time. Therefore it has been selected.”
Examiner Zhang, School Preceptor, comments: “It captures the purport of Mencius’s refutation of Xu Xing.”
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: “It follows Mencius’s manner of composition quite closely.”
The crafts on which a single person depends are many; for a single person to be without crafts is difficult [?]. That the various craftsmen exchange their products is certainly the proper principle. If, then, a person only begins to use things after doing nothing [?], how could this accord with principle…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也哉昔孟子因陳相述許行之言闢之至此意
謂子之所謂農夫陶冶之相易正猶君子小人
之相須且即子之道而論之一身之需衣焉褐
焉冠與釜焉何者而非工之所為一人之用未
焉耜焉甑與釜焉何者而非工之所制不止於
衣褐冠屨也尤有不可以枚舉者使一工缺則
一用缺矣百工不亦備乎不獨於耒耜釜甑也
尤有不可以數計者使一工乏則一用乏矣不
亦備百工乎夫一身之用資乎衆藝如此若曰
===
百工之所成者非其力也於凡用之物而自為
之不以有無而相通必自為其工而後用之不
以彼此而相濟吾見一身有限衆藝無窮力乎
農者苦技藝之不能工於此者顧他藝之不暇
卒使天下之人衣無成也褐無成也冠屨亦無
成也擾擾焉奔走道塗疲精神於無用者我倡
之耳寧能休息乎釜無為也甑無為也耒耜亦
無為也紛紛焉往來道路勞人力於無益者我
率之耳豈能寧止乎噫百工為藝之小者且不
punctuated: 也哉？昔孟子因陳相述許行之言，闢之至此，意謂：子之所謂農夫陶冶之相易，正猶君子小人之相須。且即子之道而論之，一身之需，衣焉，褐焉，冠與釜焉，何者而非工之所為？一人之用，未焉，耜焉，甑與釜焉，何者而非工之所制？不止於衣褐冠屨也，尤有不可以枚舉者。使一工缺，則一用缺矣，百工不亦備乎？不獨於耒耜釜甑也，尤有不可以數計者。使一工乏，則一用乏矣，不亦備百工乎？夫一身之用資乎衆藝如此，若曰百工之所成者，非其力也，於凡用之物而自為之，不以有無而相通，必自為其工而後用之，不以彼此而相濟，吾見一身有限，衆藝無窮。力乎農者，苦技藝之不能；工於此者，顧他藝之不暇。卒使天下之人，衣無成也，褐無成也，冠屨亦無成也，擾擾焉奔走道塗，疲精神於無用者，我倡之耳，寧能休息乎？釜無為也，甑無為也，耒耜亦無為也，紛紛焉往來道路，勞人力於無益者，我率之耳，豈能寧止乎？噫！百工為藝之小者，且不
translation_en:
…could that accord with principle? Formerly, when Chen Xiang recounted Xu Xing’s teachings, Mengzi carried his refutation to this point. His meaning was: “What you call the exchange of goods between farmers, potters, and metalworkers is precisely like the mutual dependence of gentlemen and common people. Let us consider the matter according to your own doctrine. Among the things one person needs—clothes, coarse hemp garments, caps, and cauldrons [?]—which is not made by a craftsman? Among the things one person uses—the item transcribed as 未 [?], plowshares, steamers, and cauldrons—which is not fashioned by a craftsman? Nor is it merely clothes, hemp garments, caps, and shoes: there are further things too numerous to enumerate. If one craft is missing, one useful article will be missing. Must not all the crafts therefore be present? Nor is it merely plows, plowshares, cauldrons, and steamers: there are further things beyond counting. If one craft is lacking, one useful article will be lacking. Must one not therefore have the full range of crafts available?

“One person’s needs thus depend on many skills. Suppose you say that the products of the various craftsmen are not made by one’s own labor, and therefore insist on making every article oneself, refusing to exchange what one has for what one lacks; suppose one must personally perform the craft before using its products, refusing mutual assistance. I see that one person’s capacities are limited, while the various skills are inexhaustible. Those who devote their strength to farming suffer from their inability to practice the crafts; those skilled in one craft have no leisure for the others. In the end, this would leave the people of the world with no finished clothes, no finished hemp garments, and no finished caps or shoes. Bustling anxiously along the roads, exhausting their minds and spirits to no purpose—they would do so only because I had set this in motion. How could they find rest? No cauldrons would be made, no steamers would be made, and no plows or plowshares would be made. Hurrying to and fro along the roads, expending human labor to no benefit—they would do so only because I had led them into it. How could they find peace?

“Alas! The various crafts are but the lesser skills, yet even they cannot …”

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
可無於一人如此矧夫天下甚有大於此者尚
可耕且爲哉抑論之孟子所言天經地義聖賢
之常道許子所論旁蹊曲徑異端之小說觀其
所學之陋不惟不能害吾之正道而在彼之時
亦自難於行矣外此又有楊墨孫韓之說交熾
於當時使非孟子出而排之則人心爲其所溺
也久矣嗚呼豈天未欲後世蒙先王井田之澤
而處士橫議一至此耶
易
九二包蒙吉納婦吉子克家
劉儲秀
===
同考試官教諭吳　批〔文義頭緒頗多作者不知文已具象隨句分析破碎可厭此篇挑剔明白詞義無美蓋嘗究心於易者宜寘前列〕
考試官學正張　批〔作文辭當是如此〕
考試官教授方　批〔得潔淨旨〕
聖人於蒙九二之爻著其所具之象而示其所
應之占蓋象具於爻而占之善以之九二所以
punctuated:
可無於一人如此，矧夫天下甚有大於此者，尚可耕且爲哉？抑論之，孟子所言，天經地義，聖賢之常道；許子所論，旁蹊曲徑，異端之小說。觀其所學之陋，不惟不能害吾之正道，而在彼之時，亦自難於行矣。外此，又有楊墨孫韓之說，交熾於當時。使非孟子出而排之，則人心爲其所溺也久矣。嗚呼！豈天未欲後世蒙先王井田之澤，而處士橫議一至此耶？

易
九二，包蒙，吉；納婦，吉；子克家。
劉儲秀

考試官學正張，批〔作文辭當是如此。〕

聖人於蒙九二之爻，著其所具之象，而示其所應之占。蓋象具於爻，而占之善以之。九二所以
translation_en:
…cannot be dispensed with by a single person, as we have seen. How much more does this apply to matters in the world far greater than these! Could one still attend to them while also tilling the fields? To consider the matter further: what Mengzi taught was the constant order of Heaven and the proper order of Earth—the enduring Way of sages and worthies. What Master Xu argued consisted of side paths and crooked tracks—the petty teachings of heterodoxy. Considering the shallowness of his learning, it could not harm our correct Way; even in his own time, it was inherently difficult to put into practice. Besides this, the teachings of Yang, Mo, Sun, and Han all flourished together in that age. Had Mengzi not arisen to repudiate them, people’s hearts would long have remained submerged in their influence. Alas! Was Heaven not yet willing for later generations to enjoy the blessings of the former kings’ well-field system, that the reckless arguments of private scholars should have reached such an extreme?

Book of Changes
“Nine in the second place: embracing the ignorant brings good fortune; taking a wife brings good fortune; the son is capable of managing the household.”
Liu Chuxiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The passage has quite a number of strands of meaning. Writers do not understand that the text already contains the images; they analyze it phrase by phrase, producing a fragmentation that is tiresome. This essay distinguishes the points clearly. Its wording and meaning have no beauty [?]. The author evidently has devoted serious study to the Book of Changes and should be placed among the leading candidates.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “This is indeed how an essay should be worded.”
Comment by Examiner Fang, Professor: “It captures the purport of purity and refinement.”

In the nine in the second place of the hexagram Meng, ‘Youthful Ignorance,’ the sage sets forth the images it contains and indicates the prognostications that correspond to them. For the images are embodied in the line, and the favorable prognostications derive from them. The reason why the nine in the second place…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
備蒙之善者豈非本於象所具之自然者哉蒙
之九二以陽剛而為內卦之主統羣陰而當發
蒙之任剛而不過有包蒙之象焉以陽受陰有
納婦之象焉又居下位而能任上之事有子克
家之象焉聖人於是爻也觀是象也以為占者
有其德而當其事亦必如是而後可耳若童蒙
求我也則敷教以寬而優柔以俟其化寬柔以
敎而漸漬以待其成天下之蒙由之以發而其
道也廣矣治蒙之功因之以成而其施也博矣
===
吉何如之若往求婚媾也則納闞觀之女而無
不有躬之嫌取愆期之妹而無歸以娣之賤得
男女之正而室家宜也適婚姻之時而交相愛
也吉何似之至若當克治其家也則肯構肯堂
而有富家之道善繼善述而成前人之業嚴勵
整肅所謂裕父之蠱者無有也飭治振起所謂
幹父用譽者在是也吁爻之有善而聖人歷著
其象占如此蒙九二之義於斯盡矣抑象具於
蒙爻如此然豈無當之者乎若孔子之教人包
punctuated: 備蒙之善者，豈非本於象所具之自然者哉？蒙之九二，以陽剛而為內卦之主，統羣陰而當發蒙之任。剛而不過，有包蒙之象焉；以陽受陰，有納婦之象焉；又居下位而能任上之事，有子克家之象焉。聖人於是爻也，觀是象也，以為占者有其德而當其事，亦必如是而後可耳。若童蒙求我也，則敷教以寬而優柔以俟其化，寬柔以敎而漸漬以待其成。天下之蒙由之以發，而其道也廣矣；治蒙之功因之以成，而其施也博矣。吉何如之！若往求婚媾也，則納闞觀之女而無不有躬之嫌，取愆期之妹而無歸以娣之賤。得男女之正而室家宜也，適婚姻之時而交相愛也。吉何似之！至若當克治其家也，則肯構肯堂而有富家之道，善繼善述而成前人之業。嚴勵整肅，所謂裕父之蠱者無有也；飭治振起，所謂幹父用譽者在是也。吁！爻之有善，而聖人歷著其象占如此，蒙九二之義於斯盡矣。抑象具於蒙爻如此，然豈無當之者乎？若孔子之教人，包
translation_en:
…possesses the virtues appropriate to Youthful Ignorance: does this not arise from what its images naturally embody? The second, yang line of Youthful Ignorance, being firm and yang, governs the inner trigram. It commands the several yin lines and assumes responsibility for enlightening the ignorant. Firm without excess, it presents the image of embracing the ignorant; receiving yin with yang, it presents the image of taking a wife. Moreover, occupying a lower position while being capable of undertaking the affairs of those above, it presents the image of a son capable of managing the household. In considering this line and observing these images, the sage held that a person consulting the oracle who possesses its virtues and faces the corresponding circumstances must likewise act in this way before proceeding is fitting.

If youthful ignorance seeks me out, I spread instruction with generosity and patiently await its transformation; I teach with breadth and gentleness, allowing gradual immersion to bring it to maturity. Through this, ignorance throughout the world is enlightened, and the Way extends widely. Through this, the work of remedying ignorance is accomplished, and its benefits spread broadly. What good fortune could equal this! If one goes to seek a marriage alliance, one takes in a woman who peers out [?], without the suspicion that she has lost possession of herself; one marries a maiden whose appointed time has passed, without the low status of marrying as a secondary wife. The proper relationship between man and woman is secured, and the household enjoys harmony; the appropriate time for marriage is met, and the two love one another. What good fortune could compare with this!

As for being capable of governing the household, one is willing both to lay its foundations and to build upon them, possessing the means of enriching the family; one skillfully continues and carries forward what came before, completing the work of one’s predecessors. Through stern diligence and orderly discipline, there is none of what is called ‘indulging the corruption left by the father.’ Through putting affairs in order and restoring their vigor, what is called ‘setting right the father’s affairs and thereby earning praise’ is realized here. Ah! Such are the virtues of this line, and such is the sage’s successive exposition of its images and prognostications. The meaning of the second, yang line of Youthful Ignorance is fully expressed in this.

Yet, if these are the images embodied in the lines of Youthful Ignorance, can there be no people who correspond to them? Take Confucius’s teaching of others: embracing…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
蒙之吉也文王之配后納婦之吉也武王之纘
緒子之克家者也要之三聖人者亦偶然與之
合耳推之天下之事萬物之理何者不可體而
為之乎說者猶以卜筮小吾易是豈知易者哉
變化者進退之象也
胡鎰
同考試官教諭吳　批〔繫義人多泛說理此篇本聖人作易立說而據理精到必老於易者取冠本房〕
考試官學正張　批〔講進退人不能到〕
===
考試官教授方　批〔理學極明白〕
論剛柔之相易者乃消息之可見者甚矣卦爻
陰陽迭相變易也即是觀之則進退之象豈不
於是而可見乎大傳論聖人作易上既言剛柔
相推以生變化此復明變化之義意謂觀卦爻
於易則剛柔有定位求卦爻於蓍則剛柔無定
居是故陰而耦者卦爻之柔也柔或有時而推
夫剛則柔不一於柔矣陽而奇者剛也剛或有
時而推夫柔則剛不專於剛矣六而之七勃然
punctuated:
蒙之吉也，文王之配后，納婦之吉也；武王之纘緒，子之克家者也。要之，三聖人者亦偶然與之合耳。推之天下之事、萬物之理，何者不可體而為之乎？說者猶以卜筮小吾易，是豈知易者哉？
變化者，進退之象也。
胡鎰
同考試官教諭吳批〔繫義，人多泛說理。此篇本聖人作易立說，而據理精到，必老於易者。取冠本房。〕
考試官學正張批〔講進退，人不能到。〕
考試官教授方批〔理學極明白。〕
論剛柔之相易者，乃消息之可見者，甚矣！卦爻陰陽迭相變易也，即是觀之，則進退之象豈不於是而可見乎？大傳論聖人作易，上既言剛柔相推以生變化，此復明變化之義。意謂觀卦爻於易，則剛柔有定位；求卦爻於蓍，則剛柔無定居。是故陰而耦者，卦爻之柔也。柔或有時而推夫剛，則柔不一於柔矣。陽而奇者，剛也。剛或有時而推夫柔，則剛不專於剛矣。六而之七，勃然
translation_en:
…the auspiciousness of nurturing the unenlightened. King Wen’s union with his consort exemplifies the auspiciousness of taking a wife; King Wu’s continuation of the royal succession exemplifies the son’s ability to manage the household. In sum, these three sages merely happened to accord with these meanings. Extending this to the affairs of the world and the principles of all things, what could not be embodied and put into practice? Yet interpreters still belittle our Book of Changes by treating it as mere divination. Can they really understand the Changes?

“Change and transformation are images of advance and retreat.”

Hu Yi 胡鎰

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔In interpreting the meaning of the Appended Statements, most people discuss principles in generalities. This essay bases its argument on the sages’ making of the Changes, and its reasoning is precise and penetrating. Its author must be a seasoned student of the Changes. Selected as the best in this examining room.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Its explanation of advance and retreat reaches where others cannot.〕

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: 〔Its exposition of the learning of principle is exceptionally clear.〕

I submit that the interchange of the firm and the yielding makes waxing and waning visible. How striking this is! In the hexagrams and their lines, yin and yang alternate and change into one another. Viewed in this light, are not the images of advance and retreat thereby made visible? In discussing the sages’ making of the Changes, the Great Commentary has already stated above that the firm and the yielding push upon one another to produce change and transformation. Here it further elucidates the meaning of change and transformation. Its intention is to say that, when we examine the hexagrams and lines in the Changes, the firm and the yielding have fixed positions; but when we seek hexagrams and lines through yarrow stalks, the firm and the yielding have no fixed abode. Thus, what is yin and even constitutes the yielding in the hexagrams and lines. Yet the yielding sometimes pushes upon the firm, so it does not invariably remain yielding. What is yang and odd constitutes the firm. Yet the firm sometimes pushes upon the yielding, so it does not exclusively remain firm. When six becomes seven, vigorously…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
浸長之莫過也非所謂變乎九而之八默然形
迹之莫窺也非所謂化乎是皆具於分掛揲扐
之後參伍錯綜之餘者也易之所謂變化者以
此然是變化也則為進退之象焉柔者陰之退
也退極而進為剛凡天下之由退而進者皆此
理也剛者陽之進也進極而退為柔凡天下之
由進而退者皆是物也數盈於十柔退而至於
六其後之五乃生數無可退者自息而至於七
以進之焉柔之變非進之象乎數起於一剛進
===
而至於九其前之十乃極數無可進者自消而
至於八以退之焉剛之化非退之象乎是皆出
於理勢之自然而非人之所能損益者也變化
之為進退之象如此吁聖人以進退而明變化
其義無餘蘊矣抑是變化也極而復為剛柔流
行於一卦六爻之間占者得因所值以斷吉凶
者蓋與剛柔相推以生變化循環而無端也然
變化剛柔微者也進退晝夜顯者也非至著之
象固無以明其理然非理以主之幾何而不至
punctuated: 浸長之莫過也，非所謂變乎？九而之八，默然形迹之莫窺也，非所謂化乎？是皆具於分掛揲扐之後、參伍錯綜之餘者也。《易》之所謂變化者，以此。然是變化也，則為進退之象焉。柔者，陰之退也；退極而進為剛，凡天下之由退而進者，皆此理也。剛者，陽之進也；進極而退為柔，凡天下之由進而退者，皆是物也。數盈於十，柔退而至於六，其後之五乃生數，無可退者，自息而至於七以進之焉。柔之變，非進之象乎？數起於一，剛進而至於九，其前之十乃極數，無可進者，自消而至於八以退之焉。剛之化，非退之象乎？是皆出於理勢之自然，而非人之所能損益者也。變化之為進退之象如此。吁！聖人以進退而明變化，其義無餘蘊矣。抑是變化也，極而復為剛柔，流行於一卦六爻之間，占者得因所值以斷吉凶者，蓋與剛柔相推以生變化，循環而無端也。然變化剛柔，微者也；進退晝夜，顯者也。非至著之象，固無以明其理；然非理以主之，幾何而不至
translation_en:
…nothing surpasses its gradual growth—is this not what is called change? When nine becomes eight, it does so silently, its traces impossible to discern—is this not what is called transformation? These are all present after the operations of dividing the stalks, setting one aside, counting them off, and placing the remainders between the fingers, and after grouping and cross-checking the numbers. This is what the Book of Changes means by change and transformation. Such change and transformation are images of advance and retreat. The yielding is the retreat of yin; when retreat reaches its utmost, it advances and becomes firm. Everything under Heaven that passes from retreat to advance follows this principle. The firm is the advance of yang; when advance reaches its utmost, it retreats and becomes yielding. Everything under Heaven that passes from advance to retreat exemplifies this same thing.

Numbers reach their fullness at ten. The yielding retreats until it reaches six; five, which lies behind it, is a generating number, so there is no further retreat available. It grows of itself until it reaches seven, thereby advancing. Is the change of the yielding not an image of advance? Numbers begin at one. The firm advances until it reaches nine; ten, which lies ahead of it, is the ultimate number, so there is no further advance available. It wanes of itself until it reaches eight, thereby retreating. Is the transformation of the firm not an image of retreat? All this arises naturally from principle and the tendency of things; it is not something that human beings can diminish or augment. Such is the way change and transformation serve as images of advance and retreat.

Ah! By explaining change and transformation through advance and retreat, the sage leaves none of their meaning undisclosed. Yet these changes and transformations, upon reaching their utmost, again become firmness and yielding, circulating among the six lines of a hexagram. That the diviner can judge good or ill fortune according to what is encountered is because this process, together with firmness and yielding impelling one another to produce change and transformation, forms a cycle without beginning or end. Change and transformation, firmness and yielding, are subtle; advance and retreat, day and night, are manifest. Without utterly manifest images, there would indeed be no means of illuminating their principle. Yet without principle to govern them, how could they fail to lapse into…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
於無且誕耶故曰六爻之動三極之道也噫易
爲人謀於此尤可見云
書
無教逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日萬幾
無曠庶官天工人其代之
韓邦奇
同考試官訓導陳　批〔臯陶之學極純粹故見於陳謨如此此篇能摸寫之其璧經中之翹楚者乎〕
同考試官學正張　批〔能體認臯陶陳謨之意而發揮之無踰此作〕
===
考試官學正張　批〔意語俱到〕
考試官教授方　批〔明白〕
大臣之於聖君戒其謹於率下而言其所當謹
戒其公於用人而言其所當公甚矣萬幾不可
忽天工不可廢也人君於此顧可不以縱逸欲
用非才爲戒哉昔臯陶陳知人之謨至此蓋謂
百辟視君身以爲儀刑率之有道也當以勤率
之不可教之以逸以儉率之不可導之以欲要
punctuated:
於無且誕耶？故曰：「六爻之動，三極之道也。」噫！易爲人謀，於此尤可見云。

書
「無教逸欲有邦，兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。無曠庶官，天工人其代之。」
韓邦奇
同考試官訓導陳，批〔臯陶之學極純粹，故見於陳謨如此。此篇能摸寫之，其璧經中之翹楚者乎？〕
同考試官學正張，批〔能體認臯陶陳謨之意而發揮之，無踰此作。〕
考試官學正張，批〔意語俱到。〕
考試官教授方，批〔明白。〕

大臣之於聖君，戒其謹於率下，而言其所當謹；戒其公於用人，而言其所當公。甚矣，萬幾不可忽，天工不可廢也！人君於此，顧可不以縱逸欲、用非才爲戒哉？昔臯陶陳知人之謨，至此蓋謂：百辟視君身以爲儀刑，率之有道也。當以勤率之，不可教之以逸；以儉率之，不可導之以欲。要
translation_en:
…into emptiness and absurdity? Thus it is said: “The movements of the six lines embody the Way of the Three Powers.” Ah! How the Changes provides counsel for human beings is especially apparent here.

Documents
“Do not teach those who possess states to indulge in ease and desire. Be vigilant and cautious: in a day or two, myriad incipient affairs arise. Do not leave the various offices unfilled; humans must perform Heaven’s work in its stead.”
Han Bangqi
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Gao Yao’s learning was supremely pure, and thus it found expression in his presentation of counsels in this manner. This essay succeeds in portraying it. Surely it ranks among the outstanding essays on the Classics [?].〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔For grasping and expounding the meaning of Gao Yao’s presentation of counsels, no work surpasses this one.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Both the ideas and their expression are fully realized.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and lucid.〕

In addressing a sage ruler, a great minister admonishes him to take care in leading his subordinates and explains where such care is due; he admonishes him to be impartial in employing men and explains where such impartiality is due. How vital it is that the myriad incipient affairs not be neglected and Heaven’s work not be abandoned! In these matters, can the ruler fail to guard against indulgence in ease and desire and the employment of men without the requisite abilities? When Gao Yao long ago presented his counsels on discerning men’s qualities, his meaning at this point was, in essence: All the lords look to the ruler’s own person as their model, and there is a proper way to lead them. He should lead them through diligence, never teaching them ease; he should lead them through frugality, never guiding them toward desire. What is essential is …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
必兢兢其心而戒謹之不忽業業其念而危懼
之恒存所以然者蓋以一日二日之間而事幾
之來有萬其繁于焉不察則禍患之所由生今
日明日之際而事幾之至有萬其多于焉不審
則怠荒之所由起是萬幾也君惟兢業以圖之
豈可一日而縱欲乎庶官輔人君以理萬幾任
之有要也當無用非才而使庶官曠其職勿任
非人而使百僚瘝厥官要必嚴於遴選務登崇
俊良慎於簡擇惟進用賢哲所以然者蓋以人
===
君代天以圖萬幾庶官分圖者無非天之事官
曠則廢其事人君代天以理萬物庶官分理者
無非天之工官曠則隳厥工是庶官也君惟任
賢以宅之豈可一職之或曠乎吁臯陶陳知人
之謨而終之以此可謂善導君者矣抑考有虞
之時四方有風動之休萬邦有咸寧之美若無
待於戒飭矣臯臣為國之心猶有覆盆遺照之
慮此知人安民之謀切切而陳於當時也奈何
後世僅底小康便忘戒飭君日驕而臣日諂此
punctuated: 必兢兢其心，而戒謹之不忽；業業其念，而危懼之恒存。所以然者，蓋以一日二日之間，而事幾之來有萬其繁，于焉不察，則禍患之所由生；今日明日之際，而事幾之至有萬其多，于焉不審，則怠荒之所由起。是萬幾也，君惟兢業以圖之，豈可一日而縱欲乎？庶官輔人君以理萬幾，任之有要也。當無用非才而使庶官曠其職，勿任非人而使百僚瘝厥官。要必嚴於遴選，務登崇俊良；慎於簡擇，惟進用賢哲。所以然者，蓋以人君代天以圖萬幾，庶官分圖者，無非天之事，官曠則廢其事；人君代天以理萬物，庶官分理者，無非天之工，官曠則隳厥工。是庶官也，君惟任賢以宅之，豈可一職之或曠乎？吁！臯陶陳知人之謨，而終之以此，可謂善導君者矣。抑考有虞之時，四方有風動之休，萬邦有咸寧之美，若無待於戒飭矣。臯臣為國之心，猶有覆盆遺照之慮，此知人安民之謀切切而陳於當時也。奈何後世僅底小康，便忘戒飭，君日驕而臣日諂，此
translation_en:
…he must keep his heart ever vigilant, never neglecting caution, and his thoughts ever watchful, constantly preserving a sense of peril and apprehension. The reason is that, within a day or two, the incipient affairs that arise number in the myriad: failure to discern them is the source of calamity. Between today and tomorrow, the incipient affairs that arrive are myriad in number: failure to examine them is the source of indolence and neglect. These are the myriad affairs. The ruler must attend to them with vigilance and watchfulness; how could he indulge his desires for even a single day? The various officials assist the ruler in managing these myriad affairs, and there are essential principles governing their appointment. He must not employ those without ability and thereby cause officials to neglect their duties, nor appoint unsuitable men and thereby cause the whole body of officials to leave their offices untended. He must be rigorous in selection, striving to elevate the talented and good, and careful in choosing, advancing only the worthy and wise. The reason is that the ruler attends to the myriad affairs on Heaven’s behalf, and the portions entrusted to the various officials are all Heaven’s business: when an office is left untended, that business is neglected. The ruler orders the myriad things on Heaven’s behalf, and the portions entrusted to the various officials are all Heaven’s work: when an office is left untended, that work is ruined. Such are the various offices. The ruler must appoint worthy men to occupy them; how could even a single office be left untended?

Ah! Gao Yao presented his counsel on discerning men’s character and abilities and concluded it with these words. He may indeed be called one who knew how to guide his ruler. Yet consider the age of Youyu: throughout the four quarters, people responded to his transforming influence as things stir in the wind, and the myriad states enjoyed universal peace. It would seem that there was no need for admonition. Yet the minister Gao, in his concern for the state, still feared that some might be missed by its illumination, like what lies beneath an overturned basin. This is why he so earnestly presented his counsel on discerning men and bringing peace to the people at that time. How is it that later generations, upon attaining only modest well-being, immediately forgot caution, with rulers growing daily more arrogant and ministers daily more flattering? This…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
治道所以終愧於古也可勝嘆哉
百姓王人罔不秉德明恤小臣屏侯甸矧
咸奔走
尚班爵
同考試官訓導刁　批〔講內外得人與秉德明恤矧咸奔走處極爲明著是用錄出以式將來〕
考試官學正張　批〔文無剩語〕
考試官教授方　批〔整潔〕
職列於內者有其人職列於外者有其人大臣
===
言前代然也甚矣賢才有關於人國也有商之
臣合內外而皆賢焉則其國有人而實矣宜周
公舉之以留召公也且其意蓋謂成王幼冲公
固不當去天命未凝公尤不可去盍觀有商之
事乎上天有佑命之純故當時生賢才之盛其
在內也百官著姓位之尊者也與夫王臣之微
位之卑者也尊卑雖有不同不罔不秉持其德確
乎貞良而不回凜乎節義而不變忠懇爲之拳
拳也顯微雖有不一無不明致其憂上懼天命
punctuated:
治道所以終愧於古也，可勝嘆哉！

百姓王人罔不秉德明恤，小臣屏侯甸，矧咸奔走。

尚班爵

同考試官訓導刁　批〔講內外得人與秉德明恤矧咸奔走處極爲明著是用錄出以式將來〕
考試官學正張　批〔文無剩語〕
考試官教授方　批〔整潔〕

職列於內者有其人，職列於外者有其人。大臣言前代然也。甚矣，賢才有關於人國也！有商之臣，合內外而皆賢焉，則其國有人而實矣，宜周公舉之以留召公也。且其意蓋謂：成王幼冲，公固不當去；天命未凝，公尤不可去。盍觀有商之事乎？上天有佑命之純，故當時生賢才之盛。其在內也，百官著姓，位之尊者也；與夫王臣之微，位之卑者也。尊卑雖有不同，不罔不秉持其德，確乎貞良而不回，凜乎節義而不變，忠懇爲之拳拳也。顯微雖有不一，無不明致其憂，上懼天命
translation_en:
…This is why the way of governing ultimately falls short of antiquity. How deeply lamentable!

“The officials of the great lineages and the king’s men all upheld virtue and clearly understood their responsibilities; the lesser servants and the protective lords of the hou and dian domains—how much more did they all hasten about their duties!”

Shang Banjue

Associate Examiner Diao, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of finding suitable men for service within and outside the court, and of the passages ‘upheld virtue and clearly understood their responsibilities’ and ‘how much more did they all hasten about their duties,’ is exceptionally clear. Accordingly, this essay has been selected and recorded as a model for future candidates.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The essay contains no superfluous words.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔Orderly and polished.〕

For offices within the court there were suitable men; for offices outside the court there were suitable men. A great minister spoke of the preceding dynasty as having been thus. How profoundly worthy talent affects a state! The ministers of Shang, both within and outside the court, were all worthy; thus its state was indeed amply supplied with capable men. It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should cite this to persuade the Duke of Shao to remain. His meaning was presumably this: King Cheng was still young, so the duke certainly ought not to depart; Heaven’s Mandate was not yet secure, so all the more must he remain. Why not consider the affairs of Shang? Heaven bestowed its abundant favor and mandate, and therefore worthy talent arose in such profusion at that time.

Within the court, the officials of prominent lineages occupied exalted positions, while the king’s humbler servants occupied lowly ones. Although their ranks differed, all upheld their virtue [?]: steadfast in integrity and goodness, they did not turn aside; resolute in principle and righteousness, they did not change. They devoted themselves earnestly to loyalty and sincerity. Although some were prominent and others obscure, all clearly understood and gave full expression to their concern: above, they feared that Heaven’s Mandate…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之靡常下慮小民之無賴誠意爲之切切也則
在內者無不賢矣其在外也凡百執事職之小
者也與夫藩屏侯甸職之大者也大小不一其
職矧皆奔走王事或致身而宣力或鞠躬而盡
瘁爲之不厭其勤也遠近不一其地矧咸趨承
王命或承流而宣化或折衝以禦侮任之不憚
其勞也則在外者無不賢矣內外皆賢則商國
有人而實令日公可求去使我周空虛而無人
哉雖然周公此言有商得人之盛以留之下文
===
又言文武得人之助致拳拳之意不一言而足
蓋其憂之深故留之切其留之切故言之詳無
非欲其輔成王而凝固天命也宜乎召公之心
油然而感惕然而留厥後既相成王又相康王
再世尤未釋其政有味於周公之言也夫
詩
二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌陰
王龍山
同考試官教諭王　批〔藏冰備暑莫大于節陽薦祭〕
punctuated:
之靡常，下慮小民之無賴，誠意爲之切切也，則在內者無不賢矣。其在外也，凡百執事，職之小者也，與夫藩屏侯甸，職之大者也。大小不一其職，矧皆奔走王事，或致身而宣力，或鞠躬而盡瘁，爲之不厭其勤也。遠近不一其地，矧咸趨承王命，或承流而宣化，或折衝以禦侮，任之不憚其勞也，則在外者無不賢矣。內外皆賢，則商國有人而實。令日公可求去，使我周空虛而無人哉？雖然，周公此言有商得人之盛以留之，下文又言文武得人之助，致拳拳之意，不一言而足。蓋其憂之深，故留之切；其留之切，故言之詳，無非欲其輔成王而凝固天命也。宜乎召公之心油然而感，惕然而留。厥後既相成王，又相康王，再世尤未釋其政，有味於周公之言也夫！
詩
二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。
王龍山
同考試官教諭王　批〔藏冰備暑，莫大于節陽薦祭〕
translation_en:
…the inconstancy of Heaven’s mandate, and below they worried that the common people had nothing to rely upon: their sincerity was earnest indeed. Thus all those serving within the court were worthy. As for those serving outside it, the various functionaries held lesser offices, while the regional lords who formed its protective bulwark held greater ones. Though their offices differed in importance, all hastened about the king’s business. Some devoted themselves to exerting their strength; others bent to their tasks and exhausted themselves in service, never wearying of their exertions. Though their territories differed in distance from the court, all hastened to carry out the king’s commands. Some disseminated his beneficent influence and spread his transforming instruction; others repelled aggression and resisted insult, undertaking their duties without shrinking from the toil. Thus all those serving outside the court were worthy. With worthy men both within and without, the Shang realm was well supplied with capable servants. Could you, my lord, now [?] seek to depart, leaving our Zhou empty and bereft of men?
Here the Duke of Zhou speaks of the abundance of capable men obtained by Shang in order to persuade the Duke of Shao to stay; further below, he also speaks of the assistance that Kings Wen and Wu received from capable men. A single statement did not suffice to convey his earnest concern. Because his anxiety was deep, his plea that the duke remain was urgent; because that plea was urgent, his words were detailed. His sole desire was that the duke assist King Cheng and firmly secure Heaven’s mandate. It was fitting, then, that the Duke of Shao should feel spontaneously moved and, with an apprehensive sense of duty, remain. Thereafter he served as chief minister to King Cheng and then to King Kang. Even through two reigns he had yet to relinquish his governmental responsibilities: he had indeed savored the meaning of the Duke of Zhou’s words!
Book of Odes
“In the days of the second month, they hew the ice with resounding blows; in the days of the third month, they bring it into the icehouse.”
Wang Longshan
