Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔In storing ice against the summer heat, nothing is more important than regulating the force of yang and presenting sacrificial offerings…〕

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此作得之且措詞整潔脫去冗腐必佳士也範經之冠
舍子共誰
考試官學正張　批〔說出豳民忠愛之意〕
考試官教授方　批〔有詩人風味〕
豳人勸趨乎冰役有以時取之者有以時藏之
者盖冰所以為君備暑者也豳人兩及其時而
勸趨是役焉忠愛其君之心為何如哉昔周公
以成王秊幼嗣艱難之業故陳后稷公劉風化
之所由使瞽矇諷誦以教之至此謂夫冰為吾
===
君之用大矣所以節陽氣者在是所以薦寢廟
者在是取藏容可以失時乎故於斗柄建丑之
候二陽巳動之時斯時也栗冽之氣正寒冰可
取也不於此而取之何以給我君之用乎於是
我豳人當無小無大而奔走於深山窮谷之間
凡冰之所在則伐之冲冲而不憚其力焉從事
於固陰沍寒之際凡冰之所萃則鑿之冲冲而
不辭其勞焉懽心以從而惟恐不及也同聲以
應而惟恐或後也伊誰迫哉皆吾民分所當然
punctuated:
此作得之，且措詞整潔，脫去冗腐，必佳士也。範經之冠，舍子共誰？
考試官學正張，批〔說出豳民忠愛之意〕
考試官教授方，批〔有詩人風味〕
豳人勸趨乎冰役，有以時取之者，有以時藏之者。盖冰所以為君備暑者也。豳人兩及其時而勸趨是役焉，忠愛其君之心為何如哉！昔周公以成王秊幼，嗣艱難之業，故陳后稷、公劉風化之所由，使瞽矇諷誦以教之。至此，謂夫冰為吾君之用大矣！所以節陽氣者在是，所以薦寢廟者在是，取藏容可以失時乎？故於斗柄建丑之候，二陽巳動之時，斯時也，栗冽之氣正寒，冰可取也。不於此而取之，何以給我君之用乎？於是我豳人當無小無大，而奔走於深山窮谷之間。凡冰之所在，則伐之冲冲，而不憚其力焉；從事於固陰沍寒之際，凡冰之所萃，則鑿之冲冲，而不辭其勞焉。懽心以從，而惟恐不及也；同聲以應，而惟恐或後也。伊誰迫哉？皆吾民分所當然
translation_en:
…This composition grasps the point. Moreover, its wording is orderly and polished, free of verbosity and stale expressions: its author must be a fine scholar. As for first place among model treatments of this Classic [?], who but you could claim it [?]?
Examiner Zhang, a school instructor, comments: 〔It brings out the loyal affection of the people of Bin.〕
Examiner Fang, a professor, comments: 〔It has the flavor of a poet’s work.〕
The people of Bin eagerly undertook the labor of harvesting ice: some gathered it at the proper time, and some stored it at the proper time. Ice was used to prepare for their lord’s needs in the summer heat. That the people of Bin eagerly undertook this labor at both appointed times—how great was their loyal affection for their lord! Formerly, because King Cheng was young and had inherited a royal enterprise established through hardship, the Duke of Zhou set forth the sources of the moral influence exerted by Hou Ji and Gong Liu, and had blind musicians recite the verses to instruct him. At this point, the poem says: ice is of great use to our lord! It serves to regulate the yang energies; it serves for offerings in the ancestral temples. Could we allow its gathering and storage to miss their proper times? Thus, when the handle of the Dipper points to chou, and the two yang forces have already begun to stir, the biting air is truly cold, and ice can be gathered. If we do not gather it now, how shall we supply our lord’s needs? Thereupon we people of Bin, great and small alike, must hasten through deep mountains and remote valleys. Wherever ice is found, we cut it with resounding blows, undaunted by the exertion. Working amid firm-set yin and freezing cold, wherever ice has accumulated, we hew it with resounding blows, ungrudging of the toil. We follow gladly, fearing only that we may not arrive in time; we respond with one voice, fearing only that we may lag behind. Who compels us? All this is simply what our duty as subjects requires…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
耳迨夫斗柄建寅之日三陽用事之時斯時也
堅凝之凍未解而冰可藏也不於此而藏之何
以備我公之需乎於是我豳民則同心同力以
向之所取者是任是負納之于凌陰之中以昔
之所鑿者筐之筥之藏之于冰室之內備之以
其時而不使缺也藏之得其所而不使解也伊
誰驅哉皆吾民義所當為耳吁豳人雖勸趨藏
冰而忠愛之心寓焉周公述之以啓成王意亦
深矣哉抑論之上以誠愛下下以忠利上此自
然之符也大王都邑一遷而從者歸市文王靈
臺一作而庶民子來豳公冰役一興而民樂趨
事有周篤於愛民而民之從之自不容已周公
述是為成王告可謂善於啓迪者矣厥後成王
果能基命宥密以為一代守成之令主意者有
得於此
===
旣立之監或佐之史
田登
同考試官教諭王　批〔監史皆察儀之官作者類多〕
punctuated:
耳。迨夫斗柄建寅之日，三陽用事之時，斯時也，堅凝之凍未解，而冰可藏也。不於此而藏之，何以備我公之需乎？於是我豳民則同心同力，以向之所取者，是任是負，納之于凌陰之中；以昔之所鑿者，筐之筥之，藏之于冰室之內。備之以其時，而不使缺也；藏之得其所，而不使解也。伊誰驅哉？皆吾民義所當為耳。吁！豳人雖勸趨藏冰，而忠愛之心寓焉。周公述之以啓成王，意亦深矣哉！抑論之，上以誠愛下，下以忠利上，此自然之符也。大王都邑一遷，而從者歸市；文王靈臺一作，而庶民子來；豳公冰役一興，而民樂趨事。有周篤於愛民，而民之從之自不容已。周公述是為成王告，可謂善於啓迪者矣。厥後成王果能基命宥密，以為一代守成之令主，意者有得於此。

旣立之監，或佐之史。
田登。
同考試官教諭王，批〔監史皆察儀之官，作者類多〕
translation_en:
…that is all. When the Dipper’s handle points toward yin and the three yang forces hold sway, the solid frost has not yet thawed, and ice can be stored. If we do not store it now, how can we provide for our lord’s needs? Thus our people of Bin unite their hearts and efforts: they shoulder and carry the ice previously gathered and bring it into the ice cellar; they pack the ice previously hewn into square and round baskets and store it in the ice chamber. They make provision at the proper season so that there will be no shortage, and store it in a suitable place so that it will not melt. Who drives them to this? It is simply what righteousness requires our people to do. Ah! Though the people of Bin eagerly hasten to store the ice, their loyalty and affection are embodied in this work. The Duke of Zhou’s purpose in recounting it to instruct King Cheng was indeed profound!

To consider the matter further: those above love those below with sincerity, and those below benefit those above with loyalty. This is a natural correspondence. Once King Tai moved his capital, followers flocked to him as to a marketplace; once King Wen began building the Spirit Terrace, the common people came like children to their parent; once the lord of Bin initiated the ice-gathering service, the people gladly hastened to the task. The Zhou rulers were steadfast in their love for the people, and the people could not help following them. In recounting this to King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou may indeed be called skilled in instruction. Thereafter King Cheng truly established his rule with magnanimity and quiet diligence, becoming an excellent ruler who preserved his dynasty’s achievements. Presumably he had learned something from this.

“An overseer has already been appointed for them, and a scribe assists him.”

Tian Deng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The overseer and the scribe are both officials charged with scrutinizing ceremonial conduct. Writers generally …〕

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
分破似與朱註背馳此篇體認真切辭亦嚴正必熟
于是經者高捷何忝
考試官學正張　批〔寫出當時警戒氣象〕
考試官教授方　批〔用祭射飲酒立說良是〕
賢侯之燕飲必兩設官以察其儀焉蓋飲酒易
至有過也茍非設官以交察之安能肅其儀而
保其無過哉昔衛武公飲酒悔過而作此詩吾
想其意謂夫我之燕賔有因祭而飲之禮焉有
因射而飲之禮焉然羣飲每至於喪儀也不設
===
官以察之可乎彼司正之屬有所謂監焉乃察
儀法者也監焉不立則在燕者無所警矣故必
立是官以察其儀使旁觀乎賔主或醉或否無
一而不察焉遍覽乎左右曰臧曰否無一而不
監焉孰能敬慎威儀而禮度之是守孰為亂我
籩豆而荒湛之是耽一觸目之間使凜然知所
警也然一官不能以獨理也不設官以佐之可
乎彼司正之屬又有所謂史焉亦察儀法者也
史焉不佐則與席者無所戒矣故必佐之史以
punctuated:
分破，似與朱註背馳。此篇體認真切，辭亦嚴正，必熟于是經者，高捷何忝！

考試官學正張，批〔寫出當時警戒氣象〕

考試官教授方，批〔用祭射飲酒立說，良是〕

賢侯之燕飲，必兩設官以察其儀焉。蓋飲酒易至有過也，茍非設官以交察之，安能肅其儀而保其無過哉？昔衛武公飲酒悔過而作此詩，吾想其意謂：夫我之燕賔，有因祭而飲之禮焉，有因射而飲之禮焉。然羣飲每至於喪儀也，不設官以察之可乎？彼司正之屬，有所謂監焉，乃察儀法者也。監焉不立，則在燕者無所警矣。故必立是官以察其儀，使旁觀乎賔主，或醉或否，無一而不察焉；遍覽乎左右，曰臧曰否，無一而不監焉。孰能敬慎威儀而禮度之是守？孰為亂我籩豆而荒湛之是耽？一觸目之間，使凜然知所警也。然一官不能以獨理也，不設官以佐之可乎？彼司正之屬，又有所謂史焉，亦察儀法者也。史焉不佐，則與席者無所戒矣。故必佐之史以
translation_en:
…treat them separately in the opening exposition, seemingly running counter to Zhu Xi’s commentary. This essay grasps the meaning truly and precisely, and its language is also dignified and correct. Its author must be thoroughly versed in this Classic. What could be undeserved about his passing with a high rank?

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔It conveys the atmosphere of vigilance and admonition at the time.〕

Examiner Fang, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔Building the argument around drinking at sacrifices and archery ceremonies is indeed sound.〕

When a worthy lord holds a drinking banquet, he invariably appoints two officials to watch over its decorum. Drinking readily leads to transgressions. Unless officials are appointed to exercise joint scrutiny, how can decorum be maintained and freedom from transgression assured? Duke Wu of Wei once regretted his faults in drinking and composed this poem. I imagine his meaning to have been as follows: When I entertain guests at a banquet, there are rites of drinking following sacrifices and rites of drinking following archery. Yet drinking in company often leads to a loss of decorum. Can we dispense with appointing an official to watch over it?

Among those serving as directors of ceremony is one called the monitor, who scrutinizes decorum and its rules. If no monitor is appointed, those at the banquet will have nothing to put them on their guard. Thus this official must be appointed to observe their deportment. Let him watch host and guests from the side: whether drunk or sober, not one escapes his scrutiny. Let him survey everyone to his left and right: whether behaving well or badly, not one escapes his supervision. Who attends reverently and carefully to his deportment and abides by ritual standards? Who disorders my offering baskets and stands and indulges in drunken excess? The moment his gaze falls upon them, let them feel awe and know to be vigilant.

Yet one official cannot manage this alone. Can we dispense with appointing an official to assist him? Among those serving as directors of ceremony is also one called the scribe, who likewise scrutinizes decorum and its rules. If the scribe does not assist, those attending the feast will have nothing to admonish them. Thus he must be assisted by a scribe in order to…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
察其儀使醉否之情狀必書之而無隱藏否之
實跡必紀之而無遺其也令儀令色有德之孔
嘉其也載號載呶伐德之可恥一載筆之頃俾
肅然知所戒也夫以一燕飲之間而防範之嚴
有如此武公其善於悔過而果於進德者歟抑
論飲酒細事而聖狂分焉書曰不矜細行終累
大德又曰惟公懋德克勤小物其以此歟武公
深知乎此故荒湛于酒既陳於自警之篇飲酒
悔過又形於賓筵之雅殆與大禹之所惡周公
之所誥者異世而同符也衛之賢君武公稱首
焉
===
春秋
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男滑伯滕
子同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕
穆世傑
考試官學正張　批〔得春秋家法〕
考試官教授方　批〔胡傳兩言齊桓始霸之意作〕
者多拙於穀梁尊周一偏之說殊失本旨此卷獨□
punctuated:
察其儀，使醉否之情狀必書之而無隱，藏否之實跡必紀之而無遺。其也令儀令色，有德之孔嘉；其也載號載呶，伐德之可恥。一載筆之頃，俾肅然知所戒也。夫以一燕飲之間，而防範之嚴有如此，武公其善於悔過而果於進德者歟！抑論飲酒，細事，而聖狂分焉。書曰：「不矜細行，終累大德。」又曰：「惟公懋德，克勤小物。」其以此歟！武公深知乎此，故荒湛于酒，既陳於自警之篇；飲酒悔過，又形於賓筵之雅。殆與大禹之所惡、周公之所誥者，異世而同符也。衛之賢君，武公稱首焉。

春秋
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子，同盟于幽。〔莊公十六年〕
穆世傑
考試官學正張，批〔得春秋家法〕
考試官教授方，批〔胡傳兩言齊桓始霸之意，作〕者多拙於穀梁尊周一偏之說，殊失本旨。此卷獨□
translation_en:
…to observe their deportment, ensuring that the circumstances of their drunkenness or sobriety were recorded without concealment, and that the actual evidence of good or bad conduct [?] was documented without omission. Those displaying fine deportment and a gracious countenance were greatly to be praised for their virtue; those shouting and clamoring were to be shamed for damaging their virtue. In the brief moment of taking up the writing brush, he made them solemnly aware of what they must guard against. When precautions at even a single drinking banquet were so strict, was not Duke Wu adept at repenting his faults and resolute in advancing his virtue?

Furthermore, drinking wine is a minor affair, yet therein lies the distinction between sagehood and madness. The Book of Documents says: “If you pay no heed to minor conduct, you will ultimately impair great virtue.” It also says: “You, my lord, must strive for virtue and attend diligently to small matters.” Surely this is what those words mean! Duke Wu understood this deeply. Thus, abandonment to wine was already set forth in his poem of self-admonition, while repentance for faults committed in drinking also found expression in the ode “When Guests First Take Their Seats.” His position accorded, across different ages, with what Yu the Great abhorred and what the Duke of Zhou warned against. Among the worthy rulers of Wei, Duke Wu ranks foremost.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“[The ruler of Lu] met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng; together they entered into a covenant at You.” 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Mu Shijie

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔“It grasps the interpretive tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.”〕

Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔“Hu’s Commentary twice speaks of the significance of Duke Huan of Qi’s initial attainment of hegemony. Writ-〕ers often clumsily follow the one-sided explanation in the Guliang Commentary concerning honoring Zhou, badly missing the original purport. This paper alone □…”

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
真切而文足以發揮其蘊於經學者歟
霸主仗義以講信春秋諱望國失信之非著諸
侯同欲之美此齊桓于幽之盟諸侯皆同而魯
獨異焉春秋一惡之一美之無非為世道計歟
何則春秋中葉王政不綱列國兵爭人心無統
幸而齊桓始霸倡盟于幽肇糾合之洪圖講尊
王之大義夷狄以之而攘中國以之而安桓公
是盟其義舉也我魯莊公中國人望使能堅守
桓信以成其美不亦賢乎柰何雖聽載書實懷
===
疑貳卒之鄭詹一受大義虧矣如同盟之信何
聖人以為生有可捐食有可去而信則不可無
者況桓霸仗義之信而我莊失之是豈知所重
哉故春秋諱公不書以惡其失信蓋如此維時
宋陳七國俱齊友邦使亦猶豫桓信以僨乃事
奚足取耶所幸尊事同心推戴無異卒致桓霸
一匡厥功懋矣非同盟之力歟聖人以為上無
明王下無方伯而霸亦不可無者況齊桓霸事
之美而諸侯與之非所欲之善哉故春秋特書
punctuated:
真切，而文足以發揮其蘊，於經學者歟？

霸主仗義以講信，春秋諱望國失信之非，著諸侯同欲之美。此齊桓于幽之盟，諸侯皆同，而魯獨異焉。春秋一惡之，一美之，無非為世道計歟？何則？春秋中葉，王政不綱，列國兵爭，人心無統。幸而齊桓始霸，倡盟于幽，肇糾合之洪圖，講尊王之大義。夷狄以之而攘，中國以之而安。桓公是盟，其義舉也。我魯莊公，中國人望，使能堅守桓信，以成其美，不亦賢乎？柰何雖聽載書，實懷疑貳，卒之鄭詹一受，大義虧矣。如同盟之信何？聖人以為生有可捐，食有可去，而信則不可無者。況桓霸仗義之信，而我莊失之，是豈知所重哉？故春秋諱公不書，以惡其失信，蓋如此。維時宋陳七國，俱齊友邦，使亦猶豫桓信，以僨乃事，奚足取耶？所幸尊事同心，推戴無異，卒致桓霸一匡，厥功懋矣，非同盟之力歟？聖人以為上無明王，下無方伯，而霸亦不可無者。況齊桓霸事之美，而諸侯與之，非所欲之善哉？故春秋特書
translation_en:
…is incisive and true, and its prose adequately brings out the meaning implicit within it. Is the writer a student versed in the Classics [?]?

The hegemon upheld righteousness to establish good faith. The Spring and Autumn Annals conceals the fault of a leading state's breach of faith and makes manifest the merit of the feudal lords' shared purpose. At this covenant concluded by Duke Huan of Qi at You, the feudal lords were all united, while Lu alone differed. In condemning the one and praising the others, was the Spring and Autumn Annals not concerned throughout with the moral order of the world?

Why is this so? In the middle years of the Spring and Autumn period, royal government no longer maintained order; the various states fought one another, and the people's allegiances had no common focus. Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi began to establish his hegemony and called for a covenant at You. He initiated the grand undertaking of bringing the lords together and expounded the great principle of honoring the king. Through this, the Yi and Di peoples were repelled and the central states secured. This covenant of Duke Huan's was a righteous undertaking. Duke Zhuang of our state of Lu was a man to whom the central states looked. Had he steadfastly kept faith with Duke Huan and thereby brought this worthy undertaking to fruition, would he not have been admirable? Yet, although he heard the covenant document, he actually harbored doubts and divided loyalties. In the end, once he received Zheng Zhan, the great principle was compromised. What then became of the good faith pledged in their common covenant?

The Sage held that life could be sacrificed and food dispensed with, but good faith could never be lacking. All the more so when the good faith sustaining Duke Huan's hegemony rested upon righteousness, yet our Duke Zhuang violated it: how could he be said to understand what mattered most? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals conceals the duke's participation by omitting him from the record, thereby condemning his breach of faith. Such was its reasoning.

At that time, the seven states, including Song and Chen, were all friendly states of Qi. Had they too wavered in their faith in Duke Huan and thereby ruined that undertaking, what would there have been to commend? Fortunately, they were of one mind in honoring and serving him, and undivided in supporting his leadership. They ultimately enabled Duke Huan, as hegemon, to set the realm in order. His achievement was great indeed: was this not the power of their common covenant? The Sage held that, when there was no enlightened king above and no regional chief below, a hegemon could not be dispensed with. All the more so when Duke Huan of Qi's hegemonic undertaking was worthy, and the feudal lords supported it: was the purpose they shared not good? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同盟以美其同欲又如此可聖人於一盟事之
間所以惡魯公而美諸侯者蓋以齊桓始霸世
道攸繫雖拳拳以與之可也抑考盟幽之後自貫
澤迄于葵丘桓業可謂盛矣惜乎震矜一萌叛
者九國伐黃會卞皆不足道故曰五霸假之也
若夫勝夏而罪予一人湯之所以無荒也克商
而大賚四海武之所以不息也量淺志溢之桓
公安足與語此
宋公曹伯衛人邾人伐齊　師救齊　宋
師及齊師戰于甗齊師敗績　狄救齊
僖公十八年
===
蹇賢
考試官學正張　批〔知褒貶〕
考試官教授方　批〔題雖一事而伐戰兩役作者〕〔多體認不明此作融會傳意得於章句之法且抑揚〕〔開闔如斷案然春秋家數也允宜鶚薦〕
春秋因大國兵起於不義善內救以著其罪責
大國兵成於不義許外救以甚其罪蓋長幼之
punctuated:
同盟，以美其同欲，又如此。可聖人於一盟事之間，所以惡魯公而美諸侯者，蓋以齊桓始霸，世道攸繫，雖拳拳以與之，可也。抑考盟幽之後，自貫澤迄于葵丘，桓業可謂盛矣。惜乎震矜一萌，叛者九國，伐黃、會卞，皆不足道。故曰：「五霸假之也。」若夫勝夏而罪予一人，湯之所以無荒也；克商而大賚四海，武之所以不息也。量淺志溢之桓公，安足與語此？
宋公、曹伯、衛人、邾人伐齊。師救齊。宋師及齊師戰于甗，齊師敗績。狄救齊。
僖公十八年。
蹇賢。
考試官學正張，批〔知褒貶〕。
考試官教授方，批〔題雖一事而伐戰兩役作者〕〔多體認不明此作融會傳意得於章句之法且抑揚〕〔開闔如斷案然春秋家數也允宜鶚薦〕。
春秋因大國兵起於不義，善內救以著其罪；責大國兵成於不義，許外救以甚其罪。蓋長幼之
translation_en:
…“covenanted together,” thereby praising their shared purpose: this, too, is how it does so. The opening connective is doubtful [?]. The Sage’s condemnation of the lord of Lu and praise of the other feudal lords within the account of a single covenant were surely because Duke Huan of Qi was beginning his hegemony, upon which the course of the age depended. Even wholehearted support for him was therefore appropriate. Yet if we examine what followed the covenant at You, from Guanze to Kuiqiu, Huan’s achievements may indeed be called flourishing. Sadly, once arrogance began to stir, nine states rebelled; the attack on Huang and the meeting at Bian were scarcely worth speaking of. Thus it is said: “The Five Hegemons borrowed it.” By contrast, after defeating Xia, Tang declared that any guilt rested with “me alone”: this was how he avoided negligence. After conquering Shang, King Wu bestowed great gifts throughout the realm: this was how he remained unceasing in his efforts. How could Duke Huan, with his narrow capacity and overflowing ambition, merit discussion alongside them?
The duke of Song, the earl of Cao, men of Wei, and men of Zhu attacked Qi. Our army came to Qi’s aid. The army of Song fought the army of Qi at Yan; the army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. The Di came to Qi’s aid.
Eighteenth year of Duke Xi.
Jian Xian.
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Understands praise and blame.〕
Examiner Fang, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔Although the topic concerns a single affair, the invasion and the battle were two distinct military operations. Writers〕〔often fail to grasp this clearly. This composition integrates the meaning of the commentaries and masters the method of interpreting textual divisions and sentences. Moreover, its modulation of emphasis〕〔and its unfolding and closing of the argument resemble the adjudication of a case: this is the proper manner of a specialist in the Spring and Autumn Annals. It assuredly merits recommendation as an outstanding talent.〕
Because a great state’s military action began in unrighteousness, the Spring and Autumn Annals commends the aid given from within our state to make that great state’s guilt manifest. It censures the great state for bringing its military action to completion in unrighteousness, and approves the aid given from outside the Chinese states to underscore its guilt further. For the principle governing senior and junior…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
義不可廢也宋襄睹此而奉少奪長于齊春秋
得不詳書法以深罪之哉慨昔齊桓不祿國嗣
未立於是宋襄伐齊戰甗亦為之圖其後嗣以
安定其國家也春秋深罪之何歟盖無虧長子
孝公幼支使宋襄正名定分則為義兵之舉也
夫何首摟三國忍伐齊喪廢無虧之正納孝公
之逆借曰舍長立幼桓仲之命然制命非義邪
正不分宋罪大矣遂致東魯之救何善惡之相
遠邪故於四國伐齊之下特善魯師之救以著
===
宋襄之罪也然無虧雖爾就戮孝公尚未即君
使宋襄悔過息師則無怙終之刑也夫何復帥
三軍鬨戰甗地力敗齊師之衆卒定逆孝之位
雖曰泝北不支齊臣之罪然大義不明戰鬭是
逞宋曲甚矣再致北狄之救何夷狄之不若邪
故於罪宋及戰之下責齊敗績以見宋襄之曲
許狄救齊以甚宋襄之罪也吁聖人於一書法
之間責宋之詳如此盖奉少奪長於罪為大不
得不明大義以深罪之耳嗟夫黜宜臼以召犬
punctuated: 義不可廢也。宋襄睹此而奉少奪長于齊，春秋得不詳書法以深罪之哉？慨昔齊桓不祿，國嗣未立，於是宋襄伐齊、戰甗，亦為之圖其後嗣，以安定其國家也。春秋深罪之何歟？盖無虧長子，孝公幼支，使宋襄正名定分，則為義兵之舉也。夫何首摟三國，忍伐齊喪，廢無虧之正，納孝公之逆？借曰舍長立幼，桓仲之命，然制命非義，邪正不分，宋罪大矣！遂致東魯之救，何善惡之相遠邪？故於四國伐齊之下，特善魯師之救，以著宋襄之罪也。然無虧雖爾就戮，孝公尚未即君，使宋襄悔過息師，則無怙終之刑也。夫何復帥三軍，鬨戰甗地，力敗齊師之衆，卒定逆孝之位？雖曰泝北不支，齊臣之罪，然大義不明，戰鬭是逞，宋曲甚矣！再致北狄之救，何夷狄之不若邪？故於罪宋及戰之下，責齊敗績，以見宋襄之曲；許狄救齊，以甚宋襄之罪也。吁！聖人於一書法之間，責宋之詳如此，盖奉少奪長，於罪為大，不得不明大義以深罪之耳。嗟夫！黜宜臼以召犬
translation_en:
…the proper ordering of elder and younger must not be abandoned. Duke Xiang of Song saw this, yet supported the younger and deprived the elder in Qi. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to employ precise wording to condemn him severely? Alas, when Duke Huan of Qi died and the succession remained unsettled, Duke Xiang of Song attacked Qi and fought at Yan, likewise intending to arrange its succession and stabilize its state. Why, then, do the Spring and Autumn Annals condemn him so severely? Wukui was the eldest son, while Duke Xiao belonged to a younger branch. Had Duke Xiang rectified their designations and settled their respective standing, his campaign would have been a righteous undertaking. Why, instead, did he take the lead in drawing three states into an alliance, have the heart to attack Qi during its mourning, displace Wukui despite his rightful claim, and install Duke Xiao against the proper order? Even granting that setting aside the elder and installing the younger followed the instructions of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong, those instructions were unrighteous. Failing to distinguish wrong from right, Song incurred great guilt! This consequently brought aid from Lu in the east. How far apart were their good and evil deeds! Thus, after recording the four states’ attack on Qi, the Annals especially commend the rescue by Lu’s army, thereby exposing Duke Xiang’s guilt.

Yet although Wukui had thus been killed, Duke Xiao had still not assumed the rulership. Had Duke Xiang repented of his error and withdrawn his army, he would not have incurred punishment for persisting in wrongdoing to the end. Why, instead, did he again lead the three armies into clamorous battle at Yan, forcibly defeat the host of Qi’s troops, and finally secure the throne for Xiao, whose accession violated the proper order? Even if the rout and inability to hold out [?] were the fault of Qi’s ministers, Song failed to make the great moral principle clear and indulged only in warfare. Song was profoundly in the wrong! This brought yet another rescue, this time by the northern Di. How could he fall below even the Yi and Di peoples? Thus, after censuring Song in the wording recording its engagement in battle, the Annals reproach Qi for its crushing defeat, thereby revealing Duke Xiang’s wrongdoing; they approve the Di’s rescue of Qi, thereby intensifying Duke Xiang’s condemnation.

Ah! Such is the precision with which the Sage censures Song through the wording of a single record. Supporting the younger and depriving the elder is a grave offense: he therefore had to make the great moral principle clear and condemn it severely. Alas! Deposing Yijiu and thereby summoning the Quan…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
戎者周幽也廢魯桓以禍懿公者宣王也黜牟
蒙刃寵孽朔也奚齊授首易申生也桓公君臣
顚不鑒此乃欲以私愛紊長幼之節哉是則齊
國爭亂非特宋襄之罪實桓公啓之也春秋謹
嚴於此正倫之意豈過乎嗚呼以此為防猶有
欲立幼庶以釀人彘之變如漢髙之於趙王如
意者
禮記
司寇正刑明辟以聽獄訟
焦思明
同考試官訓導何　批〔場中講刑辟處多混此作體認明白非深於禮者不能也錄之〕
考試官學正張　批〔文得三易法〕
考試官教授方　批〔講結俱整〕
大臣謹治天下之法以平天下之情焉蓋刑與
辟治法之大者也大臣之司法者得不正之明
之以為聽獄訟計哉王制記此謂夫司寇詰邦
禁之官而刑辟其所司之事司寇欲聽人之獄
punctuated:
戎者，周幽也；廢魯桓以禍懿公者，宣王也。黜牟蒙刃，寵孽朔也；奚齊授首，易申生也。桓公君臣顚不鑒此，乃欲以私愛紊長幼之節哉？是則齊國爭亂，非特宋襄之罪，實桓公啓之也。《春秋》謹嚴於此，正倫之意豈過乎？嗚呼！以此為防，猶有欲立幼庶以釀人彘之變，如漢髙之於趙王如意者。
《禮記》
司寇正刑明辟以聽獄訟。
焦思明
同考試官訓導何，批〔場中講刑辟處多混，此作體認明白，非深於禮者不能也，錄之。〕
考試官學正張，批〔文得三易法。〕
考試官教授方，批〔講結俱整。〕
大臣謹治天下之法，以平天下之情焉。蓋刑與辟，治法之大者也。大臣之司法者，得不正之明之，以為聽獄訟計哉？《王制》記此，謂夫司寇，詰邦禁之官，而刑辟，其所司之事。司寇欲聽人之獄
translation_en:
…the Rong: it was King You of Zhou who summoned them. It was King Xuan who displaced Huan of Lu and thereby brought disaster upon Duke Yi [?]. Mou was displaced and met the blade because favor was bestowed upon the concubine-born Shuo [?]; Xiqi lost his head because Shen Sheng had been replaced. Did Duke Huan and his ministers fail to take warning from these events [?], and actually seek to let private affection disrupt the proper order between elder and younger? Thus the struggles and disorder in Qi were not solely the fault of Duke Xiang of Song: Duke Huan had in fact initiated them. Can the meticulous rigor of the Spring and Autumn Annals on this point, intended to rectify human relationships, be considered excessive? Alas! Even with this warning, there were still those who wished to install a younger, concubine-born son, thereby brewing a calamity like that of the “human swine”—as when Emperor Gao of Han favored Ruyi, King of Zhao.

Record of Rites
“The Minister of Justice rectifies punishments and clarifies the laws in order to hear criminal cases and civil suits.”

Jiao Siming

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Many examination essays confuse the discussion of punishments and laws. This composition understands their distinction clearly; only someone deeply versed in ritual could achieve this. Selected for inclusion.〕

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The composition achieves the method of the “three eases” [?].〕

Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition and conclusion are both well ordered.〕

A high minister carefully administers the laws of the realm so as to deal equitably with the circumstances of its people. Punishments and laws are major elements of the methods of government. How could a high minister responsible for administering justice fail to rectify the former and clarify the latter, in preparation for hearing criminal cases and civil suits? The “Royal Regulations” records this, meaning that the Minister of Justice is the official charged with enforcing the state's prohibitions, and punishments and laws are the matters under his jurisdiction. If the Minister of Justice wishes to hear people's criminal cases …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
訟可不先有以謹其刑辟乎是故刑有五而我
五用之或不能以皆平也則從而正之使其曰
墨劓曰剕宮以及大辟之類一皆大中至正而
枉撓無容於纖悉辟有八而我八議之或不能
以皆當也則從而明之使其曰親故曰賢能以
及功貴勤賓之屬一皆鑑空燭照而疑貳不蓄
之毫芒司寇正刑明辟如此豈他為哉盖民情
不能無訟也訟不決而繫於囹圄則為獄今則
以刑辟而聽其獄焉不能無爭也爭靡定而言
===
於公則為訟今則以刑辟而聽其訟焉悉聰明
於辭色之間于以察其孰可居墨劓孰可居剕
宮又孰可居大辟而上附下附之不失其情致
忠愛於言意之表于以審其何者當議之親故
何者當議之賢能又何者當議之勤賓功貴而
一輕一重之皆麗於事夫如是則刑無不當辟
無不宜在野無嗟怨之聲而在獄無寃抑之嘆
矣司寇之職庶其盡矣乎抑論刑之所係重矣
死者不可復生斷者不可復屬先王不得已之
punctuated:
訟，可不先有以謹其刑辟乎？是故刑有五，而我五用之，或不能以皆平也，則從而正之，使其曰墨劓、曰剕宮，以及大辟之類，一皆大中至正，而枉撓無容於纖悉。辟有八，而我八議之，或不能以皆當也，則從而明之，使其曰親故、曰賢能，以及功貴勤賓之屬，一皆鑑空燭照，而疑貳不蓄之毫芒。司寇正刑明辟如此，豈他為哉？盖民情不能無訟也，訟不決而繫於囹圄，則為獄，今則以刑辟而聽其獄焉；不能無爭也，爭靡定而言於公，則為訟，今則以刑辟而聽其訟焉。悉聰明於辭色之間，于以察其孰可居墨劓，孰可居剕宮，又孰可居大辟，而上附下附之不失其情；致忠愛於言意之表，于以審其何者當議之親故，何者當議之賢能，又何者當議之勤賓功貴，而一輕一重之皆麗於事。夫如是，則刑無不當，辟無不宜，在野無嗟怨之聲，而在獄無寃抑之嘆矣。司寇之職，庶其盡矣乎？

抑論刑之所係，重矣！死者不可復生，斷者不可復屬，先王不得已之
translation_en:
…litigation, can he fail first to exercise care over punishments and their legal application? Thus there are five punishments, and when we employ all five, we may not manage to apply them all equitably. We must therefore rectify them, ensuring that tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputation of the feet, castration, and the death penalty all accord fully with the proper mean and utmost justice, admitting not the slightest distortion or deviation. There are eight categories for special deliberation in applying the law, and when we deliberate on all eight, we may not manage to reach an appropriate decision in every case. We must therefore clarify them, ensuring that the categories of imperial relatives, old associates, the worthy, the capable, those of meritorious service, those of high rank, the diligent in service, and honored guests are all examined with the clarity of an unobstructed mirror and the illumination of a lamp, leaving not the slightest doubt or uncertainty. When the Minister of Justice thus rectifies punishments and clarifies their legal application, could he have any other purpose?

For disputes inevitably arise among the people. When a dispute remains unresolved and someone is confined in prison, it becomes a criminal case; such cases are now heard according to the punishments and the law. Contention, too, is inevitable. When contention remains unsettled and is brought before the authorities, it becomes litigation; such litigation is now heard according to the punishments and the law. Bringing the full powers of hearing and sight to bear upon words and facial expressions, he determines who should be subject to tattooing or cutting off the nose, who to amputation of the feet or castration, and who to death. In assigning a case to a more or less severe category by analogy, he does not lose sight of its actual circumstances. Extending his loyal concern and compassion beyond the surface of words and intentions, he carefully determines which cases call for deliberation on the grounds of imperial kinship or old association, which on the grounds of worthiness or ability, and which on the grounds of diligent service, honored guest status, merit, or high rank. Every mitigation or increase in severity thus accords with the facts of the case. If this is done, no punishment will be inappropriate and no application of the law unfitting. Among the people there will be no sounds of lamentation and resentment, and in the prisons no sighs over injustice and oppression. Might the Minister of Justice then be said to have fully discharged his duties?

Yet consider how weighty are the consequences of punishment! The dead cannot be brought back to life, and severed limbs cannot be reattached. For the former kings, this was something they had no alternative but to…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
用也故有三刺三宥八議五聲以至附從輕赦
從重欽恤之仁無往不在柰何後世慘刻之徒
有著法經者有為連坐者有請峻刑罰者緩深
故之罪急縱出之誅而刑益壞矣作詢刑之法
開密告之門而法益敝矣先王之良意安在哉
噫爰制百姓于刑之衷司刑者尚當加之意焉
故聽其雅頌之聲志意得廣焉執其干戚
習其俯仰詘伸容貌得莊焉行其綴兆
要其節奏行列得正焉進退得齊焉
===
楊天錫
同考試官訓導何　批〔題本正大而詞不均此作獨能鋪叙無偏一結尤備是宜錄出以為讀樂者式〕
考試官學正張　批〔雅贍而和學禮者之言也〕
考試官教授方　批〔說出樂有益於人本意可佳〕
聞正樂之聲有以攝其心習正樂之容有以檢
其身夫正樂有聲有容本為世教作也在人聞
之習之豈不有補於身心哉今夫先王之樂聲
莫先於雅頌容莫先於干戚其要皆歸於感動
punctuated:
用也。故有三刺、三宥、八議、五聲，以至附從輕、赦從重，欽恤之仁無往不在。柰何後世慘刻之徒，有著《法經》者，有為連坐者，有請峻刑罰者，緩深故之罪，急縱出之誅，而刑益壞矣；作詢刑之法，開密告之門，而法益敝矣。先王之良意安在哉？噫！爰制百姓于刑之衷，司刑者尚當加之意焉。

故聽其雅頌之聲，志意得廣焉；執其干戚，習其俯仰詘伸，容貌得莊焉；行其綴兆，要其節奏，行列得正焉，進退得齊焉。

楊天錫

同考試官訓導何，批〔題本正大而詞不均，此作獨能鋪叙無偏，一結尤備，是宜錄出，以為讀樂者式。〕
考試官學正張，批〔雅贍而和，學禮者之言也。〕
考試官教授方，批〔說出樂有益於人本意，可佳。〕

聞正樂之聲，有以攝其心；習正樂之容，有以檢其身。夫正樂有聲有容，本為世教作也。在人聞之習之，豈不有補於身心哉？今夫先王之樂，聲莫先於雅頌，容莫先於干戚，其要皆歸於感動
translation_en:
…a measure they employed only out of necessity. Thus there were the three consultations, the three grounds for pardon, the eight deliberations, and the five ways of assessing testimony. Even in assigning an offense to a category, the lighter penalty was followed, while pardons extended to graver offenses. The benevolence of reverent care and compassion was present throughout. Why, then, did cruel men of later ages compile the Canon of Laws (Fajing), institute collective liability, or petition for harsher punishments? They treated deliberate imposition of excessive sentences leniently, but urgently punished those who let offenders go; thus punishment became ever more corrupted. They devised methods of penal interrogation [?] and opened the way to secret denunciations; thus the law became ever more debased. Where was the good intent of the former kings? Alas! To regulate the common people through a fitting mean in punishment—those in charge of punishments should give this their earnest attention.

“Thus, when they hear the sounds of the Elegantiae and Eulogies, their aspirations are broadened. When they hold shields and battle-axes and practice bowing and rising, bending and stretching, their bearing becomes dignified. When they move through the marked dance positions and conform to the rhythms, their ranks become correct, and their advances and retreats become coordinated.”

Yang Tianxi

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is fundamentally upright and grand, but its wording is uneven. This composition alone develops it without imbalance; its conclusion is especially comprehensive. It should therefore be selected for inclusion as a model for those studying music.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Elegant, ample, and harmonious: these are the words of one who studies ritual.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔It brings out the underlying meaning that music benefits people. Commendable.〕

Hearing the sounds of proper music serves to collect the mind; practicing the movements of proper music serves to discipline the body. Proper music has both sound and movement and was originally created to instruct the world. When people hear it and practice it, how could it fail to benefit body and mind? Now, in the music of the former kings, no sounds take precedence over the Elegantiae and Eulogies, and no movements take precedence over those performed with shields and battle-axes. Their essential purpose lies entirely in stirring…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人之善心而已故以其聲而言之則雅所以陳
王政之大小而頌所以美盛德之形容也是聲
也文足論而不息聲足樂而不流父子兄弟而
聽焉則能蕩滌其邪穢和親之心油然生於中
志意以之而充廣也君臣上下而聽焉則能消
融其查滓和敬之心藹然發於中志意以之而
舒暢也所謂閳正樂之聲有以攄其心者蓋如
此以其容而言之干者直兵而其形欲立戚者
勾兵而其形欲倒者也是器也俯仰詘伸各有
===
其度綴兆節奏各有其儀故執其干戚而習俯
仰以為容詘伸以為舞則肅然於心而不過越
其度矣容貌不於是而得莊乎行其綴兆之位
要其節奏之數則惕然於心而不雜亂其儀矣
行列進退不於是而得正且齊乎所謂習正樂
之容有以檢其身者蓋如此雖然禮樂二道不
可相離樂非禮則一於和禮非樂則一於嚴有
偏廢之弊無相濟之功甚非先王制作之良意
□故記者既言樂之和禮復言禮之節樂意其
punctuated: 人之善心而已。故以其聲而言之，則雅所以陳王政之大小，而頌所以美盛德之形容也。是聲也，文足論而不息，聲足樂而不流。父子兄弟而聽焉，則能蕩滌其邪穢，和親之心油然生於中，志意以之而充廣也；君臣上下而聽焉，則能消融其查滓，和敬之心藹然發於中，志意以之而舒暢也。所謂閳正樂之聲有以攄其心者，蓋如此。以其容而言之，干者直兵而其形欲立，戚者勾兵而其形欲倒者也。是器也，俯仰詘伸各有其度，綴兆節奏各有其儀。故執其干戚而習俯仰以為容，詘伸以為舞，則肅然於心而不過越其度矣。容貌不於是而得莊乎？行其綴兆之位，要其節奏之數，則惕然於心而不雜亂其儀矣。行列進退不於是而得正且齊乎？所謂習正樂之容有以檢其身者，蓋如此。雖然，禮樂二道不可相離。樂非禮則一於和，禮非樂則一於嚴，有偏廢之弊，無相濟之功，甚非先王制作之良意□。故記者既言樂之和禮，復言禮之節樂，意其
translation_en:
…people’s good hearts, and nothing more. Thus, speaking of its sounds, the Odes of the Court set forth the greater and lesser matters of royal government, while the Hymns praise the manifestations of abundant virtue. In this music, the words afford inexhaustible material for discussion, and the sounds afford pleasure without dissoluteness. When fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers listen to it, it can wash away their depravity and impurity. Feelings of harmony and affection arise spontaneously within them, and their aspirations thereby grow fuller and broader. When rulers and ministers, superiors and subordinates listen to it, it can dissolve their dross. Feelings of harmony and respect well up within them, and their aspirations thereby become free and expansive. Such, in general, is what is meant by saying that hearing [?] the sounds of correct music serves to give expression to the heart.

Speaking of its movements, the shield is a straight weapon whose form calls for it to stand upright, while the axe is a hooked weapon whose form calls for it to tilt downward [?]. In using these implements, bowing and raising the head, bending and extending the limbs each have their prescribed measure; the positions marked out for the dancers and the rhythmic sequences each have their prescribed form. Thus, when dancers hold their shields and axes and practice bowing and raising the head as movements, and bending and extending the limbs as dance, they become reverent in heart and do not exceed the prescribed measure. Does their bearing not thereby acquire dignity? When they move through their designated positions and conform to the counts of the rhythmic sequences, they become vigilant in heart and do not confuse the prescribed forms. Do their ranks and their advances and retreats not thereby become correct and orderly? Such, in general, is what is meant by saying that practicing the movements of correct music serves to discipline the person.

Nevertheless, the two ways of ritual and music cannot be separated. Music without ritual tends exclusively toward harmony; ritual without music tends exclusively toward strictness. This brings the harm of neglecting one side, without the benefit of their mutual assistance, and is far from the good intentions with which the former kings established them [illegible character]. Thus, after speaking of how music harmonizes ritual, the author of the Record also speaks of how ritual regulates music. His intention, presumably …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有攸在哉而孔子亦曰禮之用和為貴儒先亦
曰聖人履中正而樂和平又曰等級至嚴也失
禮樂則不威山河至險也失禮樂則不固是禮
樂之益於人益於事益於造化也以其有相濟
之妙也歟
第貳場
論
主敬便是為善
胡鎰
===
同考試官教諭吳　批程子言主敬於雞鳴而起之
時蓋以一心收斂而言所謂為善亦言敬則非僻不干
而天理常存耳作者類皆掇拾浮泛動輒數千言而
不知敬為何等工夫善為何等氣象又有以敬為靜者
然此時雖未接物固已屬之動矣晚得此卷起語數句
便已中的而通篇無一言冗長非嘗究心理學者不能
以是進焉雖聖賢真可學而至科場一第之先不足為
子多也
考試官學正張　批說得敬善是如此
punctuated:
有攸在哉！而孔子亦曰：「禮之用，和為貴。」儒先亦曰：「聖人履中正而樂和平。」又曰：「等級至嚴也，失禮樂則不威；山河至險也，失禮樂則不固。」是禮樂之益於人、益於事、益於造化也，以其有相濟之妙也歟！
第貳場
論
主敬便是為善
胡鎰
同考試官教諭吳批：程子言主敬於雞鳴而起之時，蓋以一心收斂而言。所謂為善，亦言敬則非僻不干，而天理常存耳。作者類皆掇拾浮泛，動輒數千言，而不知敬為何等工夫，善為何等氣象。又有以敬為靜者，然此時雖未接物，固已屬之動矣。晚得此卷，起語數句便已中的，而通篇無一言冗長，非嘗究心理學者不能。以是進焉，雖聖賢，真可學而至。科場一第之先，不足為子多也。
考試官學正張批：說得敬善，是如此。
translation_en:
…surely has a purpose! Confucius also said: “In the practice of ritual, harmony is prized.” An earlier Confucian master likewise said: “The sage abides in centrality and correctness and delights in harmony and peace.” He also said: “The distinctions of rank are supremely strict, yet without ritual and music they command no awe; mountains and rivers are supremely formidable barriers, yet without ritual and music they afford no security.” That ritual and music benefit people, affairs, and the processes of creation—is this not because of the marvelous way they complement each other?

Second Session
Discourse
“Maintaining Reverent Attentiveness Is Precisely Doing Good”
Hu Yi 胡鎰

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor:
Master Cheng spoke of maintaining reverent attentiveness when rising at cockcrow, meaning that the whole mind is gathered inward. What he called doing good likewise means simply that, through reverent attentiveness, perversity cannot intrude and Heaven’s principle remains constantly present. Nearly all the writers have pieced together superficial generalities, readily running to several thousand words, without knowing what kind of effort reverent attentiveness entails or what character goodness displays. Some also identify reverent attentiveness with stillness. Yet at this moment, although one has not yet engaged with external things, one has certainly already entered the sphere of activity. Late in the process I came upon this script. Its first few sentences already hit the mark, and throughout the piece there is not a single word of needless elaboration. Someone who had not devoted thought to the Learning of Principle could not have achieved this. Advance on this basis, and even sagehood and worthiness can truly be attained through learning. Taking first place in an examination is insufficient to do you full credit.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor:
He has explained reverent attentiveness and goodness correctly: this is how they are.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭方　批〔此題正欲觀諸士子用心於〕
〔内之學連日閱卷許多者枝辭蔓語寫盡幅不了卒〕
〔不省其為何說其務實者又往往筆端艱澁數言而〕
〔止獨此篇以時文格調檃栝自家道理取以魁多士夫〕
〔豈幸耶〕
論曰為善於未接物之時無他亦惟存此
心而不放焉爾蓋善雖散在萬事而其本
具於吾之一心心存則欲不萌而理無壞
之者何往而不善若以鷄鳴而起無所事
事而不知有事於吾心則身在此而心在
彼身不出戶庭而心千里其奔心既不存
何往而非不善此敬所以為存心之要而
主於敬所以使存者益堅而不放則為善
也豈有外於是哉且人何以有是善也天
===
之道也又何以有是敬也人之道也人道
之敬也柰何性之有禮也存於心則為敬
心之所存為敬而敬又能存是心也以一
日言之自朝至暮敬不可去也以日日言
punctuated:
考試官教諭方批〔此題正欲觀諸士子用心於〕〔内之學。連日閱卷，許多者枝辭蔓語，寫盡幅不了，卒〕〔不省其為何說。其務實者，又往往筆端艱澁，數言而〕〔止。獨此篇以時文格調檃栝自家道理，取以魁多士，夫〕〔豈幸耶？〕

論曰：為善於未接物之時，無他，亦惟存此心而不放焉爾。蓋善雖散在萬事，而其本具於吾之一心。心存則欲不萌，而理無壞之者，何往而不善？若以鷄鳴而起，無所事事，而不知有事於吾心，則身在此而心在彼，身不出戶庭而心千里其奔。心既不存，何往而非不善？此敬所以為存心之要，而主於敬所以使存者益堅而不放，則為善也，豈有外於是哉？且人何以有是善也？天之道也。又何以有是敬也？人之道也。人道之敬也，柰何？性之有禮也，存於心則為敬。心之所存為敬，而敬又能存是心也。以一日言之，自朝至暮，敬不可去也。以日日言
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: 〔This topic was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ dedication to inward learning. In the examination papers I have read over successive days, many candidates pile up rambling phrases, filling the entire sheet without reaching a conclusion; in the end, one cannot understand what they mean to say. Those who pursue substance, meanwhile, often write so awkwardly that they stop after only a few words. This essay alone uses the form and cadence of contemporary examination prose to express the writer’s own understanding of the principles. Could its selection to head the candidates possibly have been mere luck?〕

The discourse states: To practice goodness before engaging with external things requires nothing else than preserving this mind and not letting it stray. Although goodness is dispersed throughout the myriad affairs, its root is fully present within our own single mind. When the mind is preserved, desires do not arise and nothing impairs principle: wherever one turns, how could one fail to be good? But if one rises at cockcrow and has nothing to attend to, unaware that there is work to do upon one’s own mind, then the body is here while the mind is elsewhere. The body does not leave the doorway or courtyard, yet the mind races a thousand li away. Once the mind is no longer preserved, wherever one turns, how could one avoid what is not good? This is why reverent attentiveness is essential to preserving the mind, and why making it one’s governing concern renders that preservation ever firmer and prevents the mind from straying. Could practicing goodness, then, lie anywhere outside this?

Moreover, how do human beings possess this goodness? It is the Way of Heaven. And how do they possess this reverent attentiveness? It is the human Way. How is reverent attentiveness part of the human Way? [?] Human nature possesses ritual propriety; preserved within the mind, this becomes reverent attentiveness. What the mind preserves is reverent attentiveness, and reverent attentiveness in turn can preserve this mind. Speaking of a single day, from morning until evening, reverent attentiveness must never be abandoned. Speaking of day after day …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之自少而壯壯而老老而一息之尚存敬
不可去也以一事言之徹頭徹尾敬不可
去也以事事言之無小無大敬不可去也
天道之善也柰何天地之大德曰生孔子
於化育之功而稱之曰善言其純粹而無
惡也天有是善故其所生之人於是善也
無所不具所生者必肖其所以生之者理
自然也君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友之道視
聽言動周旋食息之則皆善也夫敬雖本
===
於心而不可去然世多忽之人不能以皆
敬也故必以是為主焉主之云者在玆而
不舍之意也善雖得於天而莫不具惟聖
者全之人不能以皆善也故有待於為焉
為之云者脩治而復初之謂也是故鷄鳴
而起之時正屋漏獨處之地交於我者人
則無焉至乎前者物則無焉措於外者事
則無焉反而視吾之心固在也盖心動物
也或出入之無常而存亡之機係於是或
punctuated:
之，自少而壯，壯而老，老而一息之尚存，敬不可去也。以一事言之，徹頭徹尾，敬不可去也；以事事言之，無小無大，敬不可去也。天道之善也，柰何？天地之大德曰生。孔子於化育之功而稱之曰善，言其純粹而無惡也。天有是善，故其所生之人於是善也，無所不具。所生者必肖其所以生之者，理自然也。君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友之道，視聽言動、周旋食息之則，皆善也。

夫敬雖本於心而不可去，然世多忽之，人不能以皆敬也，故必以是為主焉。主之云者，在玆而不舍之意也。善雖得於天而莫不具，惟聖者全之，人不能以皆善也，故有待於為焉。為之云者，脩治而復初之謂也。是故鷄鳴而起之時，正屋漏獨處之地，交於我者，人則無焉；至乎前者，物則無焉；措於外者，事則無焉。反而視吾之心，固在也。盖心，動物也，或出入之無常，而存亡之機係於是；或
translation_en:
…from youth to maturity, from maturity to old age, and in old age while even a single breath remains, reverent attentiveness must never be relinquished. Speaking of a single undertaking, from beginning to end reverent attentiveness must never be relinquished; speaking of all undertakings, whether small or great, reverent attentiveness must never be relinquished. How is the Way of Heaven good? The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generating life. Confucius described the work of transformation and nurture as good, meaning that it is pure and wholly without evil. Heaven possesses this goodness; hence the human beings it brings forth possess this goodness in its entirety. That which is generated must resemble that which generates it: this follows naturally from principle. The ways governing ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends, and the standards governing seeing, hearing, speaking, acting, moving about, eating, and resting—all are good.

Although reverent attentiveness is rooted in the mind and must never be relinquished, people commonly neglect it. Since people cannot all remain reverently attentive, they must make it their guiding principle. To speak of making it one's guiding principle means remaining with it and never abandoning it. Although goodness is received from Heaven and everyone possesses it, only sages preserve it whole. Since people cannot all be good, goodness requires active cultivation. Such cultivation means putting oneself in order and returning to one's original state. Thus, when one rises at cockcrow, precisely in the secluded corner of the room where one is alone [?], there is no person interacting with oneself, no thing coming before one's eyes, and no affair being undertaken externally. Yet when I turn inward and examine my mind, it is certainly present. For the mind is something active: sometimes it goes out and comes in without constancy, and upon this hinges whether it is preserved or lost; or …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
彼此之無定而善惡之分judge於是必也正
其衣冠肅其容體端莊靜一凜乎神明之
在側整齊嚴肅儼然上帝之對越彼强者
猛以厲不足語敬吾必兢兢然不猛以厲
也愚者昏以冥不知有敬吾必惺惺然不
昏以冥也狂者倨以肆不屑於敬吾必收
斂焉不倨以肆也弱者頽以惰不能以敬
吾必喚醒焉不頽以惰也主一而無二三
之雜極尊而無内外之間如是則心管攝
===
乎血氣之軀而為一身之主宰者常存而
不放矣雖人未交於我物未至乎前事未
措於用反而視吾之善不壞也蓋善完物
也氣之決驟如奔駟善隨氣而失令敬以
為之銜轡矣情之横溢若潰川善隨情而
失令敬以為之隄防矣由是人欲之邪纖
退聽於萬事之外天理之純粹昭著於方
寸之中善之方萌於夜氣之所息者得長
養之功猶木之蘖而灌漑也善之原於民
punctuated: 彼此之無定，而善惡之分judge於是。必也正其衣冠，肅其容體，端莊靜一，凜乎神明之在側；整齊嚴肅，儼然上帝之對越。彼强者猛以厲，不足語敬，吾必兢兢然不猛以厲也；愚者昏以冥，不知有敬，吾必惺惺然不昏以冥也；狂者倨以肆，不屑於敬，吾必收斂焉不倨以肆也；弱者頽以惰，不能以敬，吾必喚醒焉不頽以惰也。主一而無二三之雜，極尊而無内外之間。如是，則心管攝乎血氣之軀，而為一身之主宰者，常存而不放矣。雖人未交於我，物未至乎前，事未措於用，反而視吾之善，不壞也。蓋善完物也。氣之決驟如奔駟，善隨氣而失，令敬以為之銜轡矣；情之横溢若潰川，善隨情而失，令敬以為之隄防矣。由是，人欲之邪纖退聽於萬事之外，天理之純粹昭著於方寸之中。善之方萌於夜氣之所息者，得長養之功，猶木之蘖而灌漑也；善之原於民
translation_en: …wavering between this and that, with the distinction between good and evil determined here [?]. One must straighten one’s robes and cap, compose one’s bearing, and remain dignified, still, and single-minded, in awe as though spirits stood beside one; orderly and solemn, one must be reverent as though facing the Lord on High. The forceful are fierce and harsh and cannot be said to possess reverence; I must remain watchful and cautious, without fierceness or harshness. The foolish are benighted and uncomprehending, unaware of reverence; I must remain alert, without such darkness of mind. The unrestrained are arrogant and presumptuous, disdaining reverence; I must collect myself, without arrogance or presumption. The weak are listless and idle, unable to maintain reverence; I must rouse myself, without listlessness or idleness. Concentrate on one thing, without the distraction of a second or third; maintain the utmost reverence, without any division between inner and outer. In this way, the mind, which governs the body of blood and vital energy and serves as master of the whole person, will remain constantly present and will not stray. Although people have not yet interacted with me, things have not yet come before me, and affairs have not yet called for action, when I turn inward to examine my goodness, it remains intact. For goodness is something whole. When vital energy rushes headlong like a team of four galloping horses, and goodness is lost in following it, let reverence serve as its bit and reins. When feelings overflow like a river bursting its banks, and goodness is lost in following them, let reverence serve as their dikes and embankments. Thus the petty perversities [?] of human desire withdraw submissively beyond all affairs, while the purity of Heaven’s principle shines forth within the heart. Goodness, just sprouting where the vital energy of the night has fostered it, receives nourishment and growth, like a tree’s new shoots being watered; goodness rooted in the people’s…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
彝之所秉者無戕賊之害猶木之根而培
植也不猛以厲善即以不猛厲而在不昏
以冥善即以不昏冥而在不倨以肆善即
以不倨肆而在不頽以惰善即以不頽惰
而在喜怒哀樂未發之中於斯乎藴蓄仁
義禮智本然之體于斯乎備具是則為善
必在乎主敬而主敬即所以為善譬之居
焉固其室廬而外寇不至無待於東西之
逐也譬之物焉實其缾罌而他水不入無
===
患於江海之浸也潛心以居而萬慮之不
起其敬至矣所以為萬慮之本者有沛然
莫遏之勢存理之固而百邪之不干其善
得矣而所以閑邪之至者確乎有不變之
守夫然則雖未至於聖人而作聖之功實
在於此豈非舜之徒哉夫舜之於善也得
之聞見而若决江河亦不過以温恭之敬
為之本耳人能進而不已其功擴而益大
其施持吾雞鳴之敬無往而非敬使吾敬
punctuated: 彝之所秉者，無戕賊之害，猶木之根而培植也。不猛以厲，善即以不猛厲而在；不昏以冥，善即以不昏冥而在；不倨以肆，善即以不倨肆而在；不頽以惰，善即以不頽惰而在。喜怒哀樂未發之中，於斯乎藴蓄；仁義禮智本然之體，于斯乎備具。是則為善必在乎主敬，而主敬即所以為善。譬之居焉，固其室廬，而外寇不至，無待於東西之逐也；譬之物焉，實其缾罌，而他水不入，無患於江海之浸也。潛心以居，而萬慮之不起，其敬至矣；所以為萬慮之本者，有沛然莫遏之勢。存理之固，而百邪之不干，其善得矣；而所以閑邪之至者，確乎有不變之守。夫然，則雖未至於聖人，而作聖之功實在於此，豈非舜之徒哉？夫舜之於善也，得之聞見，而若决江河，亦不過以温恭之敬為之本耳。人能進而不已其功，擴而益大其施，持吾雞鳴之敬，無往而非敬，使吾敬
translation_en: …what is held through the constant norms of human nature suffers no destructive injury, just as a tree’s roots are nurtured with earth. If one is neither violent nor harsh, goodness remains through the absence of violence and harshness; if neither benighted nor obtuse, goodness remains through the absence of benightedness and obtuseness; if neither arrogant nor unrestrained, goodness remains through the absence of arrogance and lack of restraint; if neither dispirited nor indolent, goodness remains through the absence of dispiritedness and indolence. Here is nurtured the equilibrium before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise; here the original constitution of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is fully present. Thus doing good necessarily depends on making reverent attentiveness one’s guiding principle, and making reverent attentiveness one’s guiding principle is itself the means of doing good. To use the analogy of a dwelling: secure its rooms and buildings, and outside raiders will not arrive; there is no need to pursue them east and west. To use the analogy of a vessel: fill its bottles and jars, and other water cannot enter; there is no fear of inundation by rivers and seas. When one dwells with the mind composed and myriad thoughts do not arise, one’s reverent attentiveness has reached its utmost; that which serves as the foundation of myriad thoughts possesses an abundant, irresistible force. When one firmly preserves principle and the hundred evils do not intrude, goodness has been attained; that which brings the exclusion of evil to its utmost possesses a firm and unchanging resolve. If this is so, then although one has not yet become a sage, the work of becoming a sage truly lies here. Is one not, then, a follower of Shun? As for Shun’s relation to goodness, when he apprehended it through hearing or seeing, he was like the rivers bursting their banks; yet even this had no foundation beyond the reverent attentiveness expressed in his gentleness and deference. If a person can advance without ceasing his efforts, broaden and increasingly extend their application, and maintain the reverent attentiveness that is mine at cockcrow, so that wherever I go there is reverent attentiveness, and cause my reverent attentiveness…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所為之善無一之或遺焉則亦舜而已矣
然舜之聖大矣而蹠之惡亦大矣孟子舉
而對言之乃在善利之分程子既以主敬
為為善則不敬者必入於利明矣善利之
分在敬與不敬一心毫釐幹轉之間耳學
者豈可以不謹哉必格物致知以講之熟
見之明使不迷於理欲之疑似而表裏交
正動靜弗違乃為敬之全體也此又孟子
之所未言而程子引而不發之意也
===
表
擬宋諫臣謝詔儆悉心獻替表〔景德三年〕
韓邦奇
同考試官訓導陳　批〔脫去塵腐〕
同考試官學正張　批〔掇拾本朝事畧盡〕
考試官學正張　批〔駢儷可觀〕
考試官教授方　批〔齊整〕
景德三年三月巳未伏蒙
詔儆諫臣悉心獻替者〔臣某〕等誠惶誠懼稽首
punctuated:
所為之善，無一之或遺焉，則亦舜而已矣。然舜之聖大矣，而蹠之惡亦大矣。孟子舉而對言之，乃在善利之分。程子既以主敬為為善，則不敬者必入於利明矣。善利之分，在敬與不敬一心毫釐幹轉之間耳。學者豈可以不謹哉？必格物致知，以講之熟、見之明，使不迷於理欲之疑似，而表裏交正，動靜弗違，乃為敬之全體也。此又孟子之所未言，而程子引而不發之意也。

表
擬宋諫臣謝詔儆悉心獻替表〔景德三年〕
韓邦奇
同考試官訓導陳批〔脫去塵腐〕。
同考試官學正張批〔掇拾本朝事畧盡〕。
考試官學正張批〔駢儷可觀〕。
考試官教授方批〔齊整〕。

景德三年三月巳未，伏蒙詔儆諫臣悉心獻替者。〔臣某〕等誠惶誠懼，稽首
translation_en:
…so that not a single good deed performed is omitted, then one would simply be another Shun. Yet Shun’s sageliness was great, and Zhi’s wickedness was also great. When Mengzi set them alongside one another, his point lay in the distinction between goodness and personal gain. Since Master Cheng took maintaining reverence to constitute doing good, it is clear that those without reverence must fall into the pursuit of gain. The distinction between goodness and gain lies merely in the slightest turn [?] of the mind between reverence and its absence. How could learners fail to exercise care? They must investigate things and extend knowledge, examining the matter thoroughly and perceiving it clearly, so that they are not confused by seeming resemblances between principle and desire. When inner and outer alike are rectified, and neither activity nor stillness departs from reverence, reverence is fully realized. This, moreover, is what Mengzi left unsaid and what Master Cheng intended by drawing the bow without releasing the arrow.

Memorial
Model memorial in the voice of Song remonstrance officials, expressing thanks for an imperial decree admonishing them to devote themselves wholeheartedly to recommending what is good and opposing what is wrong. 〔Third year of Jingde.〕
By Han Bangqi.
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Free of stale, hackneyed expressions.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The events of the dynasty represented here have been gathered almost exhaustively.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The parallel prose is worthy of admiration.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔Balanced and orderly.〕

On the siwei [?] day of the third month in the third year of Jingde, we reverently received an imperial decree admonishing the remonstrance officials to devote themselves wholeheartedly to recommending what is good and opposing what is wrong. We, 〔your servant So-and-so〕 and the others, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
頓首伏以天地高厚人或有憾於災祥海
嶽崇深時或不辭乎塵潦故孔子亦欲助
我而大舜每樂取人若非决壅於四聰即
是拒善於千里初諫院之肇置實
昭代之宏規諫議大夫沿嬴秦而雖舊正言
司諫乃端拱之更新寵錫嘉名令其顧而
思義別勑供職俾之專以無他但重任畀
於凡庸顧綿力何能振起事非食稱人與
官違愧久濫於素餐譏難逃於清論幸追
===
邦憲乃勞
帝懷
九重之詔下臨百僚之心皆竦謂未前聞諸古
乃獲始見於
今臣等目相視以厚顏手共舉而加額誓勉
方來之績圖彌已往之愆兹盖伏遇
○○○○
大君有為
至誠無息
punctuated:
頓首，伏以天地高厚，人或有憾於災祥；海嶽崇深，時或不辭乎塵潦。故孔子亦欲助我，而大舜每樂取人。若非决壅於四聰，即是拒善於千里。初諫院之肇置，實昭代之宏規。諫議大夫沿嬴秦而雖舊，正言司諫乃端拱之更新。寵錫嘉名，令其顧而思義；別勑供職，俾之專以無他。但重任畀於凡庸，顧綿力何能振起？事非食稱，人與官違。愧久濫於素餐，譏難逃於清論。幸追邦憲，乃勞帝懷。九重之詔下臨，百僚之心皆竦。謂未前聞諸古，乃獲始見於今。臣等目相視以厚顏，手共舉而加額。誓勉方來之績，圖彌已往之愆。
兹盖伏遇○○○○大君有為，至誠無息，
translation_en:
…we bow our heads to the ground and humbly reflect: Heaven and Earth are lofty and vast, yet people may have grievances concerning calamities and auspicious signs; the seas and mountains are deep and towering, yet at times they do not disdain dust and puddle-water. Thus even Confucius desired others to help him, and the great Shun always delighted in drawing upon others. Unless obstructions to hearing in all four directions are cleared, good counsel is being repelled a thousand li away.
The initial establishment of the Remonstrance Bureau was truly a grand undertaking of this illustrious dynasty. Although the office of Grand Master of Remonstrance was inherited from the Qin dynasty of the Ying house, the offices of Rectifier of Omissions and Controller of Remonstrance were newly instituted in the Duangong era. These fine titles were graciously bestowed so that their holders would consider their meaning and reflect upon their duties. Special commands assigned them their service so that they might devote themselves exclusively to it. Yet weighty responsibilities were entrusted to mediocre men: how could our feeble powers rise to the task? Our work has not matched our stipends, and we have failed to measure up to our offices. We are ashamed to have long drawn salaries without rendering service, and can hardly escape the censure of discerning opinion. We might have expected the laws of the realm to be invoked against us [?]; instead, we have troubled Your Majesty’s thoughts.
The edict has descended from the ninefold palace, and the hearts of all officials tremble in awe. What we had never heard of in antiquity we have now been privileged to witness for the first time. We your servants look at one another, our faces thick with shame, and together raise our hands to our foreheads in gratitude. We vow to strive for accomplishments in the days ahead and seek to make amends for our past faults.
This is because we have humbly had the good fortune to encounter ○○○○ a great sovereign who acts with purpose, whose utmost sincerity never ceases…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
生質特異天字成文
幼志非凡
御榻升坐經書一覽戚誦賓客每見降階北
冠征誅
獨斷於羣議四方水旱不厭於屢陳真
至聖之殊常故萬善之無備轉對之典
祖法遙傳直言之求
父訓親受茲因星變之異益致
天聽之卑
===
虛受體易之咸大諫
誦詩之板
慕讜言之諤諤極
聖德之謙謙臣等敢不許此官以是身堅赤心
於白首閑邪陳善願
隆堯舜之君補過進忠必以仁義之道若
發令舉事之未當及賢良忠孝之可稱或廷
議或上封皆稽故事雖犯
顏雖逆
punctuated:
生質特異，天字成文；幼志非凡，御榻升坐。經書一覽戚誦，賓客每見降階北冠。征誅獨斷於羣議，四方水旱不厭於屢陳。真至聖之殊常，故萬善之無備。轉對之典，祖法遙傳；直言之求，父訓親受。茲因星變之異，益致天聽之卑。
虛受體易之咸，大諫誦詩之板。慕讜言之諤諤，極聖德之謙謙。臣等敢不許此官以是身，堅赤心於白首？閑邪陳善，願隆堯舜之君；補過進忠，必以仁義之道。若發令舉事之未當，及賢良忠孝之可稱，或廷議，或上封，皆稽故事。雖犯顏，雖逆
translation_en:
…Your innate endowment was exceptional, with the character tian (“Heaven”) appearing as a pattern [?]; your aspirations in childhood were extraordinary, and you ascended the imperial couch and sat upon it. After one reading of the canonical books, you could recite them [?]; whenever you received guests, you descended the steps [the following words, 北冠, are unclear]. In punitive campaigns, you reached independent decisions amid the assembled opinions; you never wearied of repeated reports of floods and droughts throughout the realm. Truly, your supreme sagacity surpasses the ordinary; hence your myriad virtues are without completeness [?]. The institution of officials taking turns to address the throne was handed down from your ancestors; the injunction to seek forthright speech you received personally from your father. Now, because of anomalous changes among the stars, you have made the imperial ear still more humble and receptive.
In receiving counsel with an open mind, you embody the meaning of Xian (“Influence”) in the Book of Changes; for earnest remonstrance, you recite Ban (“The Board”) in the Book of Odes. You esteem the unflinching frankness of upright speech and carry the humility of your sagely virtue to its utmost. How could we, your servants, fail to pledge our very persons to these offices and preserve our loyal hearts until our hair turns white? By restraining error and presenting what is good, we wish to exalt our sovereign as a Yao or Shun; in correcting faults and offering loyal counsel, we must follow the way of benevolence and righteousness. Whether concerning inappropriate decrees and undertakings, or worthy, loyal, and filial persons deserving commendation, we shall consult precedents in every case, whether deliberating at court or submitting sealed memorials. Though we offend your countenance, though we go against…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
耳敢賣直名夙夜匪躬惟期
君正而國定寵辱無慮務見
世治以民安伏願
求諫非難思難於用
初銳雖易保易於終
山藏疾川納污廣容狂誕而恕愚淺之量
木從繩金作礪擴屏諛佞而除誹謗之心三
事擇官為
社稷萬年之慶
===
六弊絶念遺
子孫百世之謨臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
punctuated:
耳，敢賣直名？夙夜匪躬，惟期君正而國定；寵辱無慮，務見世治以民安。伏願求諫非難，思難於用；初銳雖易，保易於終。山藏疾，川納污，廣容狂誕而恕愚淺之量；木從繩，金作礪，擴屏諛佞而除誹謗之心。三事擇官，為社稷萬年之慶；六弊絶念，遺子孫百世之謨。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
translation_en:
…the ears, would we dare seek a reputation for forthrightness? Serving selflessly morning and night, we hope only that the ruler will be upright and the state secure. Untroubled by favor or disgrace, we strive to see the realm well governed and the people at peace. We humbly pray: seeking remonstrance is not difficult; consider the difficulty of putting it into practice. Though initial zeal is easy, preserve that ease to the end [?]. As mountains harbor blemishes and rivers receive filth, enlarge your capacity to tolerate wild and extravagant speech and forgive ignorance and shallowness. As wood follows the marking cord and metal is worked upon the whetstone, broaden your resolve to reject flatterers and remove the grounds for slander. Choose officials for the three affairs [?], bringing blessings to the altars of soil and grain for ten thousand years; banish all thought of the six abuses, bequeathing a guiding plan to your descendants for a hundred generations. We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere Your Sagely Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第一問　李澍
同考試官教諭吳　批〔我〕
皇祖
列聖
皇上禮樂相傳一道所以致治之隆歷數前代皆莫及此策能鋪張而揚
聖化竊窺
天地運用之妙有年者他日對
〔厲之必涵泳〕
===
大廷頌
德教之盛尚有待於子
考試官學正張　批〔通篇條荅無遺於論樂處尤〕
〔有考據必非徒言者〕
考試官教授方　批〔五策皆善敷陳而此篇尤勝〕
〔故錄〕
對觀禮樂於
聖祖之諭則知欲復古之治者禮樂不可偏廢
考禮樂於歷代之跡則知治之不古若者
punctuated:
第一問　李澍
同考試官教諭吳　批〔我〕皇祖、列聖、皇上，禮樂相傳一道，所以致治之隆，歷數前代，皆莫及。此策能鋪張而揚聖化，竊窺天地運用之妙有年者。他日對〔厲之必涵泳〕大廷，頌德教之盛，尚有待於子。
考試官學正張　批〔通篇條荅無遺，於論樂處尤〕〔有考據，必非徒言者。〕
考試官教授方　批〔五策皆善敷陳，而此篇尤勝，〕〔故錄。〕
對：觀禮樂於聖祖之諭，則知欲復古之治者，禮樂不可偏廢；考禮樂於歷代之跡，則知治之不古若者
translation_en:
First policy question. Li Shu.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Our imperial progenitor, the successive sage emperors, and His Majesty have transmitted rites and music along a single Way, thereby bringing government to its flourishing height. Reviewing the preceding dynasties one by one, none can equal this. This policy essay amply expounds and extols the sage ruler’s transforming influence; its author appears to have glimpsed the marvelous workings of Heaven and Earth for years. When you answer before the imperial court someday, we shall look to you to celebrate the flourishing of imperial virtue and instruction.” An interposed annotation reads: “Exert yourself in this; you must immerse yourself thoroughly” [?].
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Throughout the essay, the answers address each point without omission. The discussion of music is especially well supported by textual evidence; this certainly is no mere empty talk.”
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: “All five policy essays are skillfully developed, but this one is particularly outstanding; hence its inclusion.”
Response: By considering rites and music in the sacred progenitor’s instructions, we recognize that anyone wishing to restore the government of antiquity must neglect neither rites nor music. By examining rites and music in the surviving traces of successive dynasties, we recognize that, where government falls short of that of antiquity, …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂皆為虛文禮樂者所以昭天地事鬼
神諧萬民致百物者也今
朝廷無一事而非禮樂率土無一處而無禮
樂大夫士無一人而去禮樂百姓日用禮
樂而不知盈天地間無非禮樂之道至矣
盛矣無以復加矣草野之臣嘗莊誦我
太祖高皇帝禮樂治天下之諭每竊嘆曰大哉
皇言一言而隆唐虞三代之化定萬載太平之
基彼漢以下諸君智皆不足以知此無怪
===
乎有緣物設教之說也則其治又安得與
先王並言也哉嘅自文武之澤息而禮樂
之道墜呂項之火熾而禮樂之書亡至漢
賈誼嘗有志於是矣儀法已具而文帝謙
讓未遑說者乃謂絳灌之徒害之則借曰
有其君未必有其臣也唐太宗亦有志於
是矣禮樂致問而房魏愧無素業說者又
謂關雎麟趾之意安在則借曰有其臣未
必有其君也宋朱子論宗廟而曰神祖慨
punctuated:
禮樂皆為虛文。禮樂者，所以昭天地、事鬼神、諧萬民、致百物者也。今朝廷無一事而非禮樂，率土無一處而無禮樂，大夫士無一人而去禮樂，百姓日用禮樂而不知。盈天地間，無非禮樂之道，至矣！盛矣！無以復加矣！草野之臣嘗莊誦我太祖高皇帝禮樂治天下之諭，每竊嘆曰：「大哉，皇言！一言而隆唐虞三代之化，定萬載太平之基。彼漢以下諸君，智皆不足以知此，無怪乎有緣物設教之說也，則其治又安得與先王並言也哉！」
嘅自文武之澤息，而禮樂之道墜；呂項之火熾，而禮樂之書亡。至漢，賈誼嘗有志於是矣，儀法已具，而文帝謙讓未遑。說者乃謂絳灌之徒害之，則借曰有其君，未必有其臣也。唐太宗亦有志於是矣，禮樂致問，而房魏愧無素業。說者又謂關雎麟趾之意安在，則借曰有其臣，未必有其君也。宋朱子論宗廟而曰：「神祖慨
translation_en:
…rites and music had both become empty formalities. Rites and music are the means by which Heaven and Earth are made manifest, ghosts and spirits are served, the myriad people are brought into harmony, and all things are brought to their proper fulfillment. Today, at court there is no affair that does not embody rites and music; throughout the realm there is no place without them; among the grandees and scholars there is no one who departs from them. The common people practice rites and music daily without knowing it. All that fills the space between Heaven and Earth embodies their Way. How consummate! How flourishing! Nothing further could be added! Your servant, dwelling in the countryside, has reverently recited the injunction of our Emperor Taizu Gao concerning governing the world through rites and music. Each time, I have privately exclaimed: “Great indeed are these imperial words! With a single utterance, he brought to full flowering the transforming influence of the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and established the foundation of peace for ten thousand years. The rulers from the Han onward all lacked the wisdom to understand this. No wonder they spoke of establishing instruction through external things. How, then, could their governance be mentioned alongside that of the former kings?”
Alas, once the beneficent influence of Kings Wen and Wu ceased, the Way of rites and music fell into decline; when the fires of Lü and Xiang [?] blazed, the books of rites and music perished. In the Han, Jia Yi once aspired to restore them. His ceremonial procedures were already prepared, but Emperor Wen modestly deferred and had not found time to act. Commentators then said that men such as Jiang and Guan obstructed him, thus pleading that even when the requisite ruler existed, the requisite minister did not necessarily exist. Emperor Taizong of the Tang likewise aspired to this. He inquired about rites and music, but Fang and Wei were ashamed that they had not previously studied them. Commentators also asked where the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi) was to be found, thus pleading that even when the requisite ministers existed, the requisite ruler did not necessarily exist. Master Zhu of the Song, discussing the imperial ancestral temples, said: “Shenzu [?], deeply stirred…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
然討論舊典遠跡三代之隆不幸未及營
表而又欲脩定禮書且以律呂新書審音
協律皆未及就君臣難遇遂爲萬世闕典
考之當時禮出於叔孫通房玄齡劉温叟
輩之所脩樂出於司馬相如祖孝孫和峴
輩之所定雖亦未嘗無禮樂然大抵漢因
於秦唐因於隋宋因於唐於五代禮多闕
畧樂雜俗鄭臨事之際指儀文器數而曰
此禮也指鍾磬琴瑟而曰此樂也君臣上
===
下之間皆視之為虛文長物何補於治間
有一二明君學士未能忘情於此然不究
其全體本末而徒曰禮云樂云亦將如之
何哉蓋禮非徒用之祭享冠婚賓射之謂
凡國家之辨方正位體國經野設官分職
自宮室衣服器用以至飲食動止若周禮
之所載三綱五常之教若夏殷之所因易
象之決疑春秋之記事若韓宣子之所稱
者禮之全體也若董仲舒以立太學劉向
punctuated:
然討論舊典，遠跡三代之隆，不幸未及營表，而又欲脩定禮書，且以《律呂新書》審音協律，皆未及就。君臣難遇，遂爲萬世闕典。」考之當時，禮出於叔孫通、房玄齡、劉温叟輩之所脩，樂出於司馬相如、祖孝孫、和峴輩之所定。雖亦未嘗無禮樂，然大抵漢因於秦，唐因於隋，宋因於唐、於五代。禮多闕畧，樂雜俗鄭。臨事之際，指儀文器數而曰：「此禮也。」指鍾磬琴瑟而曰：「此樂也。」君臣上下之間，皆視之為虛文長物，何補於治？間有一二明君學士，未能忘情於此，然不究其全體本末，而徒曰「禮云樂云」，亦將如之何哉？
蓋禮非徒用之祭享、冠婚、賓射之謂。凡國家之辨方正位、體國經野、設官分職，自宮室衣服器用，以至飲食動止，若《周禮》之所載；三綱五常之教，若夏殷之所因；《易》象之決疑，《春秋》之記事，若韓宣子之所稱者，禮之全體也。若董仲舒以立太學，劉向
translation_en:
…earnestly discussed the ancient canons, seeking far back to emulate the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties. Unfortunately, he did not have time to undertake the construction [?]. He also wished to revise and establish the ritual books and, using the New Treatise on Pitch Pipes (Lülü xinshu), to ascertain the tones and harmonize the pitches; none of these undertakings reached completion. A meeting of the right ruler and ministers is difficult to achieve, and thus these institutions remained lacking for all subsequent ages.”
If we examine those times, their rites were revised by men such as Shusun Tong, Fang Xuanling, and Liu Wensou, and their music was established by men such as Sima Xiangru, Zu Xiaosun, and He Xian. Although they certainly did not lack rites and music altogether, broadly speaking the Han inherited from the Qin, the Tang from the Sui, and the Song from the Tang and the Five Dynasties. Their rites had many omissions, and their music was mingled with vulgar tunes and the music of Zheng. When an occasion arose, they would point to ceremonial forms and the prescribed implements and numbers, saying, “These are rites.” They would point to bells, stone chimes, and the qin and se zithers, saying, “This is music.” Rulers and ministers, superiors and subordinates alike, regarded these as empty formalities and superfluous things. What benefit could they bring to government? Occasionally, one or two enlightened rulers or learned men could not put these matters out of their minds. Yet if they failed to investigate their entirety, their roots and ramifications, and merely spoke of “rites” and “music,” what could be done?
Rites do not mean merely what is employed in sacrifices and offerings, capping and marriage ceremonies, the reception of guests, and archery ceremonies. They encompass the state's determination of directions and proper positions, the planning of the capital and demarcation of the countryside, and the establishment of offices and allocation of duties; everything from palaces, clothing, and utensils to eating, drinking, movement, and repose, as recorded in the Rites of Zhou; the teachings of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues, as inherited by the Xia and Yin; and the resolution of doubts through the images of the Changes and the recording of events in the Spring and Autumn Annals, as praised by Han Xuanzi. These constitute rites in their entirety. As for Dong Zhongshu, who took the establishment of the Imperial University as rites, and Liu Xiang…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以興辟雍設庠序明帝以大射養老為禮
者則禮之一而真宗東封西祀乃禮之無
稽者也樂非徒用之朝廷郊廟學宮之謂
凡絃歌二南於房中不用鍾磬若鄭氏之
所言大禹九歌之勸周禮九德之歌用之
鄉人邦國沐浴膏澤詠歌勤苦若太史公
之所論者樂之全體也若制氏以鏗鎗鼓
舞劉向以隆雅頌之聲𣪍盈孫以鑄鎛鐘
編鐘為樂者則樂之一而蔡京度帝指定
===
黃鍾乃樂之至繆者也禮以一心之敬異
天下之分無不相敬為本而見於升降揖
遜者為末樂以一心之和同天下之情無
不和合為本而見於音聲舞容者為末禮
樂本末不在是乎司馬遷稱子夏曰綱紀
正然後絃歌詩頌周子曰萬物各得其理
而後和然禮又為樂之本而樂又為禮之
末也夫欲為禮樂而全體本末之不究安
所取禮樂矣此三代而下治出於二而禮
punctuated:
以興辟雍、設庠序，明帝以大射、養老為禮者，則禮之一，而真宗東封西祀，乃禮之無稽者也。樂非徒用之朝廷、郊廟、學宮之謂。凡絃歌二南於房中，不用鍾磬，若鄭氏之所言；大禹九歌之勸，《周禮》九德之歌，用之鄉人邦國；沐浴膏澤，詠歌勤苦，若太史公之所論者，樂之全體也。若制氏以鏗鎗鼓舞，劉向以隆雅頌之聲，𣪍盈孫以鑄鎛鐘、編鐘為樂者，則樂之一，而蔡京度帝指定黃鍾，乃樂之至繆者也。
禮以一心之敬，異天下之分，無不相敬為本，而見於升降揖遜者為末；樂以一心之和，同天下之情，無不和合為本，而見於音聲舞容者為末。禮樂本末不在是乎？司馬遷稱子夏曰：「綱紀正，然後絃歌詩頌。」周子曰：「萬物各得其理而後和。」然禮又為樂之本，而樂又為禮之末也。夫欲為禮樂，而全體本末之不究，安所取禮樂矣？此三代而下，治出於二，而禮
translation_en:
…regarded establishing the Biyong academy and setting up local schools as ritual, while Emperor Ming regarded the Great Archery Ceremony and care for the aged as ritual: these were only individual aspects of ritual. Emperor Zhenzong’s performance of the feng sacrifice in the east and sacrifices in the west, however, were rituals without authoritative foundation. Music does not mean merely what is employed at court, at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, or in the schools. Singing the songs of the Two Southern Sections of the Book of Odes to string accompaniment in the inner chambers, without bells or chime stones, as Master Zheng described; the exhortations of Great Yu’s Nine Songs and the songs of the Nine Virtues in the Rites of Zhou, employed among villagers and throughout the states; receiving the gracious bounty of government and singing of toil and hardship, as the Grand Historian discussed—these constitute music in its entirety. When Master Zhi regarded the clangor of instruments, drumming, and dancing as music, Liu Xiang regarded the promotion of the sounds of the Elegantiae and Hymns as music, and 𣪍 Yingsun [?] regarded casting large bells and sets of chime bells as music, these were only individual aspects of music. Cai Jing’s measuring the emperor’s finger to establish the Yellow Bell pitch standard, however, was music at its most erroneous.
Ritual takes as its root the reverence of a single heart, distinguishing the respective stations of all under Heaven so that everyone respects one another; its manifestations in ascending and descending, bowing and yielding precedence, are its branches. Music takes as its root the harmony of a single heart, uniting the feelings of all under Heaven so that everyone lives in concord; its manifestations in sounds and dance movements are its branches. Are not the roots and branches of ritual and music found here? Sima Qian quotes Zixia as saying: “Only after the guiding principles are set right do people sing the Odes and Hymns to string accompaniment.” Master Zhou said: “Only after all things attain their proper principle is there harmony.” Thus ritual is also the root of music, and music is also a branch of ritual. If one wishes to institute ritual and music without thoroughly investigating their entirety, roots and branches alike, how can one grasp ritual and music? This is why, after the Three Dynasties, governance proceeded along two separate tracks, and ritual…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
樂爲虛名所以致嘆於歐陽子也禮樂旣
爲虛名則其架漏度日牽補過時而把持
一世者不以獄訟兵食簿書期會之法而
何以哉下至胡元禮容樂音多用本俗而
禮樂之壞極矣無往不復極否必治我
太祖高皇帝以神聖之德在
天子之位旣以諭羣臣之言治天下矣又徵耆
儒分局以究禮樂然草刱之初諸儒未足
以當
===
上意僅成大明集禮一書而樂書竟無聞焉我
皇上承
聖祖
神宗重熈累洽之後正百年興禮樂之期乃若
有議樂之舉豈不欲增光
聖祖而續數千載旣墜之典哉草野之下何足
以知之然樂以定黃鍾爲先定黃鍾在截
管候氣而候氣之法不易言也陰陽之氣
距地面各有淺深而淺深之閒不易測也
punctuated:
樂爲虛名，所以致嘆於歐陽子也。禮樂旣爲虛名，則其架漏度日、牽補過時而把持一世者，不以獄訟兵食簿書期會之法，而何以哉？下至胡元，禮容樂音多用本俗，而禮樂之壞極矣。無往不復，極否必治。我太祖高皇帝以神聖之德在天子之位，旣以諭羣臣之言治天下矣，又徵耆儒分局以究禮樂。然草刱之初，諸儒未足以當上意，僅成《大明集禮》一書，而樂書竟無聞焉。
我皇上承聖祖神宗重熈累洽之後，正百年興禮樂之期，乃若有議樂之舉，豈不欲增光聖祖而續數千載旣墜之典哉？草野之下，何足以知之？然樂以定黃鍾爲先，定黃鍾在截管候氣，而候氣之法不易言也。陰陽之氣距地面各有淺深，而淺深之閒不易測也。
translation_en:
…music became an empty name: this was what occasioned Master Ouyang’s lament. Once ritual and music had become empty names, what means could those who patched leaks to get through the days, cobbled things together to pass the time, and maintained their hold for a generation employ, other than procedures for criminal cases and litigation, military affairs and provisions, registers and documents, and deadlines and official reporting? By the time of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, ceremonial forms and musical sounds largely followed their native customs, and the deterioration of ritual and music reached its extreme. Nothing departs without returning; when adversity reaches its extreme, order must follow. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, possessing divine and sagely virtue and occupying the position of Son of Heaven, had already governed the realm through the words with which he instructed his ministers. He also summoned elderly Confucian scholars and assigned them to separate bureaus to investigate ritual and music. Yet in those early days of establishing institutions, the scholars were unable fully to meet the imperial intention. They completed only the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming (Da Ming jili); of a book on music, nothing was ever heard.
Our reigning emperor has inherited the successive ages of flourishing virtue and harmonious government established by his sagely and divine imperial forebears. This is precisely the time, after a hundred years, to revive ritual and music. If an undertaking to deliberate upon music is now proposed, is it not intended to add glory to the sagely founding ancestor and restore institutions that have fallen into disuse for thousands of years? How could someone of my humble station, outside official service, know enough to understand this? Yet in music, the first priority is to establish the pitch of the Yellow Bell (huangzhong). Establishing the Yellow Bell depends on cutting pitch pipes and observing the qi, and the method of observing the qi is not easily explained. The qi of yin and yang lie at differing depths beneath the ground’s surface, and the distinctions between these depths are not easily measured.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
能知陰陽氣之淺深則能以管候氣而黃
鍾定十一律由是可損益而生矣伏惟
皇上仁以用禮樂
聖以作禮樂將見以一心之敬和著之禮文樂
音舉而措之耳大禮與天地同節大樂與
天地同和斯世斯人何幸際焉
第二問
韓邦奇
同考試官訓導陳　批〔策題雖偶及於廉然亦欲因是以觀諸士今日立志何如此卷敷對詳盡而終篇極有〕
===
斷制如有用我執此以往他日卒無愧其言
同考試官學正張　批〔以守令之廉不廉歸之風憲之振不振非知世務者不能且一篇之內抑揚起伏辭藻爛〕
然必熟於策學者
考試官學正張　批〔策卷極難得嘉者此卷五對皆出人意表錄此其餘可知也〕
考試官教授方　批〔初場得子已拭目二場亦有人不能到者五策隨事而答如出諸囊中沛然有餘主〕
punctuated:
能知陰陽氣之淺深，則能以管候氣，而黃鍾定，十一律由是可損益而生矣。伏惟皇上仁以用禮樂，聖以作禮樂，將見以一心之敬和著之禮文樂音，舉而措之耳。大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，斯世斯人何幸際焉！

第二問
韓邦奇

同考試官訓導陳　批〔策題雖偶及於廉，然亦欲因是以觀諸士今日立志何如。此卷敷對詳盡，而終篇極有〕斷制。如有用我，執此以往，他日卒無愧其言。

同考試官學正張　批〔以守令之廉不廉歸之風憲之振不振，非知世務者不能。且一篇之內，抑揚起伏，辭藻爛〕然，必熟於策學者。

考試官學正張　批〔策卷極難得嘉者，此卷五對皆出人意表，錄此，其餘可知也。〕

考試官教授方　批〔初場得子，已拭目；二場亦有人不能到者。五策隨事而答，如出諸囊中，沛然有餘。主〕
translation_en:
If one can ascertain the depths of the yin and yang vital energies, one can use pitch pipes to observe their arrival and thereby establish the Yellow Bell pitch. The other eleven pitches can then be generated from it by proportional diminution and augmentation. I humbly reflect that Your Majesty employs rites and music through benevolence and creates rites and music through sagely wisdom. We shall see the reverence and harmony of your single-minded heart expressed in ritual forms and musical sounds, simply brought forth and put into practice. Great rites share the rhythms of Heaven and Earth; great music shares their harmony. How fortunate are this age and its people to encounter such a time!

Second Policy Question
Han Bangqi

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: Although the policy question touches only incidentally on incorruptibility, it also seeks thereby to see what aspirations the candidates have established for themselves today. This script develops its answers fully and thoroughly, and its conclusion displays considerable decisiveness of judgment. “If someone were to employ me”—if he proceeds holding fast to these principles, in future he will ultimately have no cause to be ashamed of his words.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: To attribute the incorruptibility or corruption of prefects and county magistrates to the vigor or laxity of the censorial authorities is something only a person who understands the affairs of the age could do. Moreover, within this single essay, the shifts of emphasis, the rising and falling cadence, and the brilliance of its language show that he must be well versed in the study of policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Fine policy-examination scripts are exceedingly hard to find. All five answers in this script surpass expectations. By recording this one, the quality of the others may be understood.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Professor: On encountering your work in the first session, I already rubbed my eyes in anticipation; in the second session, too, there were achievements beyond the reach of others. Your five policy essays answer each matter as it arises, as though drawing answers from a pouch, flowing abundantly with strength to spare. Those who preside …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
司者以此等人貢於
上寧不自愧
對廉莫嚴於古法而後之人不可不知廉
莫過於古人而後之人不可不學盖廉雖
一人之行而非一人之事也上者下之表
官者民之表士者衆之表前者後之表紀
綱之起廢風俗之美惡治道之盛衰皆係
於是惡可以為細行末節而不加之意乎
然不知古法則無以知如何而後謂之廉
===
不擇古人而學之則又何所依據如射者
之的必中之而不敢不及焉也哉執事先
生策諸士而及於廉欲以風動一世皆如
孟子所稱文繡之不願而身死之不受真
西山所論餽遺之恥而苞苴之羞不至如
朱晦庵所譏金珠脯醢契券詩文者甚盛
心也生不敏何知所對然嘗受教於有道
者而竊有志於是矣稽之古非義非道一
介不取乃盛德而伊尹行焉可見聖人檢
punctuated:
司者以此等人貢於上，寧不自愧？
對：廉莫嚴於古法，而後之人不可不知；廉莫過於古人，而後之人不可不學。盖廉雖一人之行，而非一人之事也。上者，下之表；官者，民之表；士者，衆之表；前者，後之表。紀綱之起廢、風俗之美惡、治道之盛衰，皆係於是，惡可以為細行末節而不加之意乎？然不知古法，則無以知如何而後謂之廉；不擇古人而學之，則又何所依據，如射者之的，必中之而不敢不及焉也哉？執事先生策諸士而及於廉，欲以風動一世，皆如孟子所稱文繡之不願而身死之不受，真西山所論餽遺之恥而苞苴之羞，不至如朱晦庵所譏金珠脯醢契券詩文者，甚盛心也。生不敏，何知所對？然嘗受教於有道者，而竊有志於是矣。稽之古，非義非道，一介不取，乃盛德，而伊尹行焉，可見聖人檢
translation_en:
…those presiding over the examination, in presenting such men to the throne, could hardly avoid feeling ashamed themselves [?].
Your servant replies: In matters of integrity, nothing is stricter than the ancient laws, which later generations must understand; none surpass the ancients in integrity, and later generations must learn from them. For although integrity is an individual's conduct, it is not a matter concerning that individual alone. Superiors are models for their subordinates; officials, for the people; scholars, for the multitude; and predecessors, for their successors. The establishment or abandonment of governing principles, the goodness or badness of customs, and the flourishing or decline of good government all depend upon this. How could we regard it as a minor matter of conduct or an incidental detail and give it no attention? Yet without knowing the ancient laws, we have no way of knowing what constitutes integrity. And without choosing ancients as our models and learning from them, what standard could we rely upon—as an archer relies upon a target that he must hit and dare not fall short of?
You gentlemen conducting this examination have included integrity in your policy questions to the candidates, wishing thereby to transform the whole age through your influence. You wish everyone to embody what Mengzi praised: not coveting embroidered finery and refusing to accept improper gifts even at the cost of one's life; and what Zhen Xishan discussed: feeling disgrace at gifts and shame at bribes. You wish them to avoid the practices Zhu Hui'an mocked, involving gold and pearls, dried meat and meat sauces, deeds and contracts, and poetry and prose. Yours is a most noble intention. I, a student of limited ability, scarcely know how to reply. Yet I have received instruction from men who possess the Way, and privately aspire to such integrity.
Examining antiquity, we find that to take not even the smallest thing when it accords neither with righteousness nor with the Way is consummate virtue, and Yi Yin practiced it. Here we can see how the sage disciplined…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
身之窮畜馬乘不察雞豚盖古語而獻子
述焉可見當時風俗之美苟變賦於民食
二雞子魏文侯弗用爲將雖若見譏於子
思然近古論人之精如此非後世之所及
也宋英宗禁宮貨種蔬以賣雖若微物不
足計然賢君勸下之切如此歷數代而一
見也此唐虞三代之盛所以貴賤窮達莫
非節儉清介之人後世雖上下征利士風
衰薄之日其秉彛好德天理在人心亦有
===
未泯者以故清脩苦節之士間一出焉以
相言之諸葛亮有桑有田不別治生以長
尺寸可謂廉矣而季文子相三君無衣帛
之妾盧懷慎飯客蒸豆兩器公儀休食於
舍而茹葵慍而拔其葵貴極而能此豈可
及乎以將言之張良爲帝者師不敢當齊
三萬戶可謂廉矣而馬援擊交阯惟載薏
苡一車曹彬伐蜀橐中惟圖書衣裳祭遵
久在軍旅夫人裳不加緣武人而能此豈
punctuated:
身之窮。畜馬乘，不察雞豚，盖古語而獻子述焉，可見當時風俗之美。苟變賦於民，食二雞子，魏文侯弗用爲將，雖若見譏於子思，然近古論人之精如此，非後世之所及也。宋英宗禁宮貨種蔬以賣，雖若微物不足計，然賢君勸下之切如此，歷數代而一見也。此唐虞三代之盛，所以貴賤窮達莫非節儉清介之人。後世雖上下征利、士風衰薄之日，其秉彛好德，天理在人心亦有未泯者，以故清脩苦節之士間一出焉。

以相言之，諸葛亮有桑有田，不別治生以長尺寸，可謂廉矣。而季文子相三君，無衣帛之妾；盧懷慎飯客，蒸豆兩器；公儀休食於舍而茹葵，慍而拔其葵。貴極而能此，豈可及乎？

以將言之，張良爲帝者師，不敢當齊三萬戶，可謂廉矣。而馬援擊交阯，惟載薏苡一車；曹彬伐蜀，橐中惟圖書衣裳；祭遵久在軍旅，夫人裳不加緣。武人而能此，豈
translation_en:
…the utmost extent of personal discipline [?]. “One who keeps a team of horses does not concern himself with chickens and pigs”: this was an ancient saying recounted by Xianzi, and it shows the excellence of the customs of that time. When collecting levies from the people, Gou Bian ate two chicken eggs, and Marquis Wen of Wei would not employ him as a general. Although this apparently drew criticism from Zisi, such was the exacting scrutiny with which men were judged in times close to antiquity—something later ages could not match. Emperor Yingzong of the Song prohibited palace personnel [?] from growing vegetables for sale. Though this might seem a trifling matter scarcely worth reckoning, such earnestness in a worthy ruler’s encouragement of his subordinates was seen only once in several dynasties. This explains why, in the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, everyone, high or low, in adversity or in success, was frugal and incorruptible. Even in later ages, when those above and below competed for profit and the moral standards of scholars declined, their inherent disposition to love virtue—the heavenly principle within the human heart—was not wholly extinguished. Thus men of pure conduct and rigorous integrity still appeared from time to time.

Speaking of chief ministers, Zhuge Liang possessed mulberry trees and fields but pursued no other means of livelihood to increase his holdings even slightly: he may indeed be called incorruptible.
