Yet Ji Wenzi served three rulers as chief minister and had no concubine clothed in silk; Lu Huaishen entertained guests with two dishes of steamed beans; and Gongyi Xiu, eating mallows at home, became displeased and uprooted them. To act thus at the pinnacle of eminence—how could such men be matched?

Speaking of generals, Zhang Liang served as the emperor’s teacher but did not dare accept a fief of thirty thousand households in Qi: he may indeed be called incorruptible. Yet when Ma Yuan attacked Jiaozhi, he carried back only one cartload of Job’s tears; when Cao Bin campaigned against Shu, his baggage contained only maps, books, and clothing; and although Ji Zun spent many years in military service, his wife’s skirt had no added edging. For military men to act thus—could it…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
易得乎不肯開産業而曰使後世稱為清
白吏子孫者楊震也包拯歲滿不持一硯
率及市白集終身為恨鄧攸載米之郡惟
飲吳水皆守之廉者省察至此無餘蘊矣
清身苦體而詔稱為蹈羔羊之義者王渙
也元德秀令滿笥餘一縑孔奮被徵單車
就路時苗駕牸留犢以去皆令之廉者點
檢至此無指隙矣卻帝秦而辭封辭金於
平原非魯仲連之廉為天下士乎常自耕
===
稼非其力不食者徐稚從胡翼之學饋以
食弗受者徐積偃息窮巷并日而食者管
寧也固窮至此其真可以久處約者邪是
皆古人也皆可學也然論廉者又當深探
其心而不當但觀其跡心無所為而為之
則雖舜受堯之天下周公之富孟子受薛
宋之金季儲之幣而不為過若有所為而
為之則公孫弘之布被實為釣名飾詐之
具耳故君子當學聖人之道學而至於義
punctuated: 易得乎？不肯開産業，而曰使後世稱為清白吏子孫者，楊震也。包拯歲滿不持一硯，率及市白集終身為恨；鄧攸載米之郡，惟飲吳水，皆守之廉者。省察至此，無餘蘊矣。清身苦體，而詔稱為蹈羔羊之義者，王渙也。元德秀令滿，笥餘一縑；孔奮被徵，單車就路；時苗駕牸，留犢以去，皆令之廉者。點檢至此，無指隙矣。卻帝秦而辭封，辭金於平原，非魯仲連之廉為天下士乎？常自耕稼，非其力不食者，徐稚；從胡翼之學，饋以食弗受者，徐積；偃息窮巷，并日而食者，管寧也。固窮至此，其真可以久處約者邪？是皆古人也，皆可學也。然論廉者，又當深探其心，而不當但觀其跡。心無所為而為之，則雖舜受堯之天下，周公之富，孟子受薛宋之金、季儲之幣，而不為過。若有所為而為之，則公孫弘之布被，實為釣名飾詐之具耳。故君子當學聖人之道，學而至於義
translation_en:
…could such men easily be found? It was Yang Zhen who refused to establish an estate, saying that he wished later generations to call his descendants the offspring of an incorruptible official. When Bao Zheng completed his term, he did not take even a single inkstone. The following words concerning a purchase and lifelong regret are garbled [?]. Deng You brought his own rice when he went to his commandery, drinking only the water of Wu. These were incorruptible prefects. Examined this closely, their integrity leaves nothing concealed.

It was Wang Huan who kept himself pure and subjected his body to hardship, and whom an imperial edict praised as fulfilling the moral ideal of “The Lamb.” When Yuan Dexiu completed his term as magistrate, only one piece of silk remained in his chest. When Kong Fen was summoned, he set out in a single carriage. Shi Miao drove a cow but left its calf behind when he departed. These were incorruptible magistrates. Scrutinized this closely, they offer no opening for criticism.

Rejecting the proposal to make Qin’s ruler emperor and declining an enfeoffment, refusing gold from the Lord of Pingyuan—was this not the integrity that made Lu Zhonglian an outstanding gentleman of the realm? Xu Zhi always tilled and planted for himself and ate nothing that had not come from his own labor. Xu Ji studied under Hu Yizhi and refused food offered to him. Guan Ning lived quietly in an impoverished lane, eating only once in several days. Remaining steadfast in poverty to this degree, were they not truly men who could endure straitened circumstances for long? These were all men of antiquity, and all can be emulated.

Yet those who discuss integrity should also probe deeply into their hearts, rather than merely observing their outward conduct. If one acts without an ulterior purpose, then even Shun’s acceptance of Yao’s realm, the Duke of Zhou’s wealth, and Mencius’s acceptance of gold from Xue and Song and gifts from Ji Chu [?] constitute no transgression. If one acts with an ulterior purpose, however, then Gongsun Hong’s cloth quilt was really no more than a device for fishing for fame and cloaking deceit. Thus the gentleman should study the Way of the sages, learning until he attains righteousness…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
精仁熟則辭受取予不待較計論量而自
無過不及之差矣方今
聖天子張四維之廉耻以化天下輔弼大僚秉
九德之簡廉以率百官獨若將若守令若
士視宣德正統有差焉而不敢望洪武永
樂之盛者其故何哉以愚所見其有令焉
金帛為家而有賢能之獎某有守焉賄賂
為市而有超踰之遷如是而求廉於天下
豈不難也此無他係乎風憲之振與不振
===
耳今所謂風憲巡按御史按察司官是也
為御史為按察官者誠皆志范滂之澄清
著朱子之風采登車攬轡而贓污守令望
風解印綬輕車屏徒而官吏夙夜戒飭至
自引去如是而欲求守令之不廉又豈不
難也守令者民之師帥守令既廉則育於
黌序之士孰於耳目之覩記久於彼此之
漸染莫不歆羨向慕以為終身之依歸矣
夫今日之士固他日之居宰執而布庶位
punctuated:
精仁熟，則辭受取予不待較計論量，而自無過不及之差矣。方今聖天子張四維之廉耻以化天下，輔弼大僚秉九德之簡廉以率百官，獨若將、若守令、若士，視宣德、正統有差焉，而不敢望洪武、永樂之盛者，其故何哉？以愚所見，其有令焉，金帛為家，而有賢能之獎；某有守焉，賄賂為市，而有超踰之遷。如是而求廉於天下，豈不難也？此無他，係乎風憲之振與不振耳。
今所謂風憲，巡按御史、按察司官是也。為御史、為按察官者，誠皆志范滂之澄清，著朱子之風采，登車攬轡，而贓污守令望風解印綬；輕車屏徒，而官吏夙夜戒飭，至自引去。如是而欲求守令之不廉，又豈不難也？守令者，民之師帥。守令既廉，則育於黌序之士，孰於耳目之覩記，久於彼此之漸染，莫不歆羨向慕，以為終身之依歸矣。夫今日之士，固他日之居宰執而布庶位
translation_en:
…once their understanding of righteousness is refined and their benevolence mature, they will refuse or accept, take or give, without needing to calculate and weigh things, and will naturally avoid errors of excess or deficiency. Today, our sagely Son of Heaven promotes integrity and a sense of shame, among the Four Bonds, to transform the realm. The great ministers who assist him uphold simplicity joined with uprightness, among the Nine Virtues, to lead the officials. Yet generals, prefects and magistrates, and scholars fall short of those of the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, and cannot dare aspire to the flourishing standards of the Hongwu and Yongle reigns. Why is this? In my humble observation, there are magistrates who fill their households with gold and silk yet receive commendations for worthiness and ability; there are prefects who make a marketplace of bribery yet receive promotions beyond the ordinary ranks. Under such circumstances, is it not difficult to seek integrity throughout the realm? The reason is simply whether or not censorial oversight is vigorously exercised.
Those now charged with censorial oversight are the Regional Inspecting Censors and the officials of the Provincial Surveillance Commissions. If those serving as censors and surveillance officials truly all aspired to Fan Pang’s cleansing of public administration and displayed Master Zhu’s commanding moral bearing, then, as they mounted their carriages and took up the reins, corrupt prefects and magistrates would relinquish their seals and cords at the mere news of their approach. If they traveled in light carriages, dismissing their retinues, officials and clerks would keep themselves under vigilant restraint day and night, even withdrawing voluntarily from office. Under such circumstances, would it not be difficult to find a prefect or magistrate lacking integrity? Prefects and magistrates are the teachers and leaders of the people. Once they are upright, scholars educated in the schools, familiar with what they see and hear and long exposed to its pervasive influence, will all admire and aspire to their example, taking it as their lifelong guide. For the scholars of today are precisely those who will one day hold the chief ministerial posts and fill the various offices…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者也士風既清則上下莫不一於廉彼赳
赳之夫不敢為文官不愛錢之言以誚我
輩而其心不難格矣又何患於不廉雖然
監司者郡邑之所視效朝廷者天下之所
視效本源之地則在我
皇上正心以正左右正左右以正朝廷而已如
是持以數年則今之廉者執事將稱數之
不暇又何羨於古之人古之人乎
第叁問
焦思明
同考試官訓導何　批〔此策本欲觀諸士之博而子乃以一貫為言當讓子一頭地矣〕
考試官學正張　批〔隨問以荅而末歸之一心必博而能約者〕
考試官教授方　批〔此策當錄〕
對多聞而疑之不闕則有不知之强博學
而辨之不明則無新得之益然聞之不多
固無由致其心之有疑而辨之不明則其
punctuated:
者也。士風既清，則上下莫不一於廉。彼赳赳之夫，不敢為「文官不愛錢」之言以誚我輩，而其心不難格矣，又何患於不廉？雖然，監司者，郡邑之所視效；朝廷者，天下之所視效。本源之地，則在我皇上正心以正左右，正左右以正朝廷而已。如是持以數年，則今之廉者，執事將稱數之不暇，又何羨於古之人、古之人乎？

第叁問
焦思明
同考試官訓導何，批〔此策本欲觀諸士之博，而子乃以一貫為言，當讓子一頭地矣。〕
考試官學正張，批〔隨問以荅，而末歸之一心，必博而能約者。〕
考試官教授方，批〔此策當錄。〕

對：多聞而疑之不闕，則有不知之强；博學而辨之不明，則無新得之益。然聞之不多，固無由致其心之有疑，而辨之不明，則其
translation_en:
…are those who will hold the highest offices and fill the various ranks of government in days to come. Once the ethos of scholars is pure, all, from high to low, will be united in integrity. Those martial men will not dare to mock us with the saying, “Civil officials do not love money,” and their hearts will not be difficult to rectify. What further concern need there be about a lack of integrity? Nevertheless, prefectures and counties look to the surveillance officials as their example, and the whole realm looks to the imperial court. The ultimate source lies simply in Our Emperor’s rectifying his own heart in order to rectify those around him, and rectifying those around him in order to rectify the court. If this is sustained for several years, you, honored examiners, will scarcely have time to enumerate the upright men of our day. Why then envy the men of antiquity—the men of antiquity?

Third Question
Jiao Siming

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This policy question was originally intended to reveal the breadth of the candidates’ learning, yet you have spoken in terms of a single unifying principle. I must concede you the higher place.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔He answers each question in turn, but ultimately brings everything back to the single mind. He must be someone whose broad learning enables him to grasp essentials.〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔This policy essay should be included in the record.〕

In reply: If one hears much but fails to leave doubtful matters unresolved, one risks making assertions about what one does not know. If one studies broadly but fails to discriminate clearly, one gains no fresh understanding. Yet without hearing much, one certainly has no means of bringing doubts to mind; and if one fails to discriminate clearly, then one’s…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
學也是非錯雜真妄混殽凡焉無寸稱焉
不呈而已此君子之學所以雖貴於闕疑
而尤貴於明辨也請因明問以為疑者而
辨之三皇五帝之名肇見於周禮外史後
秦博士以天地人司馬貞以庖犧女媧神
農梁武帝以伏犧神農燧人為三皇孔子
荅宰我及史記皆以黃帝顓頊帝嚳堯舜
其荅季康子及月令皆以太皞炎帝黃帝
少皞顓頊梁武帝以黃帝少皞帝嚳帝摯
===
帝堯胡五峯據繫辭以伏犧神農黃帝堯
舜為五帝至朱子依孔安國以伏犧神農
黃帝為三皇少昊顓頊高辛堯舜為五帝
三皇五帝舍安國其何據乎七十弟子之
說始見於太史公而史記世家乃曰身通
六藝者七十二人至列傳自顏回至公西
蒧則七十七人家語亦七十七人無公伯
寮秦冄鄡單而別有琴牢陳亢縣亶文翁
石室圖亦七十二人而內有申棖蘧伯玉
punctuated:
學也是非錯雜，真妄混殽，凡焉無寸，稱焉不呈而已。此君子之學所以雖貴於闕疑，而尤貴於明辨也。請因明問，以為疑者而辨之。
三皇五帝之名，肇見於《周禮》外史。後，秦博士以天地人，司馬貞以庖犧女媧神農，梁武帝以伏犧神農燧人為三皇。孔子荅宰我及《史記》，皆以黃帝顓頊帝嚳堯舜；其荅季康子及《月令》，皆以太皞炎帝黃帝少皞顓頊；梁武帝以黃帝少皞帝嚳帝摯帝堯，胡五峯據《繫辭》以伏犧神農黃帝堯舜為五帝。至朱子依孔安國，以伏犧神農黃帝為三皇，少昊顓頊高辛堯舜為五帝。三皇五帝，舍安國其何據乎？
七十弟子之說，始見於太史公，而《史記》世家乃曰：「身通六藝者七十二人。」至列傳，自顏回至公西蒧，則七十七人。《家語》亦七十七人，無公伯寮秦冄鄡單，而別有琴牢陳亢縣亶。《文翁石室圖》亦七十二人，而內有申棖蘧伯玉
translation_en:
…in their learning, right and wrong become entangled, and truth and falsehood intermixed, with no measure for assessing them or means of making them manifest [?]. This is why the gentleman’s learning, though it values leaving doubtful matters unresolved, values clear discrimination still more. Allow me, in response to your discerning question, to examine and distinguish the matters in doubt.
The designation “Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors” first appears in the section on the Outer Scribe in the Rites of Zhou. Subsequently, the erudites of Qin identified Heaven, Earth, and Man as the Three Sovereigns; Sima Zhen identified Paoxi, Nüwa, and Shennong; and Emperor Wu of Liang identified Fuxi, Shennong, and Suiren. Confucius’s reply to Zai Wo and the Records of the Grand Historian both identify Huangdi, Zhuanxu, Di Ku, Yao, and Shun as the Five Emperors. His reply to Ji Kangzi and the Monthly Ordinances both identify Taihao, Yandi, Huangdi, Shaohao, and Zhuanxu. Emperor Wu of Liang identified Huangdi, Shaohao, Di Ku, Di Zhi, and Di Yao; Hu Wufeng, drawing on the Appended Statements of the Changes, identified Fuxi, Shennong, Huangdi, Yao, and Shun. Master Zhu, following Kong Anguo, identified Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi as the Three Sovereigns, and Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Gaoxin, Yao, and Shun as the Five Emperors. For the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, if we set aside Anguo, what authority can we rely upon?
The account of seventy disciples first appears in the work of the Grand Historian, yet the “Hereditary Houses” section of the Records of the Grand Historian actually says: “Seventy-two men personally mastered the Six Arts.” In its “Biographies,” however, the number from Yan Hui to Gongxi Dian is seventy-seven. The Family Sayings of Confucius also lists seventy-seven, omitting Gongbo Liao, Qin Ran, and Que Dan, but including instead Qin Lao, Chen Kang, and Xian Dan. The Illustrations in Wen Weng’s Stone Chamber likewise depicts seventy-two, but among them are Shen Cheng and Qu Boyu…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
林放唐據列傳以贈爵列祀宋仍唐數而
增琴張陳亢申棖蘧伯玉林放為八十二
人至今因之昔孟子去孟獻子不遠其友
五人乃忘其三況馬遷漢儒舛駁之學掇
拾之書而可信乎蘧伯玉孔子稱為夫子
公伯寮愬子路於季孫恐非在弟子之列
者且太史公自言悉取論語弟子問則其
無他明據審矣然則非論語所載無年不
見書傳者姓名未可詳也七十弟子舍論
===
語其何考乎朱子告孝宗必曰誠意正心
至有上所厭聞之戒然誠正實脩身出治
之本而齊王好勇樂好貨色孟子雖就事
論事皆以格其非心即誠正之目也周子
著書首太極圖蓋當聖學不講之後先示
學者道體之大為上達底止而論語先學
習則下學而上達之意也牛畜荀欣徐越
侍而趙烈侯止歌者之田竇長君少君與
節行長者居而皆為退讓君子大儒薰陶
punctuated:
林放。唐據列傳以贈爵列祀，宋仍唐數，而增琴張、陳亢、申棖、蘧伯玉、林放，為八十二人，至今因之。昔孟子去孟獻子不遠，其友五人，乃忘其三。況馬遷漢儒舛駁之學、掇拾之書，而可信乎？蘧伯玉，孔子稱為夫子；公伯寮愬子路於季孫，恐非在弟子之列者。且太史公自言悉取《論語》弟子問，則其無他明據審矣。然則非《論語》所載，無年，不見書傳者，姓名未可詳也。七十弟子，舍《論語》其何考乎？
朱子告孝宗，必曰誠意正心，至有上所厭聞之戒。然誠正實脩身出治之本。而齊王好勇、樂，好貨、色，孟子雖就事論事，皆以格其非心，即誠正之目也。周子著書，首《太極圖》，蓋當聖學不講之後，先示學者道體之大，為上達底止；而《論語》先學習，則下學而上達之意也。牛畜、荀欣、徐越侍，而趙烈侯止歌者之田；竇長君、少君與節行長者居，而皆為退讓君子。大儒薰陶
translation_en:
…and Lin Fang. The Tang relied on the Biographies to confer posthumous titles and include these men among those receiving sacrifices. The Song retained the Tang number and added Qin Zhang, Chen Kang, Shen Cheng, Qu Boyu, and Lin Fang, making eighty-two men; this arrangement has continued to the present. Mencius lived not long after Meng Xianzi, yet of the latter’s five friends he had forgotten three. How much more doubtful, then, is the reliability of Sima Qian’s confused and inconsistent Han scholarship and his book of collected scraps? Confucius called Qu Boyu “Master,” while Gongbo Liao accused Zilu before Jisun: these men probably did not belong among the disciples. Moreover, the Grand Historian himself said that he drew entirely upon the disciples’ questions in the Analects, so it is clear that he had no other definite evidence. Thus, for those not recorded in the Analects, whose ages are unknown and who do not appear in other writings and commentaries, their names cannot be established in detail. Apart from the Analects, what basis is there for investigating the seventy disciples?
When Zhu Xi addressed Emperor Xiaozong, he invariably spoke of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, to the point of being warned that the emperor was tired of hearing it. Yet sincerity and rectification are indeed the foundation of cultivating oneself and bringing forth good government. The king of Qi delighted in valor and music, wealth and women. Although Mencius discussed each matter on its own terms, his purpose throughout was to correct what was wrong in the king’s mind: these were precisely particular applications of sincerity and rectification. Master Zhou placed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate first among his writings. Coming after a period when the learning of the sages had ceased to be expounded, he first showed students the greatness of the substance of the Way, as the ultimate destination of their ascent to higher understanding. The Analects, by contrast, begins with learning and practice, expressing the intention of proceeding from learning below to understanding above. With Niu Xu, Xun Xin, and Xu Yue attending him, Marquis Lie of Zhao abandoned his grant of fields to the singers. Dou Changjun and Dou Shaojun lived among elders of integrity and became modest and deferential gentlemen. The nurturing influence of great Confucian scholars…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
德性之說其此類歟陳蕃不見黄憲鄙吝
復存房琯見紫芝眉宇而名利都盡詩人
秉彜好德之詠於是見矣北軍或右祖則
事必敗蓋此時當驅以義而勃之問謬也
龐涓不燭書則弩不發蓋臏料涓之中智
必看無疑也或謂韓琦文章不逮古人琦
曰歐陽永叔為學士天下文章孰大於是
宰相之度何有人已之間邪或勸范鎮辭
召而鎮曰凡吾所欲為者司馬君實已為
===
之何用復出忠臣之心在利國家而已矣
黄帝教熊羆貔貅貙虎與炎帝戰似不可
信然韓邑驅虎豹犀象助威則擾馴猛獸
古有其術也唐高祖借突厥起兵乃先自
屈若沛公北貉燕人助梟騎則夷狄畏服
唐不可比也井田張子謂處之有術朱子
謂須有機會封建程子謂出於不得已朱
子謂實是不可行肉刑楊龜山論文帝曰
不忍教養而圖其末朱子謂傷肌膚以懲
punctuated:
德性之說，其此類歟？陳蕃不見黄憲，鄙吝復存；房琯見紫芝眉宇，而名利都盡。詩人秉彜好德之詠，於是見矣。北軍或右祖，則事必敗，蓋此時當驅以義，而勃之問謬也。龐涓不燭書，則弩不發，蓋臏料涓之中智，必看無疑也。或謂韓琦文章不逮古人，琦曰：「歐陽永叔為學士，天下文章孰大於是？」宰相之度，何有人已之間邪？或勸范鎮辭召，而鎮曰：「凡吾所欲為者，司馬君實已為之，何用復出？」忠臣之心，在利國家而已矣。
黄帝教熊羆貔貅貙虎，與炎帝戰，似不可信；然韓邑驅虎豹犀象助威，則擾馴猛獸，古有其術也。唐高祖借突厥起兵，乃先自屈；若沛公北貉燕人助梟騎，則夷狄畏服，唐不可比也。井田，張子謂處之有術，朱子謂須有機會；封建，程子謂出於不得已，朱子謂實是不可行；肉刑，楊龜山論文帝曰：「不忍教養而圖其末。」朱子謂傷肌膚以懲
translation_en:
…the account concerning moral nature: would these be examples of it? When Chen Fan had not seen Huang Xian for some time, his narrow-mindedness returned; when Fang Guan saw the countenance of Zizhi [?], all thoughts of fame and profit vanished. Here we see what the poet celebrated as holding fast to the constant moral nature and loving virtue. Had some of the Northern Army supported Zu [?], the undertaking would certainly have failed. At that moment they should have been impelled by righteousness; Bo’s question was therefore mistaken. Had Pang Juan not illuminated the writing, the crossbows would not have fired. But Bin reckoned that Juan, with his middling intelligence, would certainly look at it: there was no doubt. Someone said that Han Qi’s literary compositions fell short of those of the ancients. Qi replied, “Ouyang Yongshu serves as Academician. Whose literary achievement under Heaven surpasses his?” How could a chief councilor’s breadth of mind admit distinctions between others and himself? Someone urged Fan Zhen to decline a summons, but Zhen said, “Everything I wish to accomplish has already been accomplished by Sima Junshi. Why need I return to office?” A loyal minister’s sole concern is to benefit the state.
It seems incredible that the Yellow Emperor trained bears, brown bears, pi, xiu, chu, and tigers to fight the Flame Emperor. Yet in the territory of Han, tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants were driven forth to bolster military might; thus the ancients possessed methods of taming fierce beasts. Gaozu of Tang borrowed the strength of the Tujue to raise his army, first submitting himself to them. In the case of the Duke of Pei, however, the northern Mo and men of Yan furnished support as formidable cavalry: these foreign peoples submitted in awe, and Tang’s case cannot be compared with his. Regarding the well-field system, Master Zhang said that there were methods for implementing it, while Master Zhu said that an opportunity was necessary. Regarding enfeoffment, Master Cheng said that it arose from unavoidable necessity, while Master Zhu said that it was truly impracticable. Regarding corporal mutilation, Yang Guishan said in discussing Emperor Wen, “He could not bear to instruct and nurture them, yet sought to deal with the consequences [?].” Master Zhu said that injuring the skin and flesh to punish…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
惡亦不忍人之政觀此則可復不可復者
審矣郊社周禮天地分祭光武釆元始故
事合之今制亦合祀而燔犢於壇用牲於
屋蓋無泰壇明堂而一也宗廟古者天子
七廟外為都宮內各堂室漢明帝遺詔無
起寢廟後遂為同堂異室之制今
太廟總為一殿即同堂之意也樂律蔡元定欲
求律氣之元以定黃鍾之管以生十一律
舜為蕭韶而儀鳳凰舞百獸者皆是物也
===
今黃冠伶人甚至琴瑟捫而無音鍾磬識
而後擊觀此則有合未有合者明矣薄昭
之死史不言其罪狀李德裕以為於義未
安司馬光以為法無所不行皆無據濮王
之封當稱皇伯父濮國大王司馬光以為
當稱伯歐陽脩以為當稱親皆未安禪乃
佛氏欲其心收斂虛靜有似儒者之敬以
直內而無義以方外其心殆如死灰之不
復然者而儒之心則穀種也丹乃仙侶欲
punctuated: 惡，亦不忍人之政。觀此，則可復不可復者審矣。郊社，《周禮》天地分祭，光武釆元始故事合之，今制亦合祀，而燔犢於壇，用牲於屋，蓋無泰壇、明堂而一也。宗廟，古者天子七廟，外為都宮，內各堂室。漢明帝遺詔無起寢廟，後遂為同堂異室之制。今太廟總為一殿，即同堂之意也。樂律，蔡元定欲求律氣之元，以定黃鍾之管，以生十一律。舜為《蕭韶》，而儀鳳凰、舞百獸者，皆是物也。今黃冠、伶人，甚至琴瑟捫而無音，鍾磬識而後擊。觀此，則有合未有合者明矣。薄昭之死，史不言其罪狀。李德裕以為於義未安，司馬光以為法無所不行，皆無據。濮王之封，當稱皇伯父濮國大王。司馬光以為當稱伯，歐陽脩以為當稱親，皆未安。禪乃佛氏欲其心收斂虛靜，有似儒者之敬以直內，而無義以方外。其心殆如死灰之不復然者，而儒之心則穀種也。丹乃仙侶欲
translation_en:
…evil is also government that cannot bear the suffering of others. From this, it becomes clear which practices can and cannot be restored. As for the suburban sacrifices and sacrifices to the soil, the Rites of Zhou prescribes separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Emperor Guangwu adopted the precedent of the Yuanshi era and combined them. The present regulations likewise provide for joint worship, with a calf burned on the altar and sacrificial animals offered within a building. Apparently, the Great Altar and the Hall of Light are not distinguished, but are treated as one [?]. As for ancestral temples, in antiquity the Son of Heaven had seven temples, enclosed by a common outer wall, each with its own hall and chamber within. Emperor Ming of the Han decreed in his final testament that no resting hall or ancestral temple should be built for him. Thereafter, the system of separate chambers within a shared hall emerged. Today, the Imperial Ancestral Temple consists of a single main hall, embodying this same principle of a shared hall.

As for musical pitch standards, Cai Yuanding sought the source of the vital force governing pitch, in order to establish the Huangzhong pitch pipe and derive the other eleven pitches. When Shun performed the Shao music, bringing phoenixes to appear in stately array and the hundred beasts to dance, it was all through these same things. Today, among Daoist priests and musicians, matters have reached the point where they finger the qin and se zithers without producing sound, and must identify the bells and chime stones before striking them [?]. From this, it is clear where there is conformity and where there is still none.

As for Bo Zhao’s death, the histories do not state the particulars of his crime. Li Deyu considered his death inconsistent with righteousness; Sima Guang held that the law must apply without exception. Neither view has sufficient evidence. As for the title conferred upon the Prince of Pu, he ought to have been called ‘Imperial Elder Paternal Uncle, Great Prince of the State of Pu.’ Sima Guang held that he should be called an uncle; Ouyang Xiu held that he should be called a parent. Neither formulation was satisfactory.

Chan meditation is the Buddhists’ attempt to gather in their minds and make them empty and still. It somewhat resembles the Confucian practice of using reverent attentiveness to straighten the inner self, but lacks righteousness to square outward conduct. Their minds are almost like dead ashes that will never burn again, whereas the Confucian mind is a seed of grain. Elixir-making is the pursuit by adepts of immortality who wish…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其身延年益壽附會醫書之把握陰陽呼
吸精氣不治已病治未病者非真有術以
白日昇天也樂毅圍莒不拔文中子以為
善藏其用然田單能守毅亦不能攻也藺
相如完璧歸趙楊龜山以為不合與秦爭
璧然秦雖强暴相如料其不敢害已也執
事所詢盡於是矣愚復有說焉昔者孔子
以子貢謂已多學而識而曰吾道一以貫
之一者理也一理散在萬事故理亦萬焉
===
不同而不外乎吾之一心學者誠能主敬
以存此心於端莊靜一之中以為窮理之
本則自天地之大古今之變以至一塵之
微一息之頃如鑑至明而照人之妍媸如
衡至平而稱物之輕重其有爽焉者寡矣
豈但如前數端而已哉
第四問
王龍山
同考試官教諭王　批〔據古人見成說話斷今日事而〕
punctuated:
其身延年益壽，附會醫書之「把握陰陽，呼吸精氣」、「不治已病治未病」者，非真有術以白日昇天也。樂毅圍莒不拔，文中子以為善藏其用；然田單能守，毅亦不能攻也。藺相如完璧歸趙，楊龜山以為不合與秦爭璧；然秦雖强暴，相如料其不敢害已也。執事所詢，盡於是矣。愚復有說焉：昔者孔子以子貢謂已多學而識，而曰：「吾道一以貫之。」一者，理也。一理散在萬事，故理亦萬焉，不同而不外乎吾之一心。學者誠能主敬，以存此心於端莊靜一之中，以為窮理之本，則自天地之大、古今之變，以至一塵之微、一息之頃，如鑑至明而照人之妍媸，如衡至平而稱物之輕重，其有爽焉者寡矣。豈但如前數端而已哉？

第四問
王龍山
同考試官教諭王　批〔據古人見成說話斷今日事，而〕
translation_en:
…to prolong their lives and increase their longevity, drawing strained connections with such sayings in medical writings as “grasp yin and yang, breathe essential qi” and “treat illness before it arises, rather than after it has developed.” They do not truly possess an art by which to ascend to Heaven in broad daylight. Yue Yi besieged Ju but did not take it. Master Wenzhong considered him skilled at keeping his abilities concealed; yet Tian Dan was able to defend the city, and Yi was unable to capture it. Lin Xiangru returned the jade disk intact to Zhao. Yang Guishan considered that he ought not to have contested possession of the disk with Qin; yet, although Qin was powerful and violent, Xiangru judged that it would not dare harm him.

This exhausts the matters about which you have inquired. I venture to offer a further observation. Formerly, when Zigong supposed that Confucius had learned much and retained it in memory, Confucius said: “My Way is threaded together by one thing.” That one thing is principle. The single principle is distributed throughout the myriad affairs, and thus principles, too, are myriad and diverse, yet they do not lie outside this single mind of ours. If a learner can truly make reverent attentiveness his guiding practice, preserving this mind in a state of dignity, tranquility, and unity, and taking this as the foundation for investigating principle, then, from the vastness of Heaven and Earth and the changes of past and present down to the minuteness of a speck of dust and the interval of a single breath, his understanding will resemble a perfectly clear mirror reflecting people's beauty and ugliness, or perfectly balanced scales weighing things light and heavy. Instances of error will be few indeed. How could this apply merely to the several matters discussed above?

Fourth Question
Wang Longshan
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔He judges present-day affairs on the basis of the ready-made sayings of the ancients, and…〕

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時出己意亦非鑿空畫餅之言子之志則大矣他日用
於世其可以是措之乎予雖老矣儻及見之豈不一快也哉
考試官學正張　批〔此等論議雖出入史傳然能如此立意而發之筆下他日亦必擔當得起者〕
考試官教授方　批〔讀子是策不覺神爽飛越吁子亦不凡矣〕
對敵有萬變故兵之用有萬變兵有萬變
故將之才亦有萬變將不變則無以用兵
兵不變則無以應敵然將才各有所長善
===
將者就其所長而用之當變則以變為變
不當變則以不變為變勇者不能奪辯者
不能惑君命有不受已身有不恤戰必欲
勝攻必欲取追必欲獲又豈有敗績之虞
哉執事有感於今之事以古之將下詢承
學筆硯書生發緯之不恤恐足以知此然
嘗聞之孫臏救趙直走大梁而魏解邯鄲
之圍救韓直走魏都而龐消去韓歸魏此
所謂攻其無備也非其才之長於擣虛安
punctuated:
時出己意，亦非鑿空畫餅之言。子之志則大矣，他日用於世，其可以是措之乎？予雖老矣，儻及見之，豈不一快也哉！
考試官學正張，批〔此等論議雖出入史傳，然能如此立意而發之筆下，他日亦必擔當得起者。〕
考試官教授方，批〔讀子是策，不覺神爽飛越。吁，子亦不凡矣！〕
對：敵有萬變，故兵之用有萬變；兵有萬變，故將之才亦有萬變。將不變，則無以用兵；兵不變，則無以應敵。然將才各有所長，善將者就其所長而用之。當變，則以變為變；不當變，則以不變為變。勇者不能奪，辯者不能惑，君命有不受，已身有不恤。戰必欲勝，攻必欲取，追必欲獲，又豈有敗績之虞哉！執事有感於今之事，以古之將下詢承學。筆硯書生，發緯之不恤，恐足以知此。然嘗聞之：孫臏救趙，直走大梁，而魏解邯鄲之圍；救韓，直走魏都，而龐消去韓歸魏。此所謂攻其無備也。非其才之長於擣虛，安
translation_en:
…and at times you offer your own views; these, too, are no groundless words or empty promises. Your ambition is indeed great. If you are employed in public service one day, will you be able to put these ideas into practice? Though I am old, should I live to see it, would that not be a great delight!
Examiner Zhang, an instructor, comments: “Although arguments of this kind range through the histories and biographies, someone who can conceive such ideas and express them in writing will surely also be able to shoulder responsibility in the future.”
Examiner Fang, a professor, comments: “Reading this policy essay of yours, I involuntarily felt my spirits refreshed and soaring. Ah, you are indeed no ordinary man!”
In reply: The enemy changes in countless ways; hence the employment of troops must also change in countless ways. Since military operations change in countless ways, a commander's abilities must likewise encompass countless changes. If the commander cannot adapt, he has no means of employing his troops; if the troops cannot adapt, they have no means of responding to the enemy. Yet commanders each have their particular strengths, and one skilled in directing commanders employs them according to those strengths. When change is called for, he adapts by changing; when change is not called for, he adapts by remaining unchanged. The brave cannot shake his resolve, and the eloquent cannot confuse him. There are commands from his sovereign that he will not accept, and occasions when he will disregard his own safety. In battle he is determined to win; in assault, to take his objective; in pursuit, to capture the enemy. What fear of defeat could there then be?
Moved by present affairs, you have condescended to question us students about the commanders of antiquity. A scholar of brush and ink—[the wording here is garbled: 發緯之不恤恐足以知此]—could scarcely know enough of this [?]. Yet I have heard the following: when Sun Bin went to rescue Zhao, he marched directly toward Daliang, and Wei lifted its siege of Handan. When he went to rescue Han, he marched directly toward Wei's capital, and Pang Xiao [?] left Han and returned to Wei. This is what is meant by attacking where the enemy is unprepared. Had his particular talent not lain in striking at undefended points, how could he…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
能再舉而再勝乎韓信陳船臨晉渡軍夏
陽而虜魏王豹萬人背水輕騎立幟而擒
趙王歇囊沙壅水佯敗決囊而擊殺龍且
此所謂出其不意也非其才之長於出奇
安能三戰而三克乎王翦滅楚置郡將六
十萬項羽破秦入關用四十萬長於用多
也謝玄以八千敗苻堅之百萬岳飛以五
百破兀术之十萬長於用少也郭子儀御
下以恕寬厚得人而身為天下安危李廣
===
行無部伍人人自便而未嘗遇害非其用
寬之長寧不驕生而卒不可用邪李光弼
天下服其威名諸將不敢仰視而戰功為
中興第一程不識吏治軍簿軍不得休而
虜不得犯非用嚴之長寧不變生而身且
不保邪漢高以灌嬰將騎而知馮敬不能
當曹參將步而知項它不能當蓋騎乃嬰
之長步乃參之長非後世步騎混殺而苟
為具數者也馬隆討凉州用車且戰且前
punctuated: 能再舉而再勝乎？韓信陳船臨晉，渡軍夏陽而虜魏王豹；萬人背水，輕騎立幟而擒趙王歇；囊沙壅水，佯敗決囊而擊殺龍且。此所謂出其不意也。非其才之長於出奇，安能三戰而三克乎？王翦滅楚置郡，將六十萬；項羽破秦入關，用四十萬：長於用多也。謝玄以八千敗苻堅之百萬，岳飛以五百破兀术之十萬：長於用少也。郭子儀御下以恕，寬厚得人，而身為天下安危；李廣行無部伍，人人自便，而未嘗遇害。非其用寬之長，寧不驕生而卒不可用邪？李光弼，天下服其威名，諸將不敢仰視，而戰功為中興第一；程不識吏治軍簿，軍不得休，而虜不得犯。非用嚴之長，寧不變生而身且不保邪？漢高以灌嬰將騎，而知馮敬不能當；曹參將步，而知項它不能當。蓋騎乃嬰之長，步乃參之長，非後世步騎混殺而苟為具數者也。馬隆討凉州，用車且戰且前。
translation_en: …could he have campaigned twice and won twice? Han Xin arrayed boats at Linjin but crossed his army at Xiayang and captured Bao, King of Wei. He placed ten thousand men with their backs to the river and sent light cavalry to plant his banners, thereby capturing Xie, King of Zhao. He dammed a river with sacks of sand, feigned defeat, and released the dam, thereby attacking and killing Long Ju. This is what is meant by striking where the enemy does not expect it. Had his particular talent not lain in unconventional tactics, how could he have fought three battles and won all three? Wang Jian destroyed Chu and established commanderies, commanding six hundred thousand men; Xiang Yu defeated Qin and entered the passes, employing four hundred thousand. Their strength lay in employing large forces. Xie Xuan defeated Fu Jian’s million with eight thousand; Yue Fei defeated Wuzhu’s hundred thousand with five hundred. Their strength lay in employing small forces. Guo Ziyi treated his subordinates with forbearance and won their allegiance through generosity and kindness; the security or peril of the realm depended on him. When Li Guang marched, his men were not arranged in fixed units, and each acted as he found convenient, yet his army never suffered harm. Had they not excelled in governing leniently, would arrogance not have arisen and rendered their soldiers unusable? All under Heaven acknowledged Li Guangbi’s awe-inspiring reputation; his generals dared not look up at him, and his military achievements ranked first in the dynastic restoration. Cheng Buzhi had his clerks keep military registers, and his troops were given no rest, yet the enemy could not attack them. Had they not excelled in governing strictly, would mutiny not have arisen, leaving even their own lives in danger? Emperor Gao of Han put Guan Ying in command of cavalry and knew that Feng Jing could not withstand him; he put Cao Can in command of infantry and knew that Xiang Ta could not withstand him. Cavalry was Ying’s particular strength, and infantry was Can’s. This was unlike later generations, when infantry and cavalry were thrown together into battle merely to make up the numbers. When Ma Long campaigned against Liangzhou, he employed chariots, fighting as he advanced…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而樹機能不能當隆告其君曰陛下若任
臣當聽臣自任蓋隆自料必能用車取勝
非後世不問其能否而畀之以車者也孫
武斬二隊長而婦人兵整可赴水火穰苴
斬莊賈而三軍之士振慄有人所不及知
者然士有死心敵人先懼其長亦可窺也
若或撓之則氣餒然而不可用矣吳起坐
不設席行不騎乘趙奢進食以十數所友
以百數有人所不能行者然視卒如子好
===
諫而成其長亦可見也若自反之則必欲
然而不能軍矣司馬懿按行營壘而嘆諸
葛孔明為天下奇才霍去病言顧方畧何
如不至學古兵法張巡行兵不依古法雖
皆優於才然去病餘棄粱肉不知省士其
屢建大功真有天幸而有氣敢往志滅匈
奴是其長也巡令本將各以其意教戰使
兵識將意將識士情此又欲諸將咨用其
長則其以孤軍六千而四百餘戰殺賊十
punctuated: 而樹機能不能當。隆告其君曰：「陛下若任臣，當聽臣自任。」蓋隆自料必能用車取勝，非後世不問其能否而畀之以車者也。孫武斬二隊長，而婦人兵整，可赴水火；穰苴斬莊賈，而三軍之士振慄。有人所不及知者，然士有死心，敵人先懼，其長亦可窺也。若或撓之，則氣餒，然而不可用矣。吳起坐不設席，行不騎乘；趙奢進食以十數，所友以百數。有人所不能行者，然視卒如子，好諫而成，其長亦可見也。若自反之，則必欲，然而不能軍矣。司馬懿按行營壘，而嘆諸葛孔明為天下奇才。霍去病言：「顧方畧何如，不至學古兵法。」張巡行兵不依古法。雖皆優於才，然去病餘棄粱肉，不知省士，其屢建大功，真有天幸；而有氣敢往，志滅匈奴，是其長也。巡令本將各以其意教戰，使兵識將意，將識士情，此又欲諸將咨用其長。則其以孤軍六千而四百餘戰，殺賊十
translation_en:
…and Shu Jineng could not withstand him. Ma Long told his ruler: “If Your Majesty entrusts this task to your servant, you must allow your servant to exercise his own judgment.” Long had assessed his own abilities and was certain he could use chariots to win. This was unlike later times, when commanders were given chariots without anyone asking whether they could use them. Sun Wu executed the two company commanders, and his female soldiers became disciplined enough to brave water and fire. Rangju executed Zhuang Jia, and the soldiers of the entire army trembled. There was something here beyond what others could comprehend; yet when soldiers were resolved to die, the enemy was already afraid. Their particular strengths can thus be discerned. If someone interfered with them, their spirit would flag and they could no longer be employed effectively. Wu Qi sat without having a mat laid out and traveled without riding. Those who presented food to Zhao She numbered in the tens, and those he befriended numbered in the hundreds. There was something here that others could not put into practice; yet they regarded their soldiers as sons and welcomed remonstrance, thereby achieving success. Their particular strengths can likewise be seen. If they themselves acted contrary to this, they would necessarily succumb to desire [?] and could no longer command an army.

Sima Yi inspected the camps and fortifications and marveled that Zhuge Kongming was an extraordinary talent under Heaven. Huo Qubing said: “It is simply a matter of what one's strategy is like; there is no need to study ancient military methods.” Zhang Xun conducted campaigns without following ancient methods. Although all were outstanding in talent, Qubing discarded leftover fine grain and meat and did not know to attend to his soldiers' needs. His repeated great achievements truly owed something to Heaven's favor. Yet he had the spirit to advance boldly and the determination to destroy the Xiongnu: these were his strengths. Xun ordered the commanders under him each to train their troops for battle according to their own judgment, so that soldiers would understand their commanders' intentions and commanders would understand their soldiers' feelings. Here again, he wanted his commanders to make use of their respective strengths. Thus, with an isolated force of six thousand, he fought more than four hundred engagements and killed rebels numbering ten…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
二萬人非偶然也不自用其長而又用人
之長以為長也孔明則異於是用兵貴服
人之心而不尚勇力貴萬全之計而不為
僥倖寧乏糧退師而不肯取之百姓寧身
勞細務而不忍使一物失所若原上之星
未墜渭南之軍得戰則取中原如反掌耳
蓋孔明之師庶幾仁義而不可以才之短
長論也夫孔明不可尚矣然萬古此天地
萬古此人物其餘諸將今豈無若人者哉
===
漢武征伐而衛霍之徒出建紹百戰而張
韓之輩顯未聞求將於異代也但御之不
得其道耳御之之道賞罰是也賞罰者軍法
也天德交兵僅餘一弓而唐憲宗不知南
詔追擊全軍皆沒而楊國忠奏捷如此而
欲求如李牧劉錡者豈可得也子反敗績
而自殺括母先言而不坐覆軍者必誅其
身且及其族軍法之來尚矣往歲疆埸不
慎胡騎縱橫將兵者此曰虜之入非吾地
punctuated:
二萬人，非偶然也。不自用其長，而又用人之長以為長也。孔明則異於是：用兵貴服人之心，而不尚勇力；貴萬全之計，而不為僥倖。寧乏糧退師，而不肯取之百姓；寧身勞細務，而不忍使一物失所。若原上之星未墜，渭南之軍得戰，則取中原如反掌耳。蓋孔明之師庶幾仁義，而不可以才之短長論也。夫孔明不可尚矣，然萬古此天地，萬古此人物，其餘諸將，今豈無若人者哉？
漢武征伐，而衛霍之徒出；建紹百戰，而張韓之輩顯。未聞求將於異代也，但御之不得其道耳。御之之道，賞罰是也。賞罰者，軍法也。天德交兵，僅餘一弓，而唐憲宗不知；南詔追擊，全軍皆沒，而楊國忠奏捷。如此而欲求如李牧、劉錡者，豈可得也？子反敗績而自殺，括母先言而不坐。覆軍者必誅其身，且及其族，軍法之來尚矣。往歲疆埸不慎，胡騎縱橫，將兵者，此曰：「虜之入，非吾地
translation_en:
…the killing of 120,000 men was no accident. He did not rely solely on his own strengths, but also made others’ strengths his own. Kongming was different. In warfare, he prized winning people’s hearts rather than valor and force; he prized plans that ensured complete success rather than gambling on good fortune. He would sooner withdraw his army for lack of provisions than take supplies from the common people; he would sooner wear himself out over small tasks than allow even a single creature to lose its proper place. Had the star above the plain not fallen, and had his army south of the Wei River been able to engage in battle, taking the Central Plain would have been as easy as turning his palm. Kongming’s army came close to embodying benevolence and righteousness; it cannot be judged merely in terms of the strengths and weaknesses of his abilities. Kongming, indeed, cannot be surpassed. Yet throughout the ages, heaven and earth remain the same, and so does humankind. As for the other generals, could there be no men like them today?
When Emperor Wu of Han undertook his campaigns, men such as Wei Qing and Huo Qubing emerged; amid the many battles of the Jianyan and Shaoxing eras, men such as Zhang Jun and Han Shizhong distinguished themselves. Never have we heard of seeking generals in another age. The problem is simply a failure to direct them properly. The way to direct them is through rewards and punishments. Rewards and punishments constitute military law. When the Tiande forces fought, only a single bow remained, yet Emperor Xianzong of Tang knew nothing of it. When Nanzhao pursued and attacked, the entire army was destroyed, yet Yang Guozhong reported a victory. Under such circumstances, how could one hope to obtain men like Li Mu and Liu Qi? Zifan killed himself after his defeat; Zhao Kuo’s mother, having spoken beforehand, escaped punishment. A commander who loses an army must himself be executed, and punishment extends to his kin: military law has a long history. In past years, the frontier was inadequately guarded, and non-Chinese cavalry ranged freely. Among those commanding troops, one would say: “The territory the raiders have entered is not mine…”

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也彼曰吾之計在城守也今日曰彼衆我
寡吾圖以全師復
命敵勢方張不可戰也明日曰一日二日彼將
以力疲自去天時不利不可出也小勝掠
其功於已大敗分其罪於人竟未有一如
李光弼納靴中之刀示士卒必死將士一
心上下相救而建牧鋳之功者非真無才
也非其才真無一長之可試也田單黄金
横帶騁乎淄澠之間有生之樂無死之心
===
而攻狄三月不下蓋將一人耳若軍法不
足以制之則誰肯犯危涉險而試非所嘗
試之才乎然則雖有其才自不敢保其必
勝但互相戒以縱使無功得免罪巳足聞
戰鼙而神驚望敵塵而色變可勝嘆哉今
擇將者必須論其才之所長如能將步者
不强之以騎能將騎者不强之以步能將
步若騎者不强之以車能將車者不强之
以步以騎以至寬嚴多少及有他長論之
punctuated: 也。彼曰：「吾之計在城守也。」今日曰：「彼衆我寡，吾圖以全師復命；敵勢方張，不可戰也。」明日曰：「一日二日，彼將以力疲自去；天時不利，不可出也。」小勝，掠其功於已；大敗，分其罪於人。竟未有一如李光弼納靴中之刀，示士卒必死，將士一心，上下相救，而建牧鋳之功者。非真無才也，非其才真無一長之可試也。田單黄金横帶，騁乎淄澠之間，有生之樂，無死之心，而攻狄三月不下。蓋將一人耳，若軍法不足以制之，則誰肯犯危涉險，而試非所嘗試之才乎？然則雖有其才，自不敢保其必勝，但互相戒以「縱使無功，得免罪巳足」。聞戰鼙而神驚，望敵塵而色變，可勝嘆哉！今擇將者，必須論其才之所長。如能將步者，不强之以騎；能將騎者，不强之以步；能將步若騎者，不强之以車；能將車者，不强之以步、以騎。以至寬嚴、多少，及有他長，論之
translation_en: …so it is. Another says, “My strategy is to defend the city.” Today they say, “They are many and we are few. I intend to preserve the army intact and return to report on my commission. The enemy’s strength is at its height; we cannot fight.” Tomorrow they say, “In a day or two, they will exhaust themselves and withdraw. Conditions are unfavorable; we cannot march out.” When there is a small victory, they appropriate its credit; when there is a great defeat, they share out the blame among others. In the end, not one has emulated Li Guangbi, who kept a knife in his boot to show his soldiers his resolve to die, so that commanders and soldiers were of one mind, superiors and subordinates supported one another, and achievements like those of Li Mu and Liu Qi [?] were accomplished. It is not that they truly lack ability, nor that their abilities truly offer not a single strength that could be put to the test. Tian Dan, with gold belted across his waist, rode about between the Zi and Mian rivers, enjoying life and having no resolve to die; he attacked Di for three months without taking it. A commander, after all, is only a man. If military law is insufficient to restrain him, who will willingly brave danger and venture into peril to test abilities he has never yet tested? Thus, even if they possess ability, they dare not assure themselves of certain victory, but merely caution one another: “Even if we achieve nothing, it is enough to escape punishment.” At the sound of the war drums their spirits quake; at the sight of dust raised by the enemy their faces change color. Can one lament this enough? Those who now select commanders must assess where their abilities lie. A man capable of commanding infantry should not be forced to command cavalry; one capable of commanding cavalry should not be forced to command infantry. One capable of commanding infantry or cavalry should not be forced to command chariots; one capable of commanding chariots should not be forced to command infantry or cavalry. As for leniency or strictness, large or small numbers of troops, and any other strengths, their assessment …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
必精務在舍其所短而不委以所不能論
定然後用之將既將則必專其權不必主
之中貴使心有所恃以爲窟穴之地不必
衆之文臣使責有所分以爲解說之機畀
之以全軍寄之以全地戰勝則上賞事敗
則顯戮寵之渥人人自愛罰之嚴人人知
懼又誰肯不思惟計慮於平日而奮勇竭
力於接戰之時以求生於必死之地哉將
者三軍之心心怯則四肢靡心勇則四肢
===
强將有必死之心則三軍操刀必割執斧
必伐止如堵墻動如風雨聞命而感槩激
厲如坐漏船之中伏燒屋之下其有不隨
將以致死者哉故愚以爲今日無將乃軍
法之未講而非人之才不古若也此乃天
下之公言愚不自揆敢告執事幸勿誚之
曰是狂生也
第五問
蹇賢
punctuated:
必精，務在舍其所短，而不委以所不能。論定，然後用之。將既將，則必專其權，不必主之中貴，使心有所恃，以爲窟穴之地；不必衆之文臣，使責有所分，以爲解說之機。畀之以全軍，寄之以全地，戰勝則上賞，事敗則顯戮。寵之渥，人人自愛；罰之嚴，人人知懼。又誰肯不思惟計慮於平日，而奮勇竭力於接戰之時，以求生於必死之地哉？將者，三軍之心。心怯則四肢靡，心勇則四肢强。將有必死之心，則三軍操刀必割，執斧必伐，止如堵墻，動如風雨，聞命而感槩激厲，如坐漏船之中，伏燒屋之下，其有不隨將以致死者哉？故愚以爲今日無將，乃軍法之未講，而非人之才不古若也。此乃天下之公言，愚不自揆，敢告執事，幸勿誚之曰：「是狂生也。」

第五問

蹇賢
translation_en:
…the assessment must be meticulous, with every effort made to set aside their weaknesses and not entrust them with tasks beyond their abilities. Only after this assessment is settled should they be employed. Once a commander has been placed in command, his authority must be undivided. There is no need to place a palace eunuch over him, giving him someone to rely upon as a refuge; nor is there any need to surround him with civil officials, dividing responsibility and giving him an opportunity to make excuses. Entrust him with the entire army and commit the whole territory to his charge. If he wins in battle, grant him the highest reward; if his undertaking fails, execute him publicly. When favor is generous, everyone will value his own life; when punishment is severe, everyone will know fear. Who, then, would fail to deliberate and plan in ordinary times, and to summon his courage and exert his utmost when battle comes, seeking survival in a situation of certain death?

The commander is the heart of the army. If the heart is timid, the four limbs falter; if the heart is courageous, the four limbs are strong. If the commander is resolved to die, then the soldiers of the entire army will surely cut when they take up their knives and surely hew when they grasp their axes. At rest they will be like a wall; in motion, like wind and rain. On hearing an order, they will be stirred to impassioned resolve, as though sitting in a leaking boat or crouching beneath a burning roof. Would any of them fail to follow their commander to the death?

Thus, in my humble view, the present lack of commanders results from a failure to give due attention to military discipline, not from people's abilities falling short of those of antiquity. This is the common judgment of all under Heaven. Without properly measuring my own limitations, I venture to address you, and hope that you will not mock me, saying, “This is a reckless scholar.”

Fifth Question

Jian Xian

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正張　批〔近日各邊兵惟務多而不知練間知練兵者又不知習馬且士卒不畏將令騎兵〕
〔但以具數敵來將何以戰此策有議論有斷制其言〕
〔鑿鑿可行孰謂科目不足以得人耶〕
考試官教授方　批〔得此策快誦數過令人歆羨〕
〔生故識時務者在俊傑敢謂秦無人〕
對兵在精用兵在令之行不然雖百萬將
何益馬在習用馬在卒之能不然雖一二
亦為累蓋兵精則擊刺進退無不閑習令
===
行則無鼓之不前金之不卻者矣馬習則
不至外强中乾進退不可卒能則惟所納
之無不如志矣反是兵雖多不為用馬雖
多反為累比年千里餽粮而村落半空數
月供億而府庫皆罄卒未繫單于之頸而
犂幕南之庭者職是之故也兵馬之事愚
未之學然為地方之切患執事有問不敢
不盡焉且陝西昔人以為天下之首者盖
以强弓健馬胥此焉出而人尚勇樂鬬忘
punctuated:
考試官學正張　批〔近日各邊兵惟務多而不知練，間知練兵者，又不知習馬。且士卒不畏將令，騎兵〕〔但以具數，敵來將何以戰？此策有議論，有斷制，其言〕〔鑿鑿可行，孰謂科目不足以得人耶？〕
考試官教授方　批〔得此策，快誦數過，令人歆羨。〕〔生故識時務者在俊傑，敢謂秦無人？〕
對：兵在精，用兵在令之行。不然，雖百萬，將何益？馬在習，用馬在卒之能。不然，雖一二，亦為累。蓋兵精則擊刺進退無不閑習；令行則無鼓之不前、金之不卻者矣。馬習則不至外强中乾，進退不可；卒能則惟所納之，無不如志矣。反是，兵雖多不為用，馬雖多反為累。比年千里餽粮而村落半空，數月供億而府庫皆罄，卒未繫單于之頸而犂幕南之庭者，職是之故也。兵馬之事，愚未之學，然為地方之切患，執事有問，不敢不盡焉。且陝西昔人以為天下之首者，盖以强弓健馬胥此焉出，而人尚勇樂鬬，忘
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Recently, troops along all the frontiers have sought only greater numbers, without understanding training. Even those who occasionally understand training troops do not understand schooling horses. Moreover, the soldiers do not fear their commanders’ orders, and the cavalry〕〔merely make up the required numbers. When the enemy comes, how will they fight? This policy essay offers reasoned discussion and decisive judgments; its proposals〕〔are cogent and practicable. Who says that the examination system cannot obtain capable men?〕
Examiner Fang, Professor, comments: 〔On receiving this policy essay, I delightedly read it aloud several times. It inspires admiration.〕〔This candidate is indeed an outstanding talent who understands the needs of the times [?]. Who would dare say that Qin has no capable men?〕
In reply: What matters in troops is their quality; what matters in employing them is that orders are carried out. Otherwise, what use would even a million be? What matters in horses is their training; what matters in employing them is the soldiers’ skill. Otherwise, even one or two become a burden. For when troops are well trained, they are thoroughly practiced in striking, thrusting, advancing, and withdrawing. When orders are carried out, none fail to advance at the drum or withdraw at the gong. When horses are schooled, they will not merely look strong while lacking stamina, unable to advance or withdraw. When soldiers are skilled, wherever they direct their mounts, everything accords with their intentions. Conversely, however numerous the troops, they are of no use; however numerous the horses, they instead become a burden. In recent years, grain has been transported a thousand li, leaving villages half empty; only a few months of provisioning have exhausted the government treasuries. Yet in the end we have neither bound the Chanyu by the neck nor ploughed up his court south of the desert. This is precisely the reason.
I have not studied military affairs, but since they are an urgent concern for this region, and you, gentlemen, have posed the question, I dare not withhold any of my thoughts. Now, people of old regarded Shaanxi as the head of the realm because powerful bows and sturdy horses alike came from there, while its people prized courage, delighted in combat, and forgot…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
生輕死諸羌繞其西匈奴瞰其北形勝甲
於他處山川足以自固當如人首之常置
於高且安之地以起天下之脊也我
太祖高皇帝北走胡元乃設大同宣府甘肅遼
東大寧五鎮以禦之永樂以來一華大寧
而增寧夏再棄東勝而守榆林防胡大鎮
六陝西有其三於是遂重於天下矣每鎮
有主將以統治而若城若堡則偏裨以下
居焉大小相維聲勢聯絡兵之充足勇健
===
他鎮未能或之先也今困於擅科困於私
役困於治裝買馬復加以逃故則虛其尺
伍者十之三四矣其馬則以減芻秣耗以
私差遣耗以被擄掠耗復加以病瘵則失
其額籍者十之八九矣近者胡虜分寇我
榆林而肆掠無阻深入我固原而長驅莫
禦論者曰軍少也馬少也墩臺城堡各有
守望巡鎮諸將各有統領兵分而力寡曰
軍少誠是也
punctuated:
生輕死。諸羌繞其西，匈奴瞰其北，形勝甲於他處，山川足以自固，當如人首之常置於高且安之地，以起天下之脊也。我太祖高皇帝北走胡元，乃設大同、宣府、甘肅、遼東、大寧五鎮以禦之。永樂以來，一華大寧而增寧夏，再棄東勝而守榆林。防胡大鎮六，陝西有其三，於是遂重於天下矣。每鎮有主將以統治，而若城若堡，則偏裨以下居焉。大小相維，聲勢聯絡，兵之充足勇健，他鎮未能或之先也。

今困於擅科，困於私役，困於治裝買馬，復加以逃故，則虛其尺伍者十之三四矣。其馬則以減芻秣耗，以私差遣耗，以被擄掠耗，復加以病瘵，則失其額籍者十之八九矣。近者胡虜分寇我榆林，而肆掠無阻；深入我固原，而長驅莫禦。論者曰：「軍少也，馬少也。」墩臺城堡各有守望，巡鎮諸將各有統領，兵分而力寡，曰軍少，誠是也。
translation_en:
…disregard life and hold death lightly. The various Qiang peoples surround its west, and the Xiongnu look down upon its north. Its strategic terrain surpasses that of other places, and its mountains and rivers suffice for its defense. Like a person's head, it should always be kept in a high and secure position, thereby holding upright the backbone of the realm. Our Emperor Taizu Gao drove the Mongol Yuan northward and then established the five defense commands of Datong, Xuanfu, Gansu, Liaodong, and Daning to ward them off. Since the Yongle reign, Daning was first abandoned [?] and Ningxia added; subsequently Dongsheng was abandoned and Yulin defended instead. Of the six great defense commands guarding against the northern peoples, Shaanxi possesses three, and thus came to hold great importance throughout the realm. Each command has a commanding general to exercise overall control, while subordinate generals and officers below them occupy the walled towns and forts. Large and small installations support one another, their military strength and influence forming an interconnected whole. In the fullness of their troop complements and the courage and vigor of their soldiers, no other command could surpass them.

Now, however, the soldiers suffer from unauthorized levies, compulsory service for private purposes, and the expense of procuring equipment and buying horses. Desertions and deaths compound these burdens, leaving three or four places in every ten vacant in their ranks [?]. Their horses are depleted by reductions in hay and grain, by deployment on private errands, and by capture in raids. With sickness added to these losses, eight or nine out of every ten horses on the authorized registers are missing. Recently, the northern raiders attacked our Yulin in separate forces and plundered at will without obstruction; they penetrated deep into our Guyuan and advanced unchecked, with none to resist them. Commentators say: “There are too few soldiers and too few horses.” The watchtowers, walled towns, and forts each require guards and lookouts, and the various generals on patrol and in garrison each have troops under their command. The troops are dispersed and their strength diminished: to say that there are too few soldiers is indeed correct.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷屢詔巡撫官稽僉舍餘而未足嘗
遣廷臣以募軍矣然一時取盈或老羸之相
雜或名姓之作姦或非土著得賞遂逋或
無戶籍既死即缺其存者衣糧徒費技藝
茫然未審臨敵果可用否也調遣之不時
至追逐之不能前百里趨利徒每後期曰
馬少誠是也
朝廷屢詔鎮巡官買補又出太僕銀易買而
未足今
===
簡大臣以督馬矣然百年廢政或市於夷買
於民而給地募軍以牧之或補已死計方
生而作廐展營以居之官或興土木之役
民未免愁嘆之聲不知馬盛果得用否也
且軍多莫過於京營然所至束手而哺於
人未嘗有冒刃陷陳之功軍何必多乎馬
多莫過於山東河南兩畿然孳牧寄養徒
遺小民之困給俵騎操秪為姦猾之資馬
何必多乎稽之古漢築五原塞外列城而
punctuated: 朝廷屢詔巡撫官稽僉舍餘而未足，嘗遣廷臣以募軍矣。然一時取盈，或老羸之相雜，或名姓之作姦，或非土著，得賞遂逋，或無戶籍，既死即缺。其存者，衣糧徒費，技藝茫然，未審臨敵果可用否也。調遣之不時至，追逐之不能前，百里趨利，徒每後期。曰馬少，誠是也。朝廷屢詔鎮巡官買補，又出太僕銀易買而未足，今簡大臣以督馬矣。然百年廢政，或市於夷、買於民，而給地募軍以牧之；或補已死、計方生，而作廐展營以居之。官或興土木之役，民未免愁嘆之聲，不知馬盛果得用否也。且軍多莫過於京營，然所至束手而哺於人，未嘗有冒刃陷陳之功，軍何必多乎？馬多莫過於山東、河南、兩畿，然孳牧寄養，徒遺小民之困；給俵騎操，秪為姦猾之資，馬何必多乎？稽之古，漢築五原塞外列城而
translation_en: The court has repeatedly ordered the grand coordinators to inspect and conscript the sons and younger relatives of military households and their surplus males, yet these have proved insufficient; it has also dispatched court officials to recruit soldiers. But in hastily filling the quotas, some recruits are old or infirm, some enlist under fraudulent names, some are not local residents and abscond as soon as they receive their rewards, and some have no household registration, leaving vacancies upon their deaths. Those who remain merely consume clothing and grain, with no understanding of military skills. It is uncertain whether they can actually be used against the enemy. When dispatched, they fail to arrive on time; in pursuit, they cannot advance; racing a hundred li to seize an advantage, they invariably arrive too late. To say that horses are too few is indeed correct. The court has repeatedly ordered the regional commanders and grand coordinators to purchase replacements, and has also disbursed silver from the Court of the Imperial Stud to buy them. Yet these have proved insufficient, and it has now selected high ministers to supervise horse administration. But this administration has been neglected for a hundred years. Horses may be bought from the non-Chinese peoples or from the common people, with land allotted and soldiers recruited to pasture them; dead horses may be replaced and anticipated births counted, with stables built and camps enlarged to house them. Officials may initiate construction projects, while the people cannot escape occasions for grief and lamentation. It is uncertain whether abundant horses will actually prove usable. Moreover, nowhere are troops more numerous than in the capital camps; yet wherever they go, they stand helpless and depend on others to feed them. They have never accomplished feats of braving blades and breaking enemy formations. Why must troops be numerous? Nowhere are horses more numerous than in Shandong, Henan, and the two metropolitan regions; yet breeding them and entrusting them to households for rearing merely burden the common people. Distributing them for riding and drill only supplies opportunities for the unscrupulous. Why must horses be numerous? Examining antiquity, we find that the Han built a series of fortified towns beyond the frontier at Wuyuan, and…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
烽火候望精明匈奴寇邊少利希復犯塞
宋以趙贊屯延州姚内斌守慶州董遵誨
屯環州馮繼業鎮靈武而養募間諜寇至
先知設伏掩擊多致克捷此非當時將令
素行而兵無不精安能使候望者致精明
之勤間諜者有察敵之審而又能使寇而
少利戰而多捷耶練兵不至雖有鐵馬徒
瘠吾民故范延光言養馬太多虛耗國力
與虜相攻非深入窮追故宋祁言馬少則
===
騎精步多則闘健此非真見卒在能騎而
馬必須習豈敢以養馬耗國歸咎於練兵
不至而又以騎精歸之馬少且馬少反有
步多闘健之益耶夫虜盜賊之智耳每聚
犬羊之衆竊窺藩籬之外然亦豈敢肆然
相隨而入我疆場哉其來也必導以擄叛
之我民探我整怠先以數十之零騎試我
勇怯若望之審而知之豫步兵有畏將畏
法之心騎兵有且馳且射之材則麾而卻
punctuated: 烽火候望精明，匈奴寇邊少利，希復犯塞。宋以趙贊屯延州，姚内斌守慶州，董遵誨屯環州，馮繼業鎮靈武，而養募間諜，寇至先知，設伏掩擊，多致克捷。此非當時將令素行而兵無不精，安能使候望者致精明之勤，間諜者有察敵之審，而又能使寇而少利、戰而多捷耶？練兵不至，雖有鐵馬，徒瘠吾民。故范延光言：「養馬太多，虛耗國力。」與虜相攻，非深入窮追，故宋祁言：「馬少則騎精，步多則闘健。」此非真見卒在能騎而馬必須習，豈敢以養馬耗國歸咎於練兵不至，而又以騎精歸之馬少，且馬少反有步多闘健之益耶？夫虜，盜賊之智耳，每聚犬羊之衆，竊窺藩籬之外，然亦豈敢肆然相隨而入我疆場哉？其來也，必導以擄叛之我民，探我整怠，先以數十之零騎試我勇怯。若望之審而知之豫，步兵有畏將畏法之心，騎兵有且馳且射之材，則麾而卻
translation_en:
…the beacon signals and lookout service were vigilant and discerning; the Xiongnu gained little from raiding the frontier and seldom violated the passes again. Under the Song, Zhao Zan was stationed at Yanzhou, Yao Neibin defended Qingzhou, Dong Zunhui was stationed at Huanzhou, and Feng Jiye guarded Lingwu. They recruited and maintained spies, learned beforehand when raiders were coming, and laid ambushes to attack them by surprise, frequently securing victories. Had commanders’ orders not been consistently obeyed and the troops uniformly proficient at that time, how could they have made the lookouts exercise such vigilant diligence and the spies investigate the enemy so accurately, while also ensuring that raids brought the enemy little profit and battles brought frequent victories?

If troops are inadequately trained, even having armored horses merely impoverishes our people. Thus Fan Yanguang said: “Keeping too many horses needlessly drains the strength of the state.” Fighting the northern foes does not entail penetrating deep into their territory and pursuing them to the utmost. Thus Song Qi said: “When horses are few, the cavalry is proficient; when infantry is numerous, it fights vigorously.” Had they not truly understood that what matters is soldiers’ ability to ride and that horses must be trained, how could they have attributed the drain on the state from keeping horses to inadequate military training, and further attributed cavalry proficiency to having few horses, asserting moreover that fewer horses actually bring the benefit of more infantry fighting vigorously?

These foes possess only the cunning of thieves and bandits. They repeatedly gather their dog-and-sheep hordes and furtively peer in from beyond our fences; yet how would they dare follow one another brazenly into our territory? When they come, they invariably take as guides people of ours who have been captured or have defected [?], to discover whether we are prepared or negligent. First they use a scattered contingent of a few dozen horsemen to test our courage or cowardice. If our observation is careful and our knowledge obtained beforehand, if the infantry fear their commanders and the law, and if the cavalry have the skill to shoot while riding, then, with a wave of the command flag, we can drive back…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之追而擒之逐而出之不難矣前既不利
後雖千萬亦引而遁矣為今之計兵之技
或弓矢刀斧焉或矛盾鎗銃焉務各專其
一而必得其巧如射則發必命中不能射
者習他技他技亦然乘高而失望者必誅
有敵而失哨者必誅交鋒而不前者必誅
黜姑息之説作勇敢之氣若馬則用其健
者而習其馳逐閑其進止卒能乘者給為
騎兵不能者勿强與夫馬未必皆可戰而
===
卒亦未必皆善乘故以曹操用兵如神而
呂布不許其將騎馬豈易言者哉況小弱
之人一槩乘之以馬遇敵則狡者走而愚
者死矣兵之技既精而將令無不行馬之
性既習而騎卒無不能此克用騎軍三千
所以當時兵勢最强而吳起人馬相親告
文侯以横行天下也如是將見氈毳之徒
聞風而懼帖耳而遁非喘息於翰海之濵
則跧伏於陰山之窟矣尚何侵擾之足慮
punctuated: 之，追而擒之，逐而出之，不難矣。前既不利，後雖千萬，亦引而遁矣。為今之計，兵之技，或弓矢刀斧焉，或矛盾鎗銃焉，務各專其一而必得其巧。如射，則發必命中；不能射者，習他技，他技亦然。乘高而失望者必誅，有敵而失哨者必誅，交鋒而不前者必誅。黜姑息之説，作勇敢之氣。若馬，則用其健者，而習其馳逐，閑其進止。卒能乘者，給為騎兵；不能者，勿强與。夫馬未必皆可戰，而卒亦未必皆善乘，故以曹操用兵如神，而呂布不許其將騎，馬豈易言者哉？況小弱之人，一槩乘之以馬，遇敵則狡者走而愚者死矣。兵之技既精，而將令無不行；馬之性既習，而騎卒無不能。此克用騎軍三千所以當時兵勢最强，而吳起人馬相親，告文侯以横行天下也。如是，將見氈毳之徒聞風而懼，帖耳而遁，非喘息於翰海之濵，則跧伏於陰山之窟矣。尚何侵擾之足慮
translation_en:
…them; pursuing and capturing them, and driving them out, would not be difficult. Once their advance force has met with failure, those behind, even in their thousands and tens of thousands, will also withdraw and flee. For present purposes, soldiers must each specialize in one skill—whether with bows and arrows, sabers and axes, spears and shields, or lances and firearms—and thoroughly master it. In archery, for example, every shot must hit its mark. Those unable to shoot should practice another skill, to which the same requirement applies. Those stationed on high ground who fail to keep watch must be executed; those who fail to give warning when an enemy is present must be executed; those who fail to advance when battle is joined must be executed. Reject arguments for indulgence and rouse a spirit of courage.

As for horses, use the robust ones, train them to gallop and pursue, and school them in advancing and halting. Give them to soldiers who can ride, to serve as cavalry; do not force them upon those who cannot. Not every horse is necessarily fit for battle, nor is every soldier necessarily a skilled rider. Thus, although Cao Cao employed troops with godlike mastery, Lü Bu did not concede his ability to command cavalry. Can the use of horses be treated lightly? Moreover, if men who are small and weak are indiscriminately mounted on horses, then upon meeting the enemy the cunning will flee and the foolish will die.

Once the soldiers have mastered their skills, every command of their generals will be carried out; once the horses have been schooled in their dispositions, every cavalryman will be capable. This is why Keyong’s cavalry force of three thousand was the strongest military force of its time, and why Wu Qi, with men and horses accustomed to one another, told Marquis Wen that he could range unopposed throughout the realm. If this is done, we shall see those clad in felt and fur take fright at the mere news and flee with ears laid back in submission. They will either gasp for breath at the edge of the Hanhai desert or crouch in hiding in the caverns of the Yinshan mountains. What cause would then remain to fear their incursions…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
哉又何必爲益軍增馬之擾哉愚見如此
執事倘以爲有可采轉而聞之於
上未必無小補也
punctuated: 哉！又何必爲益軍增馬之擾哉？愚見如此，執事倘以爲有可采，轉而聞之於上，未必無小補也。
translation_en: …be cause for concern! And why incur the disruption of increasing troops and adding horses? Such is my humble view. If you, sir, consider anything in it worthy of adoption and convey it to His Majesty, it might be of some small benefit.

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試録後序
弘治甲子當大比〔𦍒〕不佞獲
從鄉大夫後以觀於關中之
文乃竊嘆曰美哉文乎其我
國家百年之所養者乎土之積
不厚而草樹之不茂山之積
不厚而雲雨之不廣士之養
===
不厚而英華之不著然兹土
也文王之所化也自蒙古未
北腥膻之與居射獵之與遊
戎馬之與馳逐尚勇力棄詩
書之與朝夕典籍學士遷而
之他故家遺風蕩無存者文
之厄也極矣我
punctuated:
陝西鄉試録後序

弘治甲子當大比，〔𦍒〕不佞獲從鄉大夫後，以觀於關中之文，乃竊嘆曰：「美哉，文乎！其我國家百年之所養者乎！」土之積不厚，而草樹之不茂；山之積不厚，而雲雨之不廣；士之養不厚，而英華之不著。然兹土也，文王之所化也。自蒙古未北，腥膻之與居，射獵之與遊，戎馬之與馳逐，尚勇力、棄詩書之與朝夕。典籍學士遷而之他，故家遺風蕩無存者，文之厄也極矣。我…
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year of the Hongzhi reign [1504], when the triennial examination was held, I was fortunate [?] enough, unworthy though I am, to follow in the company of the local dignitaries and observe the literary work of Guanzhong. I could not help exclaiming to myself: “How splendid this writing is! Surely it is the fruit of a hundred years of cultivation by our dynasty!” Unless soil accumulates deeply, grasses and trees cannot flourish; unless mountains rise in substantial masses, clouds and rain cannot spread far; unless scholars are nurtured abundantly, their finest talents cannot become manifest.

Yet this land was once transformed by King Wen’s civilizing influence. In the days before the Mongols withdrew northward, its people lived amid the rank smell of meat and mutton, took their recreation in archery and hunting, and raced about on warhorses; day after day they prized courage and physical strength and discarded the Odes and Documents. Classical books and learned scholars moved elsewhere, and the traditions bequeathed by old established families were swept away without a trace. The calamity that befell literary culture had reached its utmost extent. Our…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝起而挈以復周邦之
舊德教之所衣被禮樂之所
陶濡詩書之所漸摩百有餘
年而文之盛至與天下爭雄
角勝未知孰先而孰後也雖
然此所謂文以言之成章而
名之文非文之全體也言之
===
文有出於德有出於才有出
於習者出於德若典謨訓誥
是也出於才若屈平之騷韓
愈歐陽修諸君子之作是也
出於習若戰國之辯六朝之
賦晚唐之詩及朱子所論東
晉之末其文一切含胡又言
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝起而挈以復周邦之舊，德教之所衣被，禮樂之所陶濡，詩書之所漸摩，百有餘年，而文之盛至與天下爭雄角勝，未知孰先而孰後也。
雖然，此所謂文，以言之成章而名之文，非文之全體也。言之文，有出於德，有出於才，有出於習者。出於德，若典謨訓誥是也；出於才，若屈平之騷、韓愈、歐陽修諸君子之作是也；出於習，若戰國之辯、六朝之賦、晚唐之詩，及朱子所論東晉之末，其文一切含胡，又言：
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao arose and led this land back to the ancient ways of the Zhou realm. Enveloped by moral instruction, nurtured by rites and music, and gradually cultivated through the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents for more than a hundred years, its literary culture has flourished to the point that it rivals all other regions of the empire, with no knowing which stands ahead and which behind.
Yet what is called “wen” here is writing so named because its words form an accomplished composition; it is not wen—cultural refinement—in its entirety. Literary expression may arise from virtue, from talent, or from acquired practice. That arising from virtue is exemplified by the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents. That arising from talent is exemplified by Qu Ping’s Encountering Sorrow (Li Sao) and the works of such gentlemen as Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu. That arising from acquired practice is exemplified by the disputations of the Warring States, the rhapsodies of the Six Dynasties, and the poetry of the late Tang, as well as what Master Zhu said of the closing years of the Eastern Jin: its writing was all vague and indistinct. He further said: …

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
專做時文人只就紙上説是
也文之全體則孔子所論與
不與而歸之天者是也諸士
子今日之文其出於德乎出
於才乎出於習乎玉光珠彩
炫乎吾前求而愈奇探而愈
深出於德者敢謂無人然亦
===
未必皆出於才而習以然者
亦或有焉今旣錄於有司豈
可以是終身誦之而不知他
所以用其力乎自處身治家
以至應事接物之粲然自寢
興食息以至升降揖讓之秩
然自一事一爲之小以至建
punctuated: 專做時文人，只就紙上説」，是也。文之全體，則孔子所論與不與而歸之天者，是也。諸士子今日之文，其出於德乎？出於才乎？出於習乎？玉光珠彩，炫乎吾前，求而愈奇，探而愈深。出於德者，敢謂無人？然亦未必皆出於才，而習以然者，亦或有焉。今旣錄於有司，豈可以是終身誦之，而不知他所以用其力乎？自處身治家，以至應事接物之粲然；自寢興食息，以至升降揖讓之秩然；自一事一爲之小，以至建
translation_en:
…“Those who devote themselves exclusively to contemporary examination prose speak only on paper”—these are examples of it. As for wen—literary and cultural refinement—in its entirety, this is what Confucius discussed when he attributed its being bestowed or withheld to Heaven. Do the writings of you examination candidates today arise from virtue, from talent, or from practice? Their jade-like gleam and pearly lustre dazzle before my eyes; the more I seek, the more remarkable they become, and the more I probe, the greater their depth. Would I dare say that none arise from virtue? Yet neither do they necessarily all arise from talent; some may owe their character to practice.

Now that you have been selected by the responsible officials, how could you spend your whole lives reciting these writings without knowing where else to direct your efforts? From conducting yourselves and governing your households to the manifest refinement of handling affairs and dealing with others; from sleeping and rising, eating and resting, to the orderly observance of ascending and descending, bowing and yielding precedence; from the smallest individual undertaking or action to establishing…

title: 弘治十七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
大謨立大功而煥然顯於天
下皆文也夫是之謂全體于
此得其一肢焉則言之文將
益盛而況全體乎諸士子其
勉哉思皇濟濟之詠予欲復
聞於今以爲
聖治之助諸士子其勉哉不然則
===
言辭逞而神鑒昏於文奚取
焉
順天府涿州儒學學正張苣
謹序
punctuated:
大謨、立大功而煥然顯於天下，皆文也。夫是之謂全體，于此得其一肢焉，則言之文將益盛，而況全體乎？諸士子其勉哉！「思皇濟濟」之詠，予欲復聞於今，以爲聖治之助。諸士子其勉哉！不然，則言辭逞而神鑒昏，於文奚取焉？
順天府涿州儒學學正張苣謹序。
translation_en:
…great plans and establish great achievements, shining forth throughout the realm—all are manifestations of cultural refinement (wen). This is what is meant by its complete embodiment. If one acquires even a single limb of this whole, the refinement of one’s words will flourish still more; how much more so if one acquires the whole! You scholars, strive diligently! I wish to hear again today the praise of men as “admirable and numerous,” to aid the sagely governance of our ruler. You scholars, strive diligently! Otherwise, if verbal display runs unchecked while spiritual discernment grows dim, what value can such writing have?
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Ju, Instructor of the Confucian School of Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture.
